headings: Four ways an acute leukemic dies in the ED
docs.text: Acute myeloid leukemia ≥20% myeloid blasts — or any blast % with a defining genetic lesion · classification and treatment are now genetically driven · every new diagnosis is triaged for the three emergencies before a regimen is chosen Compiled from the Encyclopedia AML review note and Fellowship Anki deck · ELN 2022 · WHO 2022 / ICC · NCCN. Diagnosis ≥20% myeloid blasts — or any blast % with a defining fusion : t(8;21), inv(16)/t(16;16), PML::RARA. WHO 2022 also drops it for NPM1 but keeps ≥20% for CEBPA-bZIP ; ICC sets ≥10% for both Also AML at <20%: myeloid sarcoma / extramedullary disease “Blasts” on smear is morphologic — confirm lineage by flow Workup: marrow aspirate + biopsy with flow, karyotype + FISH, NGS ; CBC/smear (Auer rods); coags + fibrinogen + D-dimer ; TLS labs; baseline echo ; HLA typing early; LP only for CNS symptoms (consider if monocytic), after coags corrected Stat FISH/PCR for PML::RARA on any suspicion of APL Median age ~68. The three triage questions on every new AML: Is it APL? Is there leukostasis? Is there tumor lysis? ELN 2022 genetic risk Risk Representative genetics Favorable t(8;21) RUNX1::RUNX1T1 · inv(16)/t(16;16) CBFB::MYH11 ( core-binding factor ) · mutated NPM1 without FLT3-ITD · in-frame bZIP CEBPA Intermediate NPM1 + FLT3-ITD · wild-type NPM1 + FLT3-ITD · t(9;11) MLLT3::KMT2A · anything not otherwise classified Adverse Complex or monosomal karyotype · −5/del(5q), −7, abn(17p) · TP53 · MDS-related genes (ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, ZRSR2) · KMT2A rearrangements except t(9;11) and KMT2A-PTD · t(6;9), inv(3) ELN 2022 changes worth knowing: FLT3-ITD is intermediate regardless of allelic ratio (ratio dropped) · only in-frame bZIP CEBPA is favorable · NPM1 with adverse cytogenetics is reclassified adverse · KIT co-mutation worsens CBF-AML prognostically, but ELN 2022 kept it favorable . Genotype → phenotype FLT3-ITD Hyperleukocytosis; normal karyotype. ↑ CNS risk , most when NPM1 co-mutated KMT2A / 11q23 Monocytic — gum hypertrophy, leukemia cutis. Highest multivariable odds for CNS disease (OR ~7.6) t(8;21) Myeloid sarcoma ; aberrant CD19 / CD56 by flow inv(16) Abnormal marrow eosinophils with coarse basophilic granules (FAB M4Eo) TP53 Complex karyotype, t-AML; venetoclax-resistant , poor outcome even after allo DTA DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1 persist in CR as clonal hematopoiesis — not MRD markers CNS disease is uncommon — ~0.6% at diagnosis, ~3% at relapse . Risk factors differ by series: SAL (n=3,261) found FLT3-ITD ± NPM1 ; another found 11q23 (OR 7.6) and WBC ≥100k on multivariable analysis. Treatment pathway First: exclude APL, then assess fitness Before committing to a regimen APL must be excluded — ATRA cannot wait 7+3 may start while NGS pends, but FLT3 status changes induction — hold a day or two if stable; instability forces faster action Fit for intensive therapy Induction — 7+3 cytarabine ×7 days + anthracycline ×3 FLT3-mutated: add midostaurin (RATIFY) CD33 / CBF: add gemtuzumab (ALFA-0701) secondary or t-AML: consider CPX-351 PARADIGM (2026) adverse risk and not FLT3-mutated : aza+ven EFS 14.5 vs 6.2 mo , HR 0.57. Less infection and bleeding, and more patients reached allo phase 2, EFS endpoint — OS not significantly different Assess response day-14 marrow ; residual disease → re-induce goal is CR: blasts <5% with count recovery Consolidation by ELN risk favorable → HiDAC ×3–4 cycles, no allo intermediate / adverse → allo-HSCT in CR1 MRD-positive CR pushes toward transplant If not going to transplant oral azacitidine (CC-486) maintenance QUAZAR: OS 24.7 vs 14.8 months Unfit for intensive therapy Venetoclax + azacitidine VIALE-A : OS 14.7 vs 9.6 months vs aza alone watch TLS on ramp-up ; reduce dose with azoles IDH1-mutant alternative: ivosidenib + aza (AGILE) Relapsed / refractory Target first, then salvage FLT3 → gilteritinib (ADMIRAL) IDH1/2 → ivosidenib / enasidenib KMT2A-r or NPM1 → menin inhibitor salvage chemo: FLAG-IDA, MEC, CLAG-M Regimens & agents Regimen Notes 7+3 Cytarabine infusion ×7 days + an anthracycline ×3 — the backbone for fit patients. Daunorubicin 60 mg/m² is the modern standard: E1900 showed 90 > 45 , but AML17 found 90 vs 60 gave no CR or OS benefit and doubled 60-day mortality + midostaurin FLT3-mutated (RATIFY). Quizartinib for FLT3-ITD (QuANTUM-First) + gemtuzumab Fractionated dosing (ALFA-0701 — no CD33 cutoff). CBF benefit comes from the Hills meta-analysis , not ALFA-0701 CPX-351 Liposomal cytarabine + daunorubicin for t-AML / AML-MRC. Caveat: comparator was 7+3, not ven/aza — niche today is the fitter older adult bridging to allo HiDAC 3 g/m² q12h on days 1, 3, 5 ×3–4 cycles; best in CBF. Age >60 → IDAC 1.5 g/m² — 3 g/m² is inappropriate (ocular, cerebellar, infectious toxicity). Renal dose-reduce Venetoclax + azacitidine Unfit patients (VIALE-A). Ramp-up with TLS prophylaxis; reduce venetoclax with CYP3A inhibitors This table is when and why . Every regimen's dosing lives on page 3 — the two HiDAC numbers stay here because the dose is the teaching point. MRD and the transplant decision Measure MRD at the end of every cycle and again before transplant — order HemeSTAMP MRD (NGS) + multiparameter flow cytometry ; add NPM1 PCR where applicable MRD-positive CR is not CR for planning purposes — it predicts relapse and moves an otherwise favorable-risk patient toward transplant Allo-HSCT in CR1: generally not for favorable risk · yes for intermediate and adverse risk · modified by MRD, age, comorbidity, and donor availability Allo cures through graft-versus-leukemia . Auto-HSCT lacks GVL and relapses more — niche for MRD-negative CR1 without a donor Fitness for intensive therapy is a composite of age, performance status and comorbidity (HCT-CI) — not age alone The three emergencies APL Recognize DIC + bleeding + hypergranular promyelocytes bundled Auer rods microgranular variant can look monocytic Start ATRA immediately do not wait for PML::RARA — hemorrhage is the leading cause of APL death, and it is preventable 45 mg/m²/day PO divided q12h (22.5 mg/m² BID); a one-time dose overnight is fine Support aggressively fibrinogen >100 (cryo), platelets >30k , INR <2 coags q6–8 h; avoid LP and central lines Risk-stratify, then treat Sanz: low = WBC ≤10k and plt >40k · intermediate = WBC ≤10k and plt ≤40k · high = WBC >10k ATRA + arsenic , chemo-free, for low/intermediate high risk: add anthracycline (or GO) cure >90%; do NOT leukapherese — worsens DIC Leukostasis Hyperleukocytosis + symptoms myeloid blasts are large and sticky — symptoms at lower counts than ALL/CLL, often >50–100k CNS (headache, confusion, vision) + pulmonary (hypoxia) Management — with doses hydroxyurea up to 2 g PO q6h , goal WBC <20k literature 50–100 mg/kg/day; mucositis ≥75 mg/kg/day HU takes days — if too slow, cytarabine 1 g ×1 urgent induction is definitive ; leukapheresis if severe — never in APL , no mortality benefit. No RBC transfusion hydrate + TLS ppx. dex 10 mg IV q6h if monocytic + ARF Tumor lysis Cairo-Bishop lab TLS = ≥2 of ↑K, ↑phosphate, ↑uric acid, ↓Ca clinical TLS = lab TLS + AKI, arrhythmia or seizure Prevent and treat aggressive IV hydration is the cornerstone allopurinol 300 mg BID standard risk rasburicase if high risk or uric acid >8 — not in G6PD no urinary alkalinization Drug toxicity & monitoring Agent Watch for Cytarabine Pyrimidine analog. High-dose: cerebellar toxicity — cerebellar exam before every HiDAC dose, hold if abnormal ; conjunctivitis → prophylactic steroid eye drops ; ara-C syndrome (fever, myalgia, rash) Anthracyclines Cumulative, dose-dependent cardiotoxicity — track total dose, baseline ± serial LVEF. Vesicant — central access Venetoclax Tumor lysis on ramp-up ; neutropenia; dose-reduce with azole antifungals (CYP3A) Azacitidine vs decitabine Both hypomethylating; azacitidine incorporates into RNA and DNA , decitabine DNA-only. Azacitidine: injection-site reactions Gemtuzumab Anti-CD33 calicheamicin ADC — hepatotoxicity and VOD/SOS , especially peri-transplant; fractionated dosing lowers risk Arsenic trioxide QT prolongation — monitor ECG, replete K and Mg Differentiation syndrome ATRA/ATO and also IDH and menin inhibitors . Fever, dyspnea, hypoxia, infiltrates, effusions, weight gain, AKI → dexamethasone 10 mg IV BID at first suspicion Menin inhibitors Revumenib, ziftomenib — differentiation syndrome + QT prolongation Trial evidence RATIFY Midostaurin + 7+3 in FLT3-mutated — survival benefit QuANTUM-First Quizartinib + 7+3 in FLT3-ITD ALFA-0701 Fractionated gemtuzumab + 7+3 — EFS/RFS benefit held in the final analysis but OS was no longer significant . Hills meta-analysis (n=3,325) is what shows the favorable-cytogenetics benefit: 5-yr OS +20.7% E1900 Daunorubicin 90 vs 45 mg/m² — better CR and OS in age <60 AML17 Daunorubicin 90 vs 60 mg/m² — no CR or OS difference , and 60-day mortality 10% vs 5% (HR 1.98). Read with E1900: 60 is standard, not 90 (Burnett, Blood 2015) VIALE-A Azacitidine + venetoclax vs azacitidine — OS 14.7 vs 9.6 months (DiNardo, NEJM 2020) PARADIGM Aza+ven vs intensive induction in fit patients (CBF/FLT3/NPM1<60 excluded, 72% ELN adverse): EFS 14.5 vs 6.2 mo , HR 0.57; less infection and bleeding. Phase 2; OS not significant (Fathi, NEJM 2026) AGILE Ivosidenib + azacitidine in IDH1-mutant unfit patients ADMIRAL Gilteritinib in relapsed FLT3-mutated AML — survival benefit SORMAIN Sorafenib maintenance after allo in FLT3-ITD AML — 24-mo RFS 85% vs 53% , HR 0.39. Phase 2, n=83; off-label (Burchert, JCO 2020) MORPHO Gilteritinib maintenance after allo in FLT3-ITD, n=356. RFS missed overall (HR 0.68, P=0.052) — but benefit in the half who were MRD-positive pre- or post-HCT (HR 0.52, P=0.007) and none if MRD-negative . An MRD-guided decision (Levis, JCO 2024) APL0406 ATRA + arsenic beat ATRA + chemo in low/intermediate-risk APL (Lo-Coco, NEJM 2013) QUAZAR AML-001 Oral azacitidine (CC-486) maintenance in CR1 — OS 24.7 vs 14.8 months AML15 IDAC vs HiDAC consolidation — no overall survival difference SWOG S1203 IA regimen showed no benefit and more toxicity — 7+3 remains standard Genetics — fine points inv(3) / t(3;3) MECOM (EVI1, 3q26) activation; classically normal or high platelets ; adverse and venetoclax-resistant t(6;9) DEK::NUP214 — associates with FLT3-ITD and basophilia ; adverse NPM1 flow mimic NPM1-mutated AML can be HLA-DR− / CD34− and mimic APL — confirm PML::RARA Therapy-related After alkylators/RT : del(5q)/del(7q) ± TP53, latency ~5–7 yr. After topoisomerase-II : 11q23 KMT2A , latency ~2–3 yr Germline DDX41, RUNX1, CEBPA, GATA2 , telomere biology — send germline testing if young, family history, or multiple cytopenias; it changes related-donor selection Four ways an acute leukemic dies in the ED 1. Leukostasis — CVA, MI, respiratory failure 2. Bleeding / DIC / thrombosis 3. Infection — very low threshold for broad-spectrum antibiotics 4. Tumor lysis — renal failure, electrolyte derangement Overnight decisions 1. Triage floor vs ICU — leukapheresis and CRRT both require ICU 2. Rule out APL — start ATRA on any suspicion , do not wait for PML::RARA 3. Cytoreduction — see doses at right 4. TLS — start fluids + allopurinol, set lab frequency ( q4h to daily ). Rasburicase if uric acid >8: 0.15–0.2 mg/kg IV , in adults usually a single dose capped at 6 mg (label allows 0.2 mg/kg daily ×5 days). Check G6PD — contraindicated if deficient Supportive care Transfusion: platelets >10k (>20–50k if bleeding, procedure, or APL); irradiated and leukoreduced products Prophylaxis during induction: levofloxacin 500 mg PO daily · posaconazole DR 300 mg BID ×1 day, then 300 mg daily · acyclovir 400 mg PO BID (HSV-seropositive) Posaconazole is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor — that is what forces the venetoclax reduction: 400 mg → 70 mg daily with posaconazole (100 mg with other strong inhibitors such as voriconazole), during ramp-up and beyond Hepatitis B: screen HBsAg + anti-HBc before therapy. HBsAg-positive → entecavir or tenofovir (preferred over lamivudine) for any systemic anticancer therapy, continued ≥12 months past the last cycle. Isolated anti-HBc-positive → prophylax or monitor HBV DNA closely; AML chemotherapy carries reactivation risk similar to lymphoma Febrile neutropenia: fever ≥38.3°C once (or ≥38.0°C for 1 h) with ANC <500 → cefepime 2 g IV q8h within 1 hour . Add vancomycin for hemodynamic instability, line infection, skin/soft tissue infection, pneumonia or known MRSA. Severe mucositis is a softer trigger than it looks — IDSA lists it only when fluoroquinolone prophylaxis was used and ceftazidime is the empiric agent (viridans strep); cefepime already covers viridans strep . Antifungal if fever persists >4–7 days Fertility counseling before chemotherapy; central venous access; early palliative care in older or adverse-risk disease What to send Test When Peripheral studies Flow cytometry , AML prognosis assay (NPM1, FLT3-ITD, FLT3-TKD), IDH mutation analysis . Send if WBC >10k and marrow will be delayed, or the patient is old enough that you would rather not subject them to a marrow Cytogenetics FISH for PML::RARA and BCR::ABL1 . Send from peripheral blood if there is any concern for APL or a delay in getting marrow HLA typing Send if the patient is a possible allogeneic transplant candidate Cytoreduction overnight Dose and trigger Hydroxyurea Consider if WBC >20k . Overnight you can order a one-time dose . Typical range 500 mg–2 g , max 2 g q6h . Literature range 50–100 mg/kg/day; grade 3–4 mucositis rises at ≥75 mg/kg/day , so 2 g q6h is the ceiling, not the starting dose Leukapheresis Consider for evidence of leukostasis — headache, blurry vision, dyspnea/hypoxia, chest pain — typically with blasts >50k in AML (rare in ALL). Page apheresis 12027. Ask ER or the MICU triage fellow for a trialysis line ; admit to MICU. Ask the apheresis RN to save the product in the FGR fridge and coordinate with the research team. Never in APL Cytarabine 1 g ×1 may be considered for leukostasis when apheresis will be delayed APL overnight Start ATRA on any concern for APL — do not wait for PML::RARA Smear: bilobed / folded nuclei ± Auer rods. Page pathology on call (12005) if unsure ATRA 45 mg/m²/day PO divided q12h (= 22.5 mg/m² BID) — overnight you can give a one-time dose DIC labs q6–8h. Transfuse platelets >30 , fibrinogen >100 , INR <2 Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing 7+3 Cytarabine 100–200 mg/m²/day IV continuous infusion ×7 days from day 1 ( SHC uses 100 ) + daunorubicin 60 mg/m² IV daily days 1–3 schedule E1900; 60 vs 90 from AML17 7+3 + GO Add gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m² (max 4.5 mg) IV over 2 h on days 1, 4, 7 ALFA-0701 / Lambert 2019 7+3 + midostaurin Add midostaurin 50 mg PO q12h on days 8–21 RATIFY / Stone 2017 CPX-351 Liposomal daunorubicin 44 mg/m² + cytarabine 100 mg/m² IV on days 1, 3, 5 Lancet 2018 FLAG-IDA-VEN Fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cytarabine 1.5–2 g/m² IV days 2–6; idarubicin IV ( ND-AML 8 mg/m² days 4–6 ; R/R 6 mg/m² days 4–5 ); filgrastim 5 mcg/kg days 1–7; venetoclax ramp-up (100/200/400 mg) days 1–14 DiNardo 2021 CLAD / LDAC / VEN Cladribine 5 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cytarabine 20 mg/m² (SQ BID days 1–10; 20 mg/m² IV daily preferred at SHC ) + venetoclax PO days 1–21, alternating with azacitidine Kadia 2022 MEC Mitoxantrone 6–8 mg/m² + etoposide 80–100 mg/m² + cytarabine 1 g/m² , all daily days 1–5 (some series run 6 days) — dosing varies by protocol, check yours relapsed / refractory CLAG-M Cladribine 5 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cytarabine 2 g/m² IV days 1–5 + mitoxantrone 10 mg/m² IV days 1–3 + G-CSF 300 mcg days 0–5 relapsed / refractory HMA / VEN Venetoclax (ramp-up) daily ×28 days + decitabine 20 mg/m² days 1–5 or azacitidine 75 mg/m² days 1–7 VIALE-A / DiNardo 2020 APL induction — dosing Regimen Dosing ATO / ATRA Arsenic trioxide 0.15 mg/kg IV over 2 h daily from day 1 + ATRA 22.5 mg/m² PO BID from day 1 — both until hematologic CR or max 60 days APL0406 / Lo-Coco 2013 ATO / ATRA / IDA ATO 0.15 mg/kg IV days 9–36 + ATRA 22.5 mg/m² BID days 1–36 + idarubicin on days 2, 4, 6, 8 by age: ≤60 yr 12 mg/m² · 61–70 yr 9 mg/m² · >70 yr 6 mg/m² APML4 / Iland 2012 ATO / ATRA / GO ATO 0.3 mg/kg IV daily days 1–5, then 0.25 mg/kg twice weekly weeks 2–8 + ATRA 22.5 mg/m² BID from day 1 until CR or max 60 days + gemtuzumab 6 mg/m² IV once on day 1 — high risk only (WBC >10k) AML17 APL / Burnett 2015
