docs.text: Biliary tract cancer Gallbladder · intrahepatic, perihilar and distal cholangiocarcinoma · one systemic backbone, four different operations, and a molecular profile that depends entirely on where the tumor sits Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Gallbladder Cancer and Cholangiocarcinoma (Northness A, Heestand G) · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. Four diseases in one name Site Notes Intrahepatic CCA ~10% of CCA Arises proximal to the second-order ducts. The molecularly rich one — FGFR2 and IDH1 live here Perihilar (Klatskin) ~40% of CCA At the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts. Resection planned by Bismuth-Corlette class Distal CCA ~50% of CCA Common bile duct up to, but not including, the ampulla Gallbladder cancer <5,000 cases/yr US; fundus 60% > body 30% > neck 10%. 1–2% are found incidentally at cholecystectomy for stones ~8,000 cholangiocarcinomas/yr in the US, median age ~70. The subtypes share systemic therapy but differ in staging system, operation, and molecular profile — which is why anatomic site has to be stated before anything else. Risk: CCA — PSC, HBV/HCV, liver flukes, male sex, obesity, diabetes, alcohol. GBC — cholelithiasis, gallbladder calcification, female sex, chronic Salmonella or H. pylori infection. Workup Labs: CBC with differential, CMP, PT/INR, CA 19-9 , HBV and HCV serologies Imaging: triphasic CT abdomen/pelvis or liver-protocol MRI + CT chest to complete staging. PET/CT to exclude occult disease when the plan is resection Gallbladder: start with ultrasound — go to triphasic CT or MRI for a polyp >10 mm or wall thickening not explained by cholecystitis MRCP to plan biopsy and stenting. ERCP to stent, decompress and brush — brushings are often non-diagnostic, so go to EUS-FNA when they are Genomically profile every tumor , and send MMR, HER2 IHC and PD-L1 . This is not optional in biliary cancer — roughly a third of patients have a level 1/2 actionable alteration If perihilar CCA might go to transplant, do NOT perform a transperitoneal biopsy — tumor seeding disqualifies the patient from the protocol Treatment pathway Resectable Resection by anatomic site gallbladder T1a: cholecystectomy alone everything else: formal resection + lymphadenectomy Adjuvant therapy capecitabine ×8 cycles (BILCAP) is the default node-positive or margin-positive derive the clearest benefit — consider adding chemoradiation (SWOG S0809) Surveillance exam, CA 19-9 and triphasic CT C/A/P q3 months ×2 years , then q6 months Locally advanced, unresectable Systemic therapy first treat as metastatic — gem/cis + durvalumab or pembrolizumab Then consider local therapy no randomized evidence of survival benefit ablative RT gives excellent local control; ABC-07 was negative HAI floxuridine and Y-90 rest on single-arm phase 2 data Metastatic Start chemo-IO and profile in parallel gem/cis + durvalumab (TOPAZ-1) or + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-966) — near-identical benefit, no biomarker send NGS, MMR and HER2 IHC on day one Second line targeted therapy if an alteration was found — see page 2 otherwise FOLFOX (ABC-06) Staging — three separate AJCC systems Site T staging hinges on Intrahepatic Size and vascular invasion: T1a ≤5 cm / T1b >5 cm, both without vascular invasion · T2 vascular invasion or multiple tumors · T3 perforates visceral peritoneum · T4 direct extrahepatic invasion. N is simply N0 / N1 Perihilar Depth then vessels: T1 confined to the duct · T2a into surrounding fat, T2b into hepatic parenchyma · T3 unilateral portal vein or hepatic artery branch · T4 main portal vein bilaterally, common hepatic artery, or second-order radicals with contralateral vessel Distal Millimetres of duct-wall invasion: T1 <5 mm · T2 5–12 mm · T3 >12 mm · T4 celiac axis, SMA or common hepatic artery Gallbladder Which side of the wall: T1a lamina propria, T1b muscularis · T2a peritoneal side, T2b hepatic side — the distinction drives the operation · T3 serosa, liver or one adjacent organ · T4 main portal vein / hepatic artery or ≥2 organs Nodes: perihilar, distal and gallbladder all use N1 = 1–3 nodes, N2 = ≥4 . Intrahepatic uses N0/N1 only. Surgery — the only curative option Most patients are unresectable at presentation, and most resected patients still recur Resectability requires: no retropancreatic or paraceliac nodes, no distant liver metastases, no main portal vein or hepatic artery invasion, no adjacent-organ invasion, no dissemination Intrahepatic → hepatic lobectomy; 5-yr OS 11–40%. Perihilar → en bloc resection by Bismuth-Corlette class. Distal → Whipple + extrahepatic duct; 5-yr OS 10–40% Gallbladder: T1a is cured by simple cholecystectomy alone. T1b and above need en bloc cholecystectomy + resection of liver segments 4a/4b + regional lymphadenectomy Incidentally discovered gallbladder cancer beyond T1a must go back to the operating room for the 4a/4b bed resection and lymphadenectomy Liver transplant is an option for highly selected perihilar CCA (Mayo protocol: mass ≤3 cm, no transperitoneal biopsy, no metastases) — intention-to-treat 5-yr survival ~53% Alteration by site — why site matters iCCA eCCA GBC FGFR2 fusion / rearrangement ~12% ~1% ~1–2% IDH1 ~20% ~1% ~1% IDH2 ~6% 0% ~0.5% HER2 / ERBB2 ~4% ~9% ~11–14% BRAF V600E ~3% ~0% ~0% KRAS, any ~12% ~38% ~10% MSI-H / dMMR ~1.5% ~4% ~2% BAP1 ~19% ~2% ~1% TP53 ~21% ~44% ~60% FGFR2 and IDH1 are intrahepatic diseases and are mutually exclusive. HER2 is a gallbladder and extrahepatic disease. Roughly a third of all biliary cancers carry a level 1/2 actionable alteration — but that is ~40% of intrahepatic versus ~15% of extrahepatic . Western cohorts (AACR GENIE); in East Asian series IDH1 and FGFR2 fall and KRAS rises. Living with an FGFR inhibitor Hyperphosphatemia is on-target , not idiosyncratic — FGFR1 blockade removes the FGF23 phosphaturic signal. It is a marker that the drug is working. Pemigatinib ~60%, futibatinib ~85%, lirafugratinib ~21% . Manage with a low-phosphate diet, sevelamer , and dose holds Ocular toxicity: serous retinopathy / retinal pigment epithelial detachment, plus dry eye in over 20%. Baseline and serial ophthalmology with OCT — roughly q2 months for 6 months, then q3 months Nail and hair: onycholysis in ~47%, alopecia in a third. Stomatitis, arthralgia and diarrhea are common Resistance arrives at ~6–9 months as polyclonal secondary FGFR2 kinase-domain mutations , classically the gatekeeper V564F . The covalent agents (futibatinib, lirafugratinib) retain activity against some but not all of these Driver → therapy Alteration Therapy FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement ~12% of iCCA All second-line and beyond. Lirafugratinib (FGFR2-selective; approved 23 Sep 2026 ) — ORR 46%, DOR 11.8 mo, and notably less hyperphosphatemia (~21%) . Futibatinib ORR 42% (accelerated; label is intrahepatic only ). Pemigatinib ORR 37% (accelerated, any site). Only fusions and rearrangements qualify — point mutations do not. FIGHT-302 moved pemigatinib to 1L on PFS but showed no OS gain , and the 1L indication is not approved. Infigratinib was withdrawn in 2024 IDH1 ~20% of iCCA Ivosidenib after 1–2 prior lines (regular approval). PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.37 — statistically emphatic, clinically modest. Unadjusted OS was not significant (10.3 vs 7.5 mo) because 70% crossed over ; crossover-adjusted HR 0.49 HER2 GBC ~11–14%, eCCA ~9% Zanidatamab — the only BTC-specific approval (accelerated, Nov 2024), IHC 3+ only , 2L+: ORR 52% in IHC 3+, DOR 14.9 mo. T-DXd is covered by the tumor-agnostic IHC 3+ approval, but ILD reached 17% in the biliary cohort — higher than in most tumor types. Trastuzumab + pertuzumab is NCCN-listed but not FDA-approved here BRAF V600E ~3% of iCCA Dabrafenib + trametinib — tumor-agnostic accelerated approval. ROAR biliary cohort ORR 47–53%, PFS 9.0 mo MSI-H / dMMR ~1–3% Pembrolizumab (tumor-agnostic, now regular approval) — KEYNOTE-158 cholangiocarcinoma cohort ORR 41% , median OS 24.3 months. Dostarlimab is an alternative TMB ≥10 mut/Mb ~4% Pembrolizumab, tumor-agnostic accelerated approval NTRK or RET fusion <1% each Larotrectinib / entrectinib / repotrectinib for NTRK; selpercatinib for RET (tumor-agnostic, converted to traditional approval in 2026). Pralsetinib has no tumor-agnostic approval KRAS G12C ~1% No approved option in biliary cancer. Adagrasib showed activity in a small pan-tumor cohort (5/12); trial or off-label only Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing Gem/cis + durvalumab TOPAZ-1, 1L Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 , with durvalumab 1500 mg day 1 — q21d . Chemotherapy for up to 8 cycles, durvalumab continues Gem/cis + pembrolizumab KEYNOTE-966, 1L Same gem/cis backbone with pembrolizumab 200 mg day 1, q21d FOLFOX ABC-06, 2L Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1 + 5-FU 1200 mg/m²/day ×48 h continuous infusion from day 1 — q14d Gem + nab-paclitaxel Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² then gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² , days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle . Single-arm phase 2 that missed its primary endpoint — an alternative, not a standard Adjuvant capecitabine BILCAP 1250 mg/m² PO twice daily, days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle, ×8 cycles (6 months). Grade 3 hand-foot in ~20% Adjuvant chemoRT SWOG S0809 Gemcitabine + capecitabine ×4 cycles, then capecitabine with radiation ×6 weeks (45 Gy nodal, 54–59.4 Gy tumor bed) Ivosidenib 500 mg PO daily — IDH1-mutant, after 1–2 prior lines Lirafugratinib 70 mg PO daily — FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement, previously treated, FGFR-inhibitor-naive Reading the adjuvant evidence honestly BILCAP is the standard of care but was a formally negative trial. ITT median OS 51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81, p=0.097 — the primary endpoint was not met . It became practice on the per-protocol analysis (HR 0.75) and a prespecified sensitivity analysis (HR 0.71). Worth knowing when someone asks why capecitabine SWOG S0809 is single-arm — 2-year OS 65% in resected extrahepatic CCA or gallbladder cancer with pT2-4, node-positive or margin-positive disease. Benchmark data, not a randomized comparison Negative adjuvant trials: PRODIGE-12 (GEMOX) and BCAT (gemcitabine) both failed. ASCOT showed adjuvant S-1 improves 3-year OS (77.1% vs 67.6%) in an all-Japanese population — but S-1 is not available in the US ACTICCA-1 (gem/cis vs capecitabine) has closed accrual and has not yet read out — it is the trial that may finally settle this Liver-directed therapy — what is actually supported Nothing randomized. Every option below rests on single-arm phase 2 or retrospective data HAI floxuridine via implanted pump (partial response 58%, median OS 25 months in a single-institution phase 2) — requires an experienced hepatobiliary program Y-90 / TARE concurrent with first-line chemotherapy: ORR 39%, median OS 22 months, 22% downstaged to surgery — but grade 3–4 toxicity was 71%, and the one randomized trial, SIRCCA, was terminated Ablative radiation gives excellent local control, but ABC-07 randomized SBRT after chemotherapy and missed its PFS endpoint (8.6 vs 9.0 months). The frequently quoted dose-escalation survival figures come from a retrospective series with heavy selection bias Key trials ABC-02 Gemcitabine + cisplatin vs gemcitabine — OS 11.7 vs 8.1 mo , HR 0.64. The backbone, since 2010 TOPAZ-1 Add durvalumab to gem/cis — OS 12.8 vs 11.5 mo, HR 0.80; 24-mo OS 24.9% vs 10.4% KEYNOTE-966 Add pembrolizumab to gem/cis — OS 12.7 vs 10.9 mo, HR 0.83. Effectively interchangeable with TOPAZ-1 ABC-06 FOLFOX after gem/cis — OS 6.2 vs 5.3 mo. Median gain is under a month; the honest number is 12-mo OS 25.9% vs 11.4% SWOG S1815 Adding nab-paclitaxel to gem/cis — negative . OS 14.0 vs 13.6 mo. Responses rose, survival did not BILCAP Adjuvant capecitabine — ITT p=0.097, primary endpoint not met ; standard of care on secondary analyses ASCOT Adjuvant S-1 , Japan — 3-yr OS 77.1% vs 67.6%. Not applicable in the US FIGHT-202 / FOENIX-CCA2 Pemigatinib (ORR 37%) and futibatinib (ORR 42%) in FGFR2-altered disease ReFocus Lirafugratinib — ORR 46%, DOR 11.8 mo, far less hyperphosphatemia. Approved 23 Sep 2026 ClarIDHy Ivosidenib in IDH1-mutant — PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, HR 0.37 HERIZON-BTC-01 Zanidatamab in HER2 IHC 3+ — ORR 52%, DOR 14.9 mo ROAR Dabrafenib + trametinib in BRAF V600E — ORR 47–53%

docs.title: Breast cancer
docs.subtitle: Every decision runs off receptor subtype (HR+/HER2−, HER2+, TNBC — and now HER2-low / ultralow) crossed with stage and setting · AJCC 8th anatomic + prognostic staging
docs.text: Breast cancer Every decision runs off receptor subtype (HR+/HER2−, HER2+, TNBC — and now HER2-low / ultralow ) crossed with stage and setting · AJCC 8th anatomic + prognostic staging Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Breast Cancer (Schultz C, Khan S, Sidhu K, Yang M, Dalal N, Tsai J) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. Workup Bilateral diagnostic mammogram + ultrasound ; MRI or contrast-enhanced mammogram if dense tissue, young, or extent unclear Core biopsy of breast (and suspicious node) with clip placement — clip the node before neoadjuvant therapy ER/PR, HER2 (IHC, reflex ISH if 2+), grade, Ki-67 on every invasive cancer Stage I–IIB: no routine staging imaging — CBC/CMP; bone scan, CT only for symptoms, raised alk phos or abnormal LFTs Clinical stage III: CT C/A/P + bone scan, or PET/CT Stage IV / recurrence: biopsy the first metastasis (receptors drift, HER2-low status can change); brain MRI for CNS symptoms · NGS on tissue or ctDNA for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN/ESR1 · germline testing if not done Fertility counseling before chemotherapy in premenopausal patients Staging — AJCC 8th T1 / T2 / T3 ≤20 mm (T1mi ≤1, T1a ≤5, T1b ≤10) / >20–50 mm / >50 mm T4 a chest wall · b skin edema/ulcer/satellite nodules · c both · d inflammatory pN1 / pN2 / pN3 1–3 / 4–9 / ≥10 axillary nodes (or infraclavicular, supraclavicular). pN1mi >0.2–2 mm; pN0(i+) ≤0.2 mm cN2 / cN3 fixed/matted axillary or IMN alone / infraclavicular, IMN + axillary, or supraclavicular Prognostic stage Grade, ER, PR, HER2 modify the anatomic stage — triple-negative is upstaged, HR+/HER2+ often downstaged. T1–2 N0 HR+/HER2− with Oncotype RS <11 → stage IA . Pathologic prognostic stage does not apply after neoadjuvant therapy After neoadjuvant yc / yp prefix; pCR = ypT0/is ypN0 — drives adjuvant escalation DCIS: lumpectomy + RT, mastectomy, or lumpectomy alone if small and age >70 ; margin ≥2 mm; ER+ → tamoxifen ×5 yr (NSABP B-24) or low-dose 5 mg ×3 yr. LCIS: florid/pleomorphic → excise to negative margins; classic does not need them. Treatment pathway by subtype HR+ / HER2− early Surgery first (neoadjuvant only if downstaging) Oncotype on the specimen: N0 or 1–3 nodes chemo by RS + menopausal status (TAILORx, RxPONDER) Endocrine therapy for all, 5–10 yr postmenopausal: AI · premenopausal: tamoxifen high risk premenopausal: OFS + AI or tamoxifen Escalate for high risk ≥4 nodes or 1–3 + high risk: abemaciclib ×2 yr stage II–III incl. N0: ribociclib ×3 yr gBRCA high risk: olaparib ×1 yr HER2+ early ≤cT1 N0: surgery first paclitaxel ×12 wk + trastuzumab ×1 yr (APT) ≥cT2 or N+: neoadjuvant TCHP ×6 or T-DXd ×4 → THP (DB-11) Adjuvant by response pCR → complete 1 yr HP (pertuzumab if N+) residual → T-DXd ×14 (DB-05) or T-DM1 HR+: neratinib ×1 yr option (ExteNET) TNBC early ≥cT2 or N+: KEYNOTE-522 carbo/paclitaxel + pembro → AC + pembro surgery → pembro to 1 yr, regardless of pCR Residual disease capecitabine (CREATE-X) · gBRCA: olaparib Metastatic HR+ / HER2− 1L: AI or fulvestrant + CDK4/6i (ribociclib) 2L: by NGS — ESR1, PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN then T-DXd (low/ultralow), SG, Dato-DXd HER2+ 1L: T-DXd + pertuzumab (DB-09) or THP 2L T-DXd · CNS: tucatinib-cape-trastuzumab TNBC CPS ≥10: pembro + chemo or SG + pembro CPS <10: SG or Dato-DXd · gBRCA: PARPi later: SG · T-DXd if HER2-low Receptor definitions — ASCO/CAP Result Meaning ER / PR ≥1% HR-positive. ER-low (1–10%) behaves like TNBC — consider TNBC-type chemo/IO HER2 IHC 0 — null No membrane staining. No HER2-directed therapy HER2-ultralow IHC 0 with staining Faint, incomplete membrane staining in ≤10% of cells . T-DXd-eligible in HR+ mBC after ET (DESTINY-Breast06) HER2-low IHC 1+ (faint, incomplete in >10%) or IHC 2+ / ISH− . Not HER2-positive — no trastuzumab benefit — but T-DXd works (DESTINY-Breast04/06) HER2-positive IHC 3+ (complete, intense, >10%) or IHC 2+ with ISH amplification Pathology reports must now distinguish 0-null from ultralow — ask for a re-read of an archival “IHC 0” before ruling out T-DXd. Scoring 0 vs 1+ is poorly reproducible; retest a metastatic biopsy. Germline testing ASCO/SSO 2024: offer BRCA1/2 testing to every patient diagnosed at ≤65 (stage I–III or de novo IV). Over 65: if TNBC, male, PARP-inhibitor candidate, or suggestive personal/family history. NCCN uses ≤50 plus family/personal criteria Testing is treatment-changing: adjuvant olaparib (OlympiA), PARP inhibitor in mBC, and surgery choice (bilateral mastectomy, RRSO) High penetrance: BRCA1 (TNBC-enriched) · BRCA2 (HR+, male BC) · PALB2 (manage like BRCA) · TP53 (avoid RT if possible) · PTEN · CDH1 (lobular + diffuse gastric) Moderate penetrance: CHEK2, ATM — annual MRI screening; risk-reducing mastectomy is not indicated on the gene alone ; RT is safe Offer a multigene panel — not BRCA alone — when history suggests other genes Local therapy — de-escalation Question Evidence 1–2 positive SLN, BCS + RT Skip ALND (Z0011: 10-yr OS 86.3 vs 83.6%). AMAROS: axillary RT = ALND for control (10-yr axillary recurrence 0.93 vs 1.82%), half the lymphedema cN0, negative axillary US SLNB can be omitted : SOUND (≤2 cm, 5-yr DDFS 98.0 vs 97.7%) · INSEMA (≤5 cm, BCS; 5-yr iDFS 91.9 vs 91.7%) — axillary recurrence slightly higher RT after BCS, age ≥65, low risk PRIME II (HR+, N0, ≤3 cm, on ET): omitting RT raised 10-yr local recurrence 9.5% vs 0.9% , OS identical (80.8 vs 80.7%). EUROPA (≥70, luminal A): RT alone had better QoL than ET alone at interim — recurrence data pending ALND still indicated ≥3 positive nodes, matted nodes, inflammatory/T4, node-positive after neoadjuvant Early HR+ / HER2− Question Evidence Chemo? N0 TAILORx: RS 11–25 → ET alone non-inferior (9-yr iDFS 83.3 vs 84.3%). Age ≤50 with RS 16–25: chemo helps . RS ≥26 → chemo Chemo? 1–3 nodes RxPONDER (RS ≤25): postmenopausal — no benefit ; premenopausal — 5-yr iDFS 93.9 vs 89.0% (likely an OFS effect) OFS SOFT/TEXT: OFS + exemestane best DFS. Final 15-yr: OS gain confined to high risk — age <35: 82.5 vs 77.9 vs 68.1% (E+OFS / T+OFS / T) Abemaciclib ×2 yr monarchE ≥4 nodes, or 1–3 + grade 3, ≥5 cm or Ki-67 ≥20%. 7-yr iDFS 77.4 vs 70.9%; OS now significant (HR 0.84; 86.8 vs 85.0%) Ribociclib ×3 yr NATALEE Stage IIB–III, or IIA N0 with grade 3 (or grade 2 + high genomic risk/Ki-67 ≥20%). 5-yr iDFS HR 0.72 (+4.5 points); OS not yet significant Olaparib ×1 yr OlympiA gBRCA, high-risk HER2−. 6-yr OS 87.5 vs 83.2% (HR 0.72) Early HER2+ Setting Evidence Small, N0 APT (single-arm, ≤3 cm): TH → 10-yr iDFS 91.3%. ATEMPT: T-DM1 ×1 yr — 3-yr iDFS 97.8% but no less toxicity (46 vs 47%) Neoadjuvant NeoSphere: pertuzumab raised pCR 29 → 46%. DESTINY-Breast11: T-DXd ×4 → THP vs ddAC → THP, pCR 67.3 vs 56.3% , grade ≥3 AE 38 vs 56%; T-DXd alone was inferior and closed Residual disease KATHERINE: T-DM1 ×14, iDFS HR 0.50, 7-yr OS 89.1 vs 84.4%. DESTINY-Breast05 (high risk): T-DXd vs T-DM1 , 3-yr iDFS 92.4 vs 83.7% (HR 0.47); ILD 9.6% Pertuzumab adjuvant APHINITY: iDFS HR 0.81; benefit is node-positive only (8-yr 86.1 vs 81.2%); OS not significant Extended ExteNET: neratinib ×1 yr, 5-yr iDFS 90.2 vs 87.7%; gain in HR+; no OS benefit ; 40% grade 3 diarrhea without prophylaxis Early TNBC Trial Evidence KEYNOTE-522 Stage II–III: pCR 64.8 vs 51.2% ; 5-yr OS 86.6 vs 81.7% . Give pembrolizumab regardless of PD-L1 or pCR CREATE-X Residual HER2− disease: capecitabine; TNBC OS HR 0.52 OlympiA gBRCA with residual TNBC or ≥pT2/pN1: olaparib ×1 yr Metastatic HR+ — 1L CDK4/6 inhibitors Trial PFS (mo) OS (mo) MONALEESA-2 ribo + letrozole 25.3 vs 16.0 63.9 vs 51.4 , HR 0.76 — sig MONALEESA-3 ribo + fulvestrant 20.5 vs 12.8 53.7 vs 41.5 , HR 0.73 — sig MONALEESA-7 ribo, premenopausal 23.8 vs 13.0 42-mo OS 70.2 vs 46.0%, HR 0.71 — sig MONARCH 2 abema + fulvestrant 16.4 vs 9.3 46.7 vs 37.3 , HR 0.76 — sig MONARCH 3 abema + NSAI 28.2 vs 14.8 66.8 vs 53.7, HR 0.80 — NS PALOMA-2 palbo + letrozole 24.8 vs 14.5 53.9 vs 51.2, HR 0.96 — NS PALOMA-3 palbo + fulvestrant 9.5 vs 4.6 34.9 vs 28.0, HR 0.81 — NS Ribociclib is the only CDK4/6i with significant OS in every phase 3 trial — the preferred 1L agent. Palbociclib improved PFS but not OS. HR+/HER2+ mBC: PATINA added palbociclib to maintenance HP + ET after induction — PFS 44.3 vs 29.1 mo (HR 0.75), OS pending. Metastatic HER2+ Line Evidence 1L DESTINY-Breast09: T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP, PFS 40.7 vs 26.9 (HR 0.56), approved Dec 2025; OS immature, ILD 12%. CLEOPATRA (THP): OS 57.1 vs 40.8 — still reasonable 2L DESTINY-Breast03: T-DXd vs T-DM1, PFS 28.8 vs 6.8 , OS HR 0.64 Brain mets HER2CLIMB: tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine, OS 21.9 vs 17.4, CNS-PFS 9.9 vs 4.2 , active mets allowed · T-DXd active (DB-12, single-arm: 12-mo PFS 61.6%) Metastatic TNBC Setting Evidence 1L CPS ≥10 22C3 Pembro + chemo (KEYNOTE-355): OS 23.0 vs 16.1 , HR 0.73; no OS gain at CPS 1–9 · SG + pembro (ASCENT-04): PFS 11.2 vs 7.8, OS immature (approved Jun 2026) 1L, not IO candidate Dato-DXd (TROPION-Breast02): PFS 10.8 vs 5.6, OS 23.7 vs 18.7 (May 2026) · SG (ASCENT-03): PFS 9.7 vs 6.9, OS immature gBRCA Olaparib (OlympiAD, PFS 7.0 vs 4.2) or talazoparib (EMBRACA, 8.6 vs 5.6) — neither improved OS 2L+ Sacituzumab (ASCENT): OS 12.1 vs 6.7 · T-DXd if HER2-low (DB-04) Metastatic HR+ — after CDK4/6 (biomarker-driven) Target Agent → evidence ESR1 mut acquired on AI; test ctDNA Elacestrant (EMERALD): ESR1m PFS 3.8 vs 1.9 (HR 0.55) · imlunestrant (EMBER-3): ESR1m 5.5 vs 3.8 (HR 0.62); + abemaciclib 9.4 vs 5.5 vs imlunestrant alone (combo approved Sep 2026: ESR1m, after ≥1 line ET) · vepdegestrant (VERITAC-2, ESR1m, May 2026) ESR1 on 1L ctDNA SERENA-6: switch AI → camizestrant , keep CDK4/6i, when ESR1m emerges before progression: PFS 16.0 vs 9.2 (HR 0.44). ODAC voted 6–3 the benefit was not clinically meaningful; accelerated approval anyway, Sep 2026 ; OS immature PIK3CA mut Inavolisib + palbo + fulvestrant (INAVO120; relapse on/≤12 mo of adjuvant ET): PFS 15.0 vs 7.3, OS 34.0 vs 27.0 (HR 0.67) · alpelisib + fulv (SOLAR-1): 11.0 vs 5.7, OS NS, grade 3–4 hyperglycemia 37%; almost no prior CDK4/6i PIK3CA / AKT1 / PTEN Capivasertib + fulv (CAPItello-291): altered PFS 7.3 vs 3.1 (HR 0.50); final OS not significant (2026) PIK3CA wild-type Gedatolisib + fulv ± palbo (VIKTORIA-1) approved Jul 2026 No target Switch CDK4/6i + ET (MAINTAIN, postMONARCH: PFS 6.0 vs 5.3) · everolimus + exemestane (BOLERO-2, OS NS) Endocrine-refractory T-DXd if HER2-low/ultralow: DB-06 (chemo-naive) PFS 13.2 vs 8.1; DB-04 (after chemo) OS 23.9 vs 17.5 · Sacituzumab (TROPiCS-02): OS 14.4 vs 11.2 · Dato-DXd (TROPION-Breast01): PFS HR 0.63 but OS HR 1.01 · gBRCA: PARPi HER2-low / ultralow — T-DXd Trial Result and caveat DESTINY-Breast04 after 1–2 chemo lines HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH−), HR+ or HR−. HR+ cohort PFS 10.1 vs 5.4 , OS 23.9 vs 17.5 (HR 0.64); all patients OS 23.4 vs 16.8. DESTINY-Breast06 after ≥1 ET, chemo-naive HR+ only. HER2-low PFS 13.2 vs 8.1 (HR 0.62). Ultralow subgroup (n=153, exploratory): 15.1 vs 8.3, HR 0.76 — CI crosses 1 . OS immature. Label covers low + ultralow (Jan 2025) ILD ~11–12% in both, with deaths Metastatic HR+ — sequencing rules Endocrine-sensitive (de novo, or relapse >12 mo after adjuvant ET) → AI + CDK4/6i . Endocrine-resistant (on or ≤12 mo after adjuvant ET) → fulvestrant + CDK4/6i , or the inavolisib triplet if PIK3CA-mutant Visceral crisis → chemotherapy first; otherwise endocrine-based therapy precedes chemo. Premenopausal/men: add GnRH agonist Re-test ctDNA at each progression — ESR1 is acquired under AI pressure, usually absent at diagnosis Early-stage dosing Regimen Dosing ddAC → T Doxorubicin 60 + cyclophosphamide 600 q14d ×4 (G-CSF) → paclitaxel 175 q14d ×4 or 80 weekly ×12 TC Docetaxel 75 + cyclophosphamide 600 q21d ×4 KEYNOTE-522 Carboplatin AUC 5 d1 + paclitaxel 80 d1, 8, 15 + pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×4 → AC (60/600) + pembro q21d ×4 → surgery → pembro ×9 (1 yr total) TCHP / TCH Docetaxel 75 + carboplatin AUC 6 + trastuzumab 8 → 6 mg/kg ± pertuzumab 840 → 420 mg q21d ×6; HER2 therapy to 1 yr TH APT Paclitaxel 80 + trastuzumab 4 → 2 mg/kg weekly ×12, then trastuzumab 6 mg/kg q3wk to 1 yr AC → TH(P) AC q14d ×4 → paclitaxel 80 weekly ×12 + trastuzumab ± pertuzumab. Never HER2 agents concurrent with anthracycline T-DM1 / T-DXd residual HER2+ T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg q21d ×14 · T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q21d ×14 (DB-05) Capecitabine 1000–1250 mg/m² BID d1–14 q21d ×6–8 Abemaciclib adjuvant 150 mg BID ×2 yr + ET Ribociclib adjuvant 400 mg daily d1–21 q28d ×3 yr + NSAI Olaparib 300 mg BID ×1 yr (tablets) Endocrine Tamoxifen 20 mg · anastrozole 1 · letrozole 2.5 · exemestane 25 mg daily · goserelin 3.6 mg SQ q4wk / leuprolide 3.75 mg q4wk Doses mg/m² unless stated. Neratinib: loperamide prophylaxis or dose escalation from the start. Metastatic dosing Regimen Dosing CDK4/6 inhibitors Ribociclib 600 mg d1–21 q28d · palbociclib 125 mg d1–21 q28d · abemaciclib 150 mg BID continuous (200 BID alone) — with AI or fulvestrant Fulvestrant 500 mg IM d1, 15, 29, then q28d. Premenopausal: add OFS to AI or fulvestrant Oral SERDs Elacestrant 345 mg daily · imlunestrant 400 mg daily · camizestrant 75 mg daily + CDK4/6i Capivasertib 400 mg BID, 4 days on / 3 off + fulvestrant PI3Kα Inavolisib 9 mg daily + palbociclib + fulvestrant · alpelisib 300 mg daily + fulvestrant Everolimus + exemestane 10 mg + 25 mg daily; dexamethasone mouthwash for stomatitis THP Docetaxel 75 (or weekly paclitaxel 80) + trastuzumab 8 → 6 mg/kg + pertuzumab 840 → 420 mg q21d; stop taxane after ~6 cycles, continue HP T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q21d (HER2+, low, ultralow) ± pertuzumab 1L. Highly emetogenic — 3-drug prophylaxis Tucatinib-cape-H Tucatinib 300 mg BID + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² BID d1–14 + trastuzumab 8 → 6 mg/kg q21d Sacituzumab 10 mg/kg d1, d8 q21d (± pembro 200 q3wk) Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg q21d PARP inhibitors Olaparib 300 mg BID · talazoparib 1 mg daily Bone-directed Zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q4wk (q12wk after 1 yr) or denosumab 120 mg SQ q4wk ; dental review, Ca/vit D Surgical, radiation and special situations Inflammatory (T4d): trimodality always — neoadjuvant systemic therapy → modified radical mastectomy + ALND → chest wall + nodal RT, even after pCR ; no BCS, delayed reconstruction BCS relative contraindications: Li-Fraumeni, active scleroderma/lupus, prior chest RT, large tumor-to-breast ratio. Mastectomy for gene carriers, prior mantle RT, or preference Pregnancy: surgery any trimester; anthracycline chemo from the 2nd trimester; no endocrine, HER2, IO or RT until after delivery Male breast cancer: mostly HR+, BRCA2-enriched; tamoxifen preferred ; an AI needs a GnRH agonist Lymphedema ~5% after SLNB, highest after ALND + nodal RT · BIA-ALCL (textured implants): cytology, then remove capsule + implant Toxicity and monitoring T-DXd ILD (10–15% across trials, fatal cases): baseline + serial chest CT on therapy, ask about cough/dyspnea at every visit. Grade 1: hold until resolved (same dose if ≤28 days), consider steroids. Grade ≥2: stop permanently + prompt systemic steroids HER2 agents — cardiac: LVEF at baseline and q3 months . Hold trastuzumab for ≥16% absolute drop , or below normal with ≥10% drop; recheck in 4 wk Ribociclib: QTc — ECG baseline (start only if QTcF <450) and ~day 14; electrolytes; never with tamoxifen ; LFTs + CBC q2wk ×2 cycles Abemaciclib: diarrhea — loperamide at the first loose stool; CBC/LFTs q2wk ×2 mo; VTE, ILD. Palbociclib: neutropenia, CBC d1 + d15 of cycles 1–2 Alpelisib / capivasertib / inavolisib: hyperglycemia — fasting glucose + HbA1c first, optimize diabetes; glucose weekly-to-biweekly in month 1; metformin first-line; rash (alpelisib: antihistamine prophylaxis) Sacituzumab: neutropenia (grade ≥3 ~50%), diarrhea; UGT1A1*28 homozygotes at higher risk. Dato-DXd: stomatitis and keratitis — steroid mouthwash + eye care Tamoxifen: VTE, endometrial cancer (annual gyn review); avoid paroxetine/fluoxetine (CYP2D6). AI: DEXA baseline + q1–2 yr Surveillance: H&P q6–12 mo ×5 yr, annual mammogram; no routine markers or imaging Key trials KEYNOTE-522 Pembro + neoadjuvant chemo, stage II–III TNBC — 5-yr OS 86.6 vs 81.7% monarchE / NATALEE Adjuvant abemaciclib (OS HR 0.84) / ribociclib (iDFS HR 0.72) DESTINY-Breast04 / 06 T-DXd in HER2-low after chemo (OS 23.4 vs 16.8) / low + ultralow after ET DESTINY-Breast03 / 09 T-DXd 2L (PFS 28.8 vs 6.8) / 1L + pertuzumab (40.7 vs 26.9) DESTINY-Breast05 / 11 T-DXd for residual HER2+ disease / neoadjuvant T-DXd → THP MONALEESA-2 Ribociclib 1L OS 63.9 vs 51.4 mo INAVO120 Inavolisib triplet, PIK3CA-mut — OS 34.0 vs 27.0 mo SERENA-6 ctDNA-guided camizestrant switch — PFS 16.0 vs 9.2 mo ASCENT / -04 SG in refractory TNBC / + pembro 1L CPS ≥10

docs.title: Colon adenocarcinoma
docs.subtitle: 2nd leading cause of cancer death · ~106,590 new cases (2024) · 5-yr survival — stage I 90%, II 70–85%, III 50–73%, IV 12–14%
docs.text: Colon adenocarcinoma 2nd leading cause of cancer death · ~106,590 new cases (2024) · 5-yr survival — stage I 90% , II 70–85% , III 50–73% , IV 12–14% Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Colon Cancer (Johnson T, Miller D) · NCCN · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup Colonoscopy with biopsy + pathology review MMR / MSI testing in ALL newly diagnosed colon cancer KRAS, NRAS, BRAF mutation + HER2 amplification by NGS panel CT C/A/P · MRI liver if potentially resectable liver mets · PET/CT in selected resectable M1 Labs: CBC, CMP, CEA Genetics referral: all diagnosed <50 y , or somatic finding with germline implications BRAF V600E + MLH1 loss largely excludes Lynch — but ~1% of Lynch is BRAF V600E Staging — AJCC 8th T1 / T2 / T3 submucosa / through muscularis propria / into pericolorectal tissue T4a / T4b through visceral peritoneum / invades adjacent organ N1 / N2 1–3 nodes (N1c = deposits only) / ≥4 nodes M1a / b / c 1 site / ≥2 sites / peritoneal Stage III any node-positive, M0 Key trials IDEA 3 vs 6 mo adjuvant — failed non-inferiority overall (HR 1.07, margin 1.12), but 3 mo CAPOX non-inferior while FOLFOX favored 6 mo (Grothey, NEJM 2018) ATOMIC adding IO to adjuvant chemo in dMMR (ASCO 2025) KEYNOTE-177 1L pembrolizumab in dMMR: PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 mo BREAKWATER 1L BRAF V600E: FOLFOX + encorafenib + cetuximab BEACON BRAF V600E later line (Kopetz, NEJM 2019) Treatment pathway Localized — stage I to III Surgery first colon is resected upfront (unlike rectal) pathology drives the adjuvant decision no adjuvant therapy for stage I Stage II (node-negative) risk factors: T4, LVI, PNI, obstruction, perforation, poor differentiation, <12 nodes low risk observe; RFs 5-FU ± oxaliplatin Stage III virtually all receive adjuvant chemotherapy age <75: fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin age >75: fluoropyrimidine alone IDEA: 3 mo CAPOX ok — FOLFOX needs 6 mo high risk (T4 and/or N2) favors 6 months dMMR / MSI-H Immunotherapy-sensitive consider neoadjuvant IO before resection adjuvant: add IO to chemo (ATOMIC) adjuvant 5-FU alone may be HARMFUL Metastatic Oligometastatic liver/lung only: surgical consult upfront FOLFOX or CAPEOX preferred — cure possible 1L by molecular subtype dMMR: pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-177) BRAF V600E: FOLFOX + encorafenib + cetuximab left-sided RAS/BRAF WT: doublet + anti-EGFR right-sided or RAS-mut: FOLFOXIRI ± bev Later lines stop oxaliplatin at ~4 months (neuropathy) swap backbone; HER2 matters in 2nd line Oxaliplatin neuropathy is the dominant long-term toxicity. Six months may raise the risk of permanent neuropathy as much as tenfold vs three months. Do not exceed ~4 months in initial metastatic therapy (OPTIMOX); never given as a single agent. Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Cycle FOLFOX oxaliplatin 85 d1 · 5-FU 1200–1500/day CIV d1–2 q14d CAPEOX / XELOX oxaliplatin 130 d1 · capecitabine 1000 BID d1–14 q21d FOLFIRI irinotecan 180 d1 · 5-FU 1200–1400/day CIV d1–2 q14d FOLFOXIRI oxaliplatin 85 · irinotecan 165 · 5-FU 1200–1400/day CIV d1–2 q14d Bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg (q3wk) or 5 mg/kg (q2wk) q21d / q14d Cetuximab / panitumumab cetuximab 400 load then 250 weekly (or 500 q2wk) · panitumumab 6 mg/kg wkly / q2wk Regorafenib ramp 80→120→160 mg weekly in C1; then 160 mg d1–21 q28d Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² PO BID d1–5 and d8–12 q28d Fruquintinib 5 mg PO daily × 21 days q28d All doses mg/m² unless stated. Institutional preference: no 5-FU bolus (higher toxicity) — which also removes the need for leucovorin as a stabilizer. Biomarker → therapy Alteration Therapy dMMR / MSI-H Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk — 1L metastatic; also neoadjuvant/adjuvant BRAF V600E, 1L FOLFOX + encorafenib 300 mg daily + cetuximab BRAF V600E, later Encorafenib + cetuximab; triplet adds binimetinib RAS WT + left-sided Cetuximab or panitumumab — no benefit if right-sided or RAS-mutant HER2 amplified Trastuzumab + pertuzumab; tucatinib 300 BID + trastuzumab; T-DXd NTRK fusion Larotrectinib 100 mg BID · entrectinib 600 mg daily Surveillance H&P + CEA q3–6 mo × 2 yr, then q6 mo — 5 years total CT C/A/P: stage II–III q6–12 mo × 5 yr; stage IV q3–6 mo × 2 yr then q6–12 mo Colonoscopy at 1 year post-op; within 3–6 mo if no complete pre-op scope If adenoma found repeat in 1 yr; otherwise 3 yr, then every 5 yr Pearls & cautions Irinotecan with great caution in the elderly, biliary obstruction, or hyperbilirubinemia Regorafenib is very toxic — many do better at lower doses; bevacizumab benefit is modest ctDNA timing conflict: results take 4–6 wk but adjuvant works best within 6 wk of surgery Metastatic rectal regimens are identical to metastatic CRC

docs.title: Hairy cell leukemia
docs.subtitle: Indolent B-cell leukemia defined by BRAF V600E · splenomegaly with pancytopenia and monocytopenia · one course of a purine analog buys most patients a decade or more; the old “variant” (now SBLPN) is a different, BRAF wild-type disease
docs.text: Hairy cell leukemia Indolent B-cell leukemia defined by BRAF V600E · splenomegaly with pancytopenia and monocytopenia · one course of a purine analog buys most patients a decade or more ; the old “variant” (now SBLPN) is a different, BRAF wild-type disease Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (Hairy Cell Leukemia Foundation consensus, Grever 2017 and 2026 update; NCCN) verified against PubMed, September 2026. Presentation Rare: <2% of leukemias ; middle-aged adults, strong male predominance Splenomegaly (often massive) without adenopathy , and pancytopenia with monocytopenia — the monocytopenia is the clue on a routine CBC Dry tap: reticulin fibrosis defeats the aspirate — diagnose on the core biopsy (interstitial “fried-egg” infiltrate) + peripheral blood flow , which finds the few circulating cells Infections are the cause of morbidity: bacterial, fungal and atypical mycobacteria (monocytopenia + neutropenia) Smear: small-to-medium cells with oval nuclei and circumferential hairy cytoplasmic projections Classic HCL vs its look-alikes Classic HCL SBLPN (ex-HCL-v) CD11c · CD103 Bright + · + + · + CD25 + − CD123 + (bright) usually − Annexin A1 (IHC) + — 100% specific Falini, Lancet 2004 − TRAP + (historical stain) variable BRAF V600E ~All (48/48; >95% in 2026 consensus) Wild-type Other driver — MAP2K1 in ~50% Waterfall 2014 Blood count Pancytopenia, low monocytes Leukocytosis, monocytes preserved Purine analog Excellent, durable Poorer, less durable HCL score (CD11c, CD103, CD123, CD25): 3–4 = classic. WHO-HAEM5 dropped “HCL-variant” and folded it into splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli (SBLPN) ; ICC 2022 keeps HCL-v as a provisional entity . When to treat — consensus Any of: Hb <11 g/dL, platelets <100,000/µL, ANC <1,000/µL Symptomatic splenomegaly , progressive cytopenias, recurrent infection or constitutional symptoms None of these → observe ; many patients sit for years CR: Hb >11 without transfusion, platelets >100,000, ANC >1,500, no hairy cells on marrow or blood, spleen regressed. MRD by IHC or flow is prognostic but not yet a treatment target Relapse cutoff is 2 years (raised from 1): relapse ≥2 yr after CR → retreat with purine analog; <2 yr → switch class IGHV4-34 — the trap. Classic-looking HCL that is BRAF wild-type : all 13 IGHV4-34+ cases were wild-type Xi, Blood 2012 . Usually unmutated, higher WBC, poor response to cladribine and shorter PFS and OS Arons, Blood 2009 ; MAP2K1 mutations cluster here too. A BRAF-negative “HCL” should prompt a second look . Treat the infection first. Cladribine and pentostatin deepen neutropenia for weeks, and post-cladribine fever is common — so defer the purine analog during active infection . If counts are too low for the infection to clear, a BRAF inhibitor (vemurafenib ± rituximab) restores counts without myelosuppression and can bridge to definitive therapy — off-label. Treatment pathway Newly diagnosed classic HCL Indication to treat? Hb <11, plt <100k, ANC <1,000, or symptoms none → observe Active infection? control it first — defer the purine analog bridge: vemurafenib ± rituximab (off-label) First line cladribine ×1 course or pentostatin + rituximab : concurrent → MRD-free CR 97% (delayed R also acceptable; see trial below) Restage ~6 months marrow biopsy + counts → CR / PR / MRD Relapse ≥2 yr after CR repeat purine analog (same or the other) ± rituximab <2 yr, or refractory vemurafenib + rituximab (CR 87%) dabrafenib + trametinib (off-label in HCL) ibrutinib · pentostatin + R · trial SBLPN (HCL-v) · IGHV4-34 HCL BRAF wild-type — a different disease cladribine + concurrent rituximab (CR 95%) BRAF inhibitors have no target relapse: ibrutinib, trials Key evidence Study Result Read it this way Scripps cladribine n=358 Single 7-day infusion: CR 91% ; 26% relapsed at a median 29 mo; retreatment CR 62% The regimen that made HCL a one-course disease Else, long-term n=233, 16 yr f/u Pentostatin or cladribine: CR 80%, median RFS 16 yr ; no difference between drugs Relapse continues late — 25% of 5-yr CRs relapse by 15 yr Intergroup Grever 1995 Pentostatin vs interferon-α: CR 76% vs 11% . 10-yr OS 81% (Flinn 2000) Pentostatin is equivalent to cladribine; no excess second cancers SAKK 32/98 n=100, randomized Cladribine daily ×5 vs weekly ×5 : response 86% in both Weekly is not less toxic (grade 3–4 neutropenia 90% vs 80%) NIH, Chihara n=68, randomized ph2 Cladribine + concurrent vs delayed (≥6 mo) rituximab : CR 100% vs 88% (NS); MRD-free CR 97% vs 24% ; at 8 yr 94% vs 12% still MRD-free Concurrent R buys deep, lasting MRD negativity at the cost of grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia 59% vs 9% . Survival benefit not shown MDACC n=139, single-arm Cladribine → rituximab: CR 97% , 10-yr EFS 87% , OS 91% Frontline classic HCL relapse only 3.6% Vemurafenib Tiacci 2015 Relapsed: ORR 96–100% , CR 35–42%; RFS 19 mo in CR, 6 mo in PR High response, short remission alone Vem + R Tiacci NEJM 2021, n=30 Median 3 prior lines: CR 87% (65% MRD-negative); PFS 78% at median 37 mo The preferred non-purine regimen at relapse Vem + obinutuzumab frontline, n=30 CR 90% , 96% of CRs MRD-negative; no relapse at 35 mo Chemo-free frontline option; single-arm Dab + tram ROAR, n=55 Relapsed: ORR 89% , CR 66% ; 24-mo PFS 94% Not FDA-approved for HCL — the tumor-agnostic label covers solid tumors only Ibrutinib n=37 Best ORR 54% ; 36-mo PFS 73% Primary endpoint not met ; modest Moxetumomab n=80 Anti-CD22 immunotoxin: CR 41%, durable CR 30%; HUS 7.5%, capillary leak 5% Withdrawn from the US market in 2023 (commercial decision) SBLPN: clad + R n=20 Concurrent rituximab: CR 95% , 5-yr PFS 63% TP53-mutant cases fare worse Dosing Regimen Dosing Cladribine 0.14 mg/kg/day IV over 2 h, days 1–5 (NIH: 0.15 mg/kg), or 0.1 mg/kg/day continuous IV ×7 days , or 0.14 mg/kg weekly ×5 — one course Clad + rituximab Cladribine 0.15 mg/kg days 1–5 + rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×8 , concurrent from day 1 (or delayed ≥6 mo) Pentostatin 4 mg/m² IV every 2 weeks until best response; hydrate; hold for renal dysfunction Vemurafenib + R Vemurafenib 960 mg PO BID ×8 weeks + rituximab 375 mg/m² ×8 doses over 18 weeks Dabrafenib + trametinib Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg daily Ibrutinib 420 mg daily Monitoring and supportive care Prolonged CD4 lymphopenia after purine analogs — median ~40 months to recover → PJP and HSV/VZV prophylaxis Irradiated blood products indefinitely after a purine analog (transfusion-associated GVHD) BSH 2020 Neutropenic fever in ~42% after cladribine. Routine G-CSF not recommended : it shortened neutropenia (9 vs 22 days) but did not cut fever or admissions Vemurafenib: rash, photosensitivity, arthralgia, cutaneous SCC / keratoacanthoma — dermatology checks. Dab/tram: pyrexia Inactivated vaccines before therapy; no live vaccines Splenic small B-cell differential Entity Distinguishing features Classic HCL CD25+ CD103+ CD123+ CD11c bright, annexin A1+ , BRAF V600E ; monocytopenia SBLPN (HCL-v) CD103+ but CD25− , annexin A1−, BRAF wild-type, MAP2K1; leukocytosis, prominent nucleoli Splenic marginal zone Polar (villous) projections , CD103 usually −, CD25 variable, annexin A1−; NOTCH2 / KLF2 ; may have a small IgM paraprotein Splenic diffuse red pulp Villous cells, red-pulp pattern, CD25−, annexin A1−; CCND3 mutations; BRAF wild-type CLL · MCL CD5+ — CD23+ (CLL) or cyclin D1+ (MCL) — HCL and its look-alikes are CD5− Annexin A1 + BRAF V600E together settle classic HCL; everything else in this list is negative for both. Pearls Splenomegaly + monocytopenia + dry tap = HCL until proven otherwise BRAF V600E is the diagnosis and the target. Wild-type → think SBLPN or IGHV4-34 Cure-like, not cure: relapse keeps happening late but responds to retreatment Moxetumomab is gone (2023) — don't list it as an option

docs.title: Burkitt lymphoma
docs.subtitle: MYC-driven, Ki-67 ~100%, curable — if you prevent tumor lysis, cover the CNS, and give intensive rituximab-containing therapy without delay. The regimen decision turns on age, fitness, and whether the CSF is involved
headings: Regimen choice — what the evidence says
Modified Magrath (Mead, Blood 2008) — q21d or on count recovery
Supportive care that trips people up
High-dose MTX — the alkalinization that DOES apply
docs.text: Burkitt lymphoma MYC-driven, Ki-67 ~100%, curable — if you prevent tumor lysis, cover the CNS, and give intensive rituximab-containing therapy without delay. The regimen decision turns on age, fitness, and whether the CSF is involved Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — Burkitt and HIV-associated lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. Biology and diagnosis Defining lesion MYC rearrangement to an Ig locus , confirmed by FISH: t(8;14) IGH ~80% · t(2;8) IGK ~15% · t(8;22) IGL ~5% . Co-operating ID3, TCF3, TP53 mutations Morphology Monomorphic medium cells, diffuse. “Starry sky” — tingible-body macrophages engulfing apoptotic debris Phenotype CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2 negative , TdT negative · Ki-67 ~100% Endemic Equatorial Africa, children; EBV+ in nearly all , malaria co-factor. Jaw / orbit , abdominal viscera Sporadic Worldwide, all ages; EBV+ in a minority. Ileocecal / abdominal mass , marrow, CNS Immunodeficiency HIV (often at relatively preserved CD4), post-transplant. Nodal, marrow and CNS disease common Not Burkitt BCL2 or BCL6 rearranged too → HGBCL double-hit (treat per DLBCL card). MYC-negative with 11q gain/loss → HGBCL with 11q aberration (WHO-HAEM5; ICC: LBCL with 11q), formerly “Burkitt-like”. TdT+ → lymphoblastic WHO-HAEM5 now subtypes Burkitt by EBV status (EBV+ vs EBV−) rather than by the epidemiologic variant. Workup — treat as an emergency Excisional or core biopsy with MYC FISH (plus BCL2, BCL6 FISH); start therapy within days TLS labs at presentation: K, phos, Ca, uric acid, creatinine, LDH — spontaneous TLS before any chemo is classic PET/CT · bone marrow biopsy · LP with cytology AND flow cytometry (brain MRI if symptoms) — CNS involved in ~19% of adults HIV , HBsAg / anti-HBc / anti-HBs, HCV · echo · G6PD before rasburicase · pregnancy test · fertility counseling No LP if circulating blasts or platelets <50,000 Risk stratification Low risk (regimen gate) All of: normal LDH, ECOG 0–1, stage I–II, no mass ≥10 cm, ≤1 extranodal site (Magrath / Mead). NCI 9177 used mass <7 cm , not 10. Everyone else is high risk (~85–90% of adults) BL-IPI (prognosis) 1 point each: age ≥40 · ECOG ≥2 · LDH >3× ULN · CNS involvement . 3-yr PFS 0 = 92% · 1 = 72% · ≥2 = 53% Olszewski, JCO 2021 Real-world (30 US centres, 641 adults): 3-yr PFS 64% , treatment-related mortality 10% — well below trial results. Rituximab (PFS 67% vs 38%) and academic-centre care (67% vs 46%) tracked with better outcome Evens, Blood 2021 . Treatment pathway Day 0 — before chemotherapy TLS prophylaxis + staging in parallel IV fluids, rasburicase , labs q6–8h, strict I/O LP / marrow; always add rituximab (LMB: EFS 75 vs 62%) Choose a regimen Low risk R-CODOX-M ×3 (A-A-A), or DA-EPOCH-R ×3 , no intrathecal (NCI 9177) High risk, CNS negative R-CODOX-M / R-IVAC ×4 (A-B-A-B) if fit, <~65 DA-EPOCH-R ×6 + IT MTX if older, HIV+, comorbid — HOVON: similar PFS, less toxicity R-hyper-CVAD / MA ×6–8 is an alternative High risk, CNS POSITIVE HD-MTX + HD-cytarabine regimen — R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC (16 IT total) or R-hyper-CVAD avoid DA-EPOCH-R : CSF+ 4-yr EFS 45.5% Response End-of-treatment PET/CT no maintenance, no consolidative ASCT in CR1 relapses are early (mostly <1 yr) and CNS-prone Relapsed / refractory — poor Clinical trial first salvage (R-ICE, R-DHAP) → ASCT if chemosensitive allo-HCT for selected young, fit patients CD19 CAR-T off-label — Burkitt not in the pivotal trials; bridge to transplant in case series Burkitt is the highest TLS-risk lymphoma (Cairo-Coiffier high-risk category). Rasburicase prophylaxis , not allopurinol alone: label 0.2 mg/kg IV daily up to 5 days, though a single fixed 6 mg dose usually suffices (handbook: give for uric acid >7.5, renal dysfunction, or WBC ≥100,000). Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis, methemoglobinemia); post-dose uric acid in a pre-chilled heparin tube on ice . NS 2–3 L/m²/day , goal UOP ~100 mL/h; labs q6–8h ; continue ≥72 h after chemo . Do NOT alkalinize urine for TLS — it promotes calcium-phosphate and xanthine precipitation (guideline: not recommended). Early nephrology if K, phos or creatinine climb. Allopurinol 300 mg BID after rasburicase. Regimen choice — what the evidence says Regimen Evidence Weak spot R-CODOX-M / R-IVAC modified Magrath LY10 (Mead 2008, MTX cut to 3 g/m²): 2-yr PFS 85% low risk, 49% high risk , with less toxicity than full-dose. Lowest CNS relapse in real-world data (~4%) Most toxic: grade 3–5 infection 56% (HOVON). Inpatient; age >65 needs dose reduction DA-EPOCH-R NCI 9177 (single arm, n=113, 25% HIV+): 4-yr EFS 84.5% — 100% low risk, 82% high risk; same across age and HIV. HOVON/SAKK randomized (CNS-negative high risk): 2-yr PFS 70% vs 76%, HR 1.42, p=0.40 — underpowered, closed early CNS. CSF+ high-risk EFS 45.5% vs 89.9% . Real-world CNS relapse 13% vs 3–4% with MTX/cytarabine regimens (aSHR 4.38) R-hyper-CVAD / MA MDACC, n=31 (29% ≥60 yr): CR 86%, 3-yr OS 89% , EFS 80%. Single arm Long (6–8 cycles), myelosuppressive; small series Rituximab Ribrag, Lancet 2016 (LMB ± R, n=260, randomized): 3-yr EFS 75% vs 62% , HR 0.59, no added toxicity — add to every regimen No regimen has beaten another for survival in a completed randomized trial. Practical rule: fit, younger, or CNS-positive → HD-MTX/cytarabine-based ; older, HIV+, or frail and CNS-negative → DA-EPOCH-R . CNS — everyone gets covered Prophylaxis is universal (IT MTX ± cytarabine built into every regimen, + systemic HD-MTX in Magrath and hyper-CVAD). The one exception: NCI 9177 low-risk patients received none and none relapsed CSF involvement is the strongest adverse factor in every series — stage it properly (cytology + flow) before cycle 1 IT CNS-positive: intensify IT (Magrath: 2 extra per cycle, 16 total; hyper-CVAD: IT twice weekly until CSF clear ×2) — systemic HD-MTX and HD-cytarabine penetrate the parenchyma, infusional EPOCH does not HIV-associated Burkitt Treat with curative intent, same regimens — HIV status no longer predicts outcome (NCI 9177 EFS 84.9% HIV+ vs 84.5% HIV−; US-UK series 3-yr PFS 61%) Continue or start ART with oncology-pharmacy review; avoid ritonavir / cobicistat boosting (CYP3A4 → vincristine neuropathy, anthracycline and etoposide toxicity) — an integrase-inhibitor backbone is usual US-UK HIV-BL cohort (n=249): baseline CNS disease 3-yr PFS 36% vs 69%; CNS recurrence higher after DA-EPOCH (sHR 2.52); CODOX-M/IVAC associated with longer PFS (aHR 0.45) — retrospective PJP prophylaxis throughout; MAC prophylaxis if CD4 <100 ; consider quinolone during nadir Modified Magrath (Mead, Blood 2008) — q21d or on count recovery Cycle Dosing (mg/m² unless stated) A — R-CODOX-M Rituximab 375 d1 · cyclophosphamide 800 d1 + 200 d2–5 (first A; later A cycles 800 d1+2) · doxorubicin 40 d1 · vincristine 1.5 (cap 2 mg) d1+8 · MTX 3000 over 24 h on d10 (300 over 1 h, then 2700 over 23 h) · IT cytarabine 70 mg d1+3 · IT MTX 12 mg d15 B — R-IVAC Rituximab 375 d1 · etoposide 60 d1–5 · ifosfamide 1500 d1–5 + mesna · cytarabine 2000 q12h ×4 d1–2 (steroid eye drops) · IT MTX 12 mg d5 Age >65 MTX 1000 (100 over 1 h, then 900 over 23 h) · ifosfamide 1000 · cytarabine 1000 CNS positive A: + IT cytarabine 70 mg d5, IT MTX 12 mg d17 · B: + IT cytarabine 70 mg d7 and d9 — 16 IT total Leucovorin 15 mg/m² IV at 36 h from MTX start, q3h to 48 h, then q6h until MTX <0.05 µM. After each IT MTX: 15 mg PO at 24 h Start cycle if ANC >1000, plt >75k, direct bili <1.4, Cr <1.2 — not required for cycle 1 or for d10 HD-MTX Rituximab was not part of LY10 (added in routine practice; Ribrag). G-CSF after the MTX level is <0.02 (A); d7–16 or pegfilgrastim d7 (B). Levofloxacin during nadir. DA-EPOCH-R (Roschewski, JCO 2020) — q21d Dosing Drugs Rituximab 375 d1 · etoposide 50, doxorubicin 10, vincristine 0.4 (no cap) , each /day CIV d1–4 · cyclophosphamide 750 d5 · prednisone 60 BID PO d1–5 (handbook lists 60/day) Cycles Low risk ×3, no IT · high risk ×6 + IT MTX 12 mg each cycle (extended IT if CSF+) Adjust CBC twice weekly; ANC nadir ≥500 → +20% (E, D, C) · <500 on 1–2 checks → same · <500 on 3 checks or plt <25k → −20% G-CSF from 24 h after chemo. Outpatient-feasible via ambulatory pump. Supportive care that trips people up Hold TMP-SMX around HD-MTX (delays clearance) — use atovaquone or pentamidine for PJP, or resume once MTX has cleared Avoid azoles that inhibit CYP3A4 (posaconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole) with vincristine — severe neuropathy and ileus. Bowel regimen with every vincristine dose HD-cytarabine: prednisolone 1% drops 2 gtt OU BID from 12 h before to 48 h after; check for cerebellar signs before each dose (higher risk with age >60 or renal dysfunction) Ifosfamide: mesna with every dose; watch for encephalopathy HBV: entecavir if HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ on rituximab · G-CSF with every cycle · quinolone during neutropenia R-hyper-CVAD / R-MA (Thomas, Cancer 2006) — alternating, 6–8 cycles Dosing A (1,3,5,7) Rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 300 q12h ×6 d1–3 (mesna) · doxorubicin 50 CIV d4 · vincristine 2 mg d4+11 · dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4, 11–14 B (2,4,6,8) Rituximab 375 · MTX 200 over 2 h + 800 over 22 h d1 · cytarabine 3000 q12h ×4 d2–3 (1000 if >60 yr or Cr >1.5) · leucovorin from 36 h CNS IT MTX 12 mg d2 + IT cytarabine 100 mg d8, cycles 1–4 (8 IT). CNS+: twice weekly until CSF clear ×2 High-dose MTX — the alkalinization that DOES apply Pre-check Drain or avoid if effusion / ascites (third-space reservoir) · stop PPIs, TMP-SMX, penicillins, NSAIDs, salicylates, probenecid · CrCl: 50% dose if 10–50, omit <10 Alkalinize ½NS + 100 mEq NaHCO₃/L at 500 mL/h ×2 h, then 125 mL/h. Start MTX only when urine pH ≥7 and UOP >100 mL/h; keep pH ≥7 until cleared Levels q24h from 24 h. Escalate leucovorin to 100 mg/m² q6h if at 24 h Cr ↑>50% or level >20 µM; 48 h >1 µM; 72 h >0.1 µM Glucarpidase 50 U/kg IV if level >1 µM with delayed clearance from renal failure. No leucovorin within 2 h either side; immunoassay unreliable for 48 h (use chromatographic assay) Contrast with TLS (page 1): urine alkalinization is required for HD-MTX (MTX precipitates in acid urine) but harmful for TLS . When both overlap (cycle 1 d10), rasburicase has already handled urate — alkalinize for the MTX. Key trials and cohorts LY10 Mead, Blood 2008 Dose-modified CODOX-M/IVAC (MTX 3 g/m²), prospective: 2-yr PFS 64% in BL; low risk 85%, high risk 49% LMB ± R Ribrag, Lancet 2016 Phase 3, n=260, HIV−: rituximab 3-yr EFS 75% vs 62% , HR 0.59 — the rituximab randomization NCI 9177 Roschewski, JCO 2020 Risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R, single arm: EFS 84.5%; CSF+ is the failure group HOVON/SAKK Chamuleau, Lancet Haem 2023 R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC vs DA-EPOCH-R, CNS− high risk: 2-yr PFS 76% vs 70%, not significant ; closed early (n=89); fewer infections with EPOCH MDACC R-hyper-CVAD Thomas, Cancer 2006 n=31: 3-yr OS 89%; rituximab improved outcome vs historical hyper-CVAD BL-IPI Olszewski, JCO 2021 Age ≥40, ECOG ≥2, LDH >3×, CNS — 3-yr PFS 92 / 72 / 53%; validated in 457 ex-US patients US real-world Evens, Blood 2021 641 adults, 30 centres: 3-yr PFS 64%, OS 70%, TRM 10% ; no difference by HIV status CNS cohort Zayac, Haematologica 2021 CNS+ in 19%; CR 59% vs 77%. 3-yr CNS relapse 13% after DA-EPOCH-R vs 4% CODOX-M/IVAC, 3% hyper-CVAD/MA HIV-BL Alderuccio, Blood Adv 2021 n=249 US-UK: 3-yr PFS 61%; CD4 did not predict; CNS relapse higher after DA-EPOCH Pearls Board triad: MYC-IG translocation + BCL2-negative + Ki-67 ~100% . BCL2-positive with MYC = think double hit, not Burkitt Urine alkalinization: never for TLS, always for HD-MTX Don’t wait for complete staging to start TLS prophylaxis — several pediatric-derived protocols (LMB) open with a low-intensity pre-phase (cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone) to debulk If CSF is positive, don’t choose DA-EPOCH-R ; if the patient is old, HIV+ or frail and CSF-negative, DA-EPOCH-R is the kinder, equally effective choice No maintenance, no consolidative transplant in CR1

docs.title: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
docs.subtitle: Mycosis fungoides · Sézary syndrome · primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs — a chronic disease managed for years: skin-directed first, systemic by compartment (skin vs blood), transplant for the few who can be cured
headings: Primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs — do not over-treat
docs.text: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma Mycosis fungoides · Sézary syndrome · primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs — a chronic disease managed for years: skin-directed first, systemic by compartment (skin vs blood), transplant for the few who can be cured Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Mycosis Fungoides/Sézary Syndrome (Chou L, Khodadoust M) · NCCN Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. What you are dealing with Entity Defining features Mycosis fungoides Most common CTCL. Patch → plaque → tumor, often in sun-protected “bathing-trunk” skin. Epidermotropic CD4+ cells, CD7 loss , Pautrier microabscesses. Skin-resident memory T-cell origin Sézary syndrome <5% of CTCL All three: erythroderma (≥80% BSA) + B2 blood + a blood clone matching the skin . Central-memory origin — a leukemic disease, not simply late MF Adverse MF variants Folliculotropic (independent predictor of progression and death) · large-cell transformation (>25% large cells; higher progression risk) · tumor stage, raised LDH Primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs 2nd most common CTCL Lymphomatoid papulosis and primary cutaneous ALCL — indolent, excellent prognosis despite anaplastic cytology. Distinguish from systemic ALCL spreading to skin (ALK+ = systemic until proven otherwise) A TCR clone alone is not diagnostic — clonal T cells occur in benign dermatoses. Early MF often needs several biopsies, ideally taken off topical steroids. Workup Skin biopsy (multiple sites) with IHC incl. CD30 and TCR gene rearrangement; measure BSA (patient palm + fingers ≈ 1%) and mSWAT Blood flow cytometry (CD4:CD8, CD4+CD7−, CD4+CD26− absolute counts) + blood TCR clone — needed to assign B stage Imaging: PET/CT or CT for T2b and above , palpable nodes, or B1–B2 blood. Stage IA with no nodes needs no imaging Excise an abnormal node — nodal histology (N1–N3) changes the stage; marrow only if unexplained cytopenias LDH, CBC, CMP; HTLV-1 serology if erythroderma or from an endemic area (ATLL mimics Sézary) ISCL/EORTC TNMB (Olsen, Blood 2022) T1 · T2 Patches/plaques <10% · ≥10% BSA (a = patch only, b = plaque) T3 · T4 ≥1 tumor ≥1 cm · erythroderma ≥80% BSA N1 · N2 · N3 Abnormal node, histology Dutch grade 1 / 2 / 3–4 (NCI LN 0–2 / 3 / 4) M1 Biopsy-proven visceral disease B0 ≤5% Sézary cells, or <250/µL, or <15% CD4+CD26− / CD4+CD7− B1 More than B0 but not B2 B2 ≥1,000/µL Sézary cells, or CD4+CD26− / CD4+CD7− / other aberrant cells by flow — plus a blood clone matching the skin Stage groups Stage T N M B IA · IB 1 · 2 0 0 0–1 IIA 1–2 1–2 0 0–1 IIB tumor 3 0–2 0 0–1 IIIA · IIIB erythrodermic 4 0–2 0 0 · 1 IVA1 = Sézary any 0–2 0 2 IVA2 · IVB any 3 · any 0 · 1 any Stage IA: 5-yr OS 94%, median survival ≥20 yr — most die of something else. Stage III–IV: median survival ~5 yr, and over half die of disease (Agar, JCO 2010; NCI PDQ). Treatment pathway Early MF — IA to IIA Skin-directed therapy IA : topical steroid, mechlorethamine gel , bexarotene gel, imiquimod, local RT IB–IIA : nbUVB (patches) or PUVA (plaques) not curative — do not escalate for cosmetics Refractory or rapidly relapsing add a low-intensity systemic: bexarotene, IFN, low-dose MTX; TSEBT 12 Gy for widespread Tumor stage IIB · LCT Limited vs generalized limited tumors: local RT 8–12 Gy + skin therapy generalized: TSEBT or systemic CD30+ or LCT: brentuximab (ALCANZA) others: HDACi, mogamulizumab, gemcitabine, liposomal doxorubicin, pralatrexate Erythrodermic III · Sézary IVA1 Treat the blood mogamulizumab (best blood responses) ECP ± IFN or bexarotene — lower blood burden romidepsin, low-dose alemtuzumab, pembrolizumab + skin care, anti-staph, antipruritics Advanced, refractory, fit Allogeneic HCT only curative option; go in remission CUTALLO: PFS 9.0 vs 3.0 mo (HR 0.38) TSEBT often used to debulk skin pre-transplant CD30+ LPD Lymphomatoid papulosis · pc-ALCL LyP: observe / topicals / low-dose MTX pc-ALCL solitary: excision or RT multifocal / relapsing: MTX or brentuximab multi-agent chemo is over-treatment Skin-directed therapy Therapy How and what to know Topical corticosteroids High-potency (clobetasol) BID for T1 patches — high response rates in limited disease. Atrophy, striae, HPA suppression with large BSA Mechlorethamine gel 0.016% Daily thin layer to lesions; gel non-inferior to compounded ointment (CAILS ORR 59% vs 48% ), faster response. Contact dermatitis ~20% — reduce frequency, add topical steroid. No systemic absorption Bexarotene gel 1% · imiquimod Retinoid gel titrated to BID–QID for limited lesions; irritation. Imiquimod for thick single plaques nbUVB · PUVA nbUVB for patches , PUVA for thicker plaques (deeper penetration); 2–3×/wk to clearance, then taper. Cumulative risk of skin cancer (PUVA: SCC, melanoma); eye protection after psoralen Local RT 8–12 Gy per lesion for palliation; 24–30 Gy for unilesional disease (curative intent). MF is exquisitely radiosensitive TSEBT 12 Gy low-dose (1 Gy ×12): ORR 88% , CR 27%, median clinical benefit ~71 wk, repeatable . 30–36 Gy gives deeper CR but more toxicity and only once or twice per lifetime Maximise skin-directed therapy and supportive care first — it lengthens time to the next systemic. Check that a systemic agent is compatible with phototherapy/TSEBT before combining. Primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs — do not over-treat Lymphomatoid papulosis: crops of papules that self-heal in weeks . No therapy changes survival — observe, topical steroids, phototherapy, or low-dose weekly MTX for scarring or frequent crops. Lifelong follow-up : associated second lymphomas (MF, ALCL, Hodgkin) Primary cutaneous ALCL: solitary/localized nodules, >75% CD30+, ALK−. Excision or RT ; multifocal → MTX or brentuximab. Staging CT/PET to exclude systemic ALCL Systemic therapy — dosing, evidence, monitoring Agent Dose Evidence · what to watch Bexarotene RXR, oral 300 mg/m²/day with food; often started lower and titrated ORR 45% in refractory IIB–IVB. Hypertriglyceridemia (pancreatitis) — start fenofibrate first, avoid gemfibrozil (raises bexarotene levels). Central hypothyroidism: TSH falls — dose levothyroxine to free T4 . Teratogen Interferon-α 3–6 MU SC daily or TIW (pegylated IFN now used — Intron A off market) Flu-like symptoms, depression, cytopenias, thyroid. Pairs well with ECP, bexarotene, PUVA Low-dose methotrexate 10–25 mg PO/SC weekly + folate Workhorse for MF and LyP . LFTs, CBC; switch to pralatrexate 15 mg/m² if more is needed Vorinostat HDACi 400 mg PO daily ORR 30% , pruritus relief 32%. Diarrhea, fatigue, thrombocytopenia, PE 5% Romidepsin HDACi 14 mg/m² IV d1, 8, 15 q28d ORR 34% , DOR 15 mo, pruritus better in 43% . Nausea; QTc — replete K/Mg . CTCL approval intact Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg q21d, up to 16 cycles ALCANZA (CD30 ≥10%): ORR4 56% vs 13% , PFS 16.7 vs 3.5 mo. Neuropathy 67% . Best for plaques/tumors, LCT , pc-ALCL Mogamulizumab anti-CCR4 1 mg/kg IV d1, 8, 15, 22 of cycle 1, then d1, 15 q28d MAVORIC: PFS 7.7 vs 3.1 mo ; ORR 28% vs 5%, Sézary 37% vs 2% — blood clears best. Drug eruption in ~24% , median onset 119 days , mimics progression — biopsy + clonality before calling relapse . Deplete Tregs: raises GVHD if given shortly before allo-HCT Denileukin diftitox-cxdl IL-2–toxin 9 µg/kg/day IV d1–5 q21d, up to 8 cycles FDA Aug 2024 , stage I–III after ≥1 systemic: ORR 36% , CR 9%. Capillary leak 20% (boxed) — weight, albumin, edema; infusion reactions, hepatotoxicity ECP 2 consecutive days q2–4 wk Erythrodermic / Sézary with modest blood burden; nearly non-immunosuppressive. Combine with IFN or bexarotene Pembrolizumab off-label 200 mg q3wk ORR 38% in advanced MF/SS; Sézary flare (erythroderma, itch) in 53% — not progression Alemtuzumab low-dose, historical 3 mg d1, then 10 mg SC TIW, max 12 wk Sézary / blood only (skips skin-resident MF cells). CMV PCR q2–3 wk + acyclovir + TMP-SMX. Off the US market — access program Gemcitabine · liposomal doxorubicin · pralatrexate Gem 1,000 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d · PLD 10–30 mg/m² q2–4wk · pralatrexate 15 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d For tumor stage and LCT. Pralatrexate at half the PTCL dose , with B12/folate Lacutamab (anti-KIR3DL2) has breakthrough designation for Sézary but is not approved ; phase 3 TELLOMAK-3 starting 2026. Multi-agent chemotherapy (CHOP, ICE, GDP) gives short responses and heavy infection risk — reserve for bridging. Itch, skin barrier and infection S. aureus colonizes ~50% of erythrodermic patients and drives flares: in one series, eradication (oral antibiotics + intranasal mupirocin) cleared carriage in >85% and improved the skin in 58% . MRSA is common — TMP-SMX or doxycycline empirically Dilute bleach baths , emollients, wet wraps; culture before calling progression — infection and drug eruption both mimic it Bacteremia from skin portals is a major risk in erythrodermic disease — avoid lines through involved skin when possible Pruritus : often the dominant symptom; antihistamines rarely enough. Gabapentin, mirtazapine, aprepitant; disease control is the best antipruritic (romidepsin 43%, vorinostat 32% itch relief) Lifelong skin-cancer surveillance after PUVA, TSEBT and mechlorethamine Key trials MAVORIC Mogamulizumab vs vorinostat — PFS 7.7 vs 3.1 mo, HR 0.53; Sézary ORR 37% vs 2% ALCANZA BV vs MTX/bexarotene, CD30+ MF or pc-ALCL — ORR4 56% vs 13% CUTALLO Allo-HCT vs none (donor availability) — PFS 9.0 vs 3.0 mo, HR 0.38 Study 302 Denileukin diftitox-cxdl — ORR 36%, capillary leak 20% CITN-10 Pembrolizumab — ORR 38%, durable Lessin 2013 Mechlorethamine gel vs ointment — non-inferior, faster
