docs.text: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma DLBCL NOS · HGBCL with MYC + BCL2 rearrangements · PMBL · transformed · HIV-associated. ~60–70% are cured with first-line R-CHOP-based therapy — the questions are double-hit status, IPI, CNS risk, fitness for anthracycline, and at relapse, timing (<12 vs ≥12 months) and CAR-T eligibility Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J, Gupta NK) and HIV-associated lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. What the pathologist has to tell you Call Why it matters Cell of origin (Hans IHC) GCB = CD10+, or CD10− BCL6+ MUM1−. Everything else is non-GCB (ABC-like) — worse on R-CHOP, and the group where Pola-R-CHP gained most. GEP is more accurate than IHC MYC / BCL2 / BCL6 FISH MYC-rearranged in ~10% of aggressive B-NHL, half with BCL2. MYC + BCL2 rearranged = HGBCL / DLBCL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (formerly “double hit”). WHO-HAEM5 folds MYC + BCL6 back into DLBCL NOS / HGBL NOS; ICC keeps it provisional Double expressor (IHC) MYC ≥40% + BCL2 ≥50% protein without rearrangement — ~20–25%, intermediate prognosis, treated as DLBCL NOS . Not the same as double hit CD30, EBER, CD5 CD30 → BV option at relapse · EBV+ DLBCL (any age, worse) · CD5+ enriched for CNS relapse Workup Excisional or core biopsy — never FNA ; hematopathology review PET/CT (staging + Deauville response); marrow biopsy only if it changes management — PET detects most marrow disease Labs: CBC, CMP, LDH , uric acid; HBsAg + anti-HBc , HCV, HIV Echo or MUGA before anthracycline · fertility counselling · pregnancy test LP (cytology + flow) if CNS-IPI high or high-risk site; MRI brain if symptomatic IPI — APLES: age >60 · PS ≥2 · LDH ↑ · ≥2 extranodal · stage III–IV Score 5-yr OS pre-R 3-yr OS R-CHOP Low (0–1) 73% 91% Low-intermediate (2) 51% 81% High-intermediate (3) 43% 65% High (4–5) 26% 59% Shipp NEJM 1993 · Ziepert JCO 2010. CNS-IPI = IPI + kidney/adrenal (0–6): 2-yr CNS relapse 0–1: 0.6% · 2–3: 3.4% · 4–6: 10.2% (Schmitz JCO 2016). Treatment pathway Limited stage (I–II, non-bulky) R-CHOP ×4 is the backbone FLYER: age ≤60, aaIPI 0, <7.5 cm → 4 R-CHOP + 2 R S1001: R-CHOP ×3 → iPET; neg → 1 more (no RT) iPET-positive (~11%) → ISRT bulky or IPI-risk → treat as advanced Advanced (III–IV, bulky, or IPI ≥2) R-CHOP ×6 or Pola-R-CHP ×6 Pola-R-CHP for IPI ≥2 (POLARIX): PFS gain, still no significant OS gain at 5 yr HGBCL MYC+BCL2: DA-EPOCH-R (see p2) PMBL: DA-EPOCH-R, or R-CHOP ± RT (see p2) End-of-treatment PET/CT Deauville 1–3 = CMR → observe no maintenance, no consolidative ASCT in CR Deauville 4–5 → biopsy before calling failure Unfit for full R-CHOP Age >80 or frail R-mini-CHOP (2-yr OS 59%) — single-arm do a geriatric assessment, prephase prednisone LVEF low / prior anthracycline R-CHOP + dexrazoxane + serial TTE (borderline) R-GCVP · R-CEOP (inferior to R-CHOP) · R-CEPP R-CDOP (liposomal doxorubicin) Relapsed / refractory Early (<12 mo) or primary refractory CAR-T: axi-cel or liso-cel (ZUMA-7, TRANSFORM) bridge with R-chemo, pola, or RT Late (≥12 mo), transplant-fit salvage R-ICE / R-DHAP / R-GDP → ASCT if CMR/PR CAR-T is also reasonable — data are from <12 mo Transplant-ineligible or 3L+ liso-cel (PILOT) · bispecific · pola-BR · tafa-len BV-R² · loncastuximab · trial — see page 2 Limited stage — the evidence FLYER : 4 R-CHOP + 2 rituximab non-inferior to 6 R-CHOP — 3-yr PFS 96% vs 93% , a third less toxicity. Only for age 18–60, aaIPI 0, bulk <7.5 cm SWOG S1001 (single-arm phase 2): R-CHOP ×3 → interim PET; 89% were PET-negative and got just 1 more cycle, no RT . 5-yr PFS 87%, OS 89%; iPET-positive patients (RT) did as well SWOG 8736 (CHOP ×3 + RT beat CHOP ×8) is pre-rituximab, and its advantage vanished on long follow-up . RT now: bulk, PET-positive residual, or when chemo must be short Advanced stage — the evidence R-CHOP is 20+ years old (GELA LNH-98.5: 10-yr OS 43.5% vs 27.6% over CHOP). Many add-ons failed: ibrutinib (PHOENIX), obinutuzumab (GOYA), venetoclax (CAVALLI), R-CHOP vs DA-EPOCH-R (CALGB 50303) POLARIX (Pola-R-CHP) : 2-yr PFS 76.7% vs 70.2%, HR 0.73. 5-yr update: PFS HR 0.77 (64.9% vs 59.1%), OS HR 0.85 — not significant . Benefit concentrated in ABC/non-GCB, IPI 3–5, age >60 . Needs G-CSF. Standard option for IPI ≥2 frontMIND (tafasitamab + lenalidomide + R-CHOP, IPI 3–5): PFS HR 0.75, 2-yr 71.1% vs 62.9%; OS immature (HR 0.85). More grade ≥3 AEs (87% vs 76%) and fatal AEs (6% vs 4%) . Not FDA-approved — sBLA filed 2026 CNS prophylaxis — the case against HD-MTX Who is high risk: CNS-IPI 4–6 · kidney/adrenal · testicular · breast, uterine · epidural / paranasal / skull base · HGBCL MYC+BCL2 HD-MTX does not clearly prevent CNS relapse. 1,923 ultra-high-risk patients (Wilson JCO 2026): 3-yr CNS relapse 8.1% with vs 9.3% without HD-MTX , adjusted HR 1.13 — no benefit in any subgroup. Alberta cohort: 11.2% vs 12.2% End-of-treatment timing is no worse than intercalated (5.8% vs 5.7%) and avoids R-CHOP delays. Adding IT did not lower CNS relapse Practical: image/LP high-risk patients at diagnosis; testicular DLBCL still gets CNS-directed therapy + contralateral testis RT ; otherwise HD-MTX 3–3.5 g/m² ×2–4 is a shared-decision, not a default Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor I One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring) II ≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II III Regions on both sides of the diaphragm IV Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site A / B B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats S · X · E S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm , or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum. HGBCL with MYC + BCL2 rearrangements FISH every new DLBCL — morphology and COO do not predict it. Often high LDH, marrow and CNS involvement DA-EPOCH-R ×6 is the usual choice (single-arm, MYC-rearranged: 4-yr EFS 71%, OS 77%; Dunleavy 2018) — no randomized proof it beats R-CHOP ; Pola-R-CHP is used by some (small POLARIX subset). Evaluate the CNS at diagnosis No consolidative ASCT in first CR. Relapse → CAR-T Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBL) Who Young (median ~30s), women , bulky anterior mediastinal mass ± SVC syndrome. Biology overlaps nodular-sclerosis cHL: 9p24.1 amplification → PD-L1/PD-L2 ; CD30 often weakly + DA-EPOCH-R ×6 NCI phase 2 (n=51): EFS 93% , OS 97% at 5 yr; only 2 of 51 needed RT. Avoids mediastinal RT (breast cancer, cardiac disease) in young women R-CHOP ×6 ± RT Accepted alternative. IELSG37 : if end-of-chemo PET is CMR (Deauville 1–3), omit RT — 30-mo PFS 96.2% observation vs 98.5% RT, 5-yr OS 99% both. Deauville 5 does poorly (5-yr PFS 60%) Relapsed Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-170: ORR 45%, CR 13%; accelerated approval) · nivolumab + BV (CheckMate 436: ORR 73%, CR 37%; not FDA-approved for PMBL) · CAR-T (included in LBCL labels) · salvage + ASCT if chemosensitive Mediastinal gray-zone lymphoma (PMBL/cHL features, often CD15+, CD20 variable): worse than either; DA-EPOCH-R, ISRT if localized. HIV-associated aggressive B-cell lymphoma Principles Continue or start ART through chemotherapy (check interactions — avoid boosted PIs/cobicistat with vincristine). PJP (TMP-SMX), MAC prophylaxis if CD4 <100 , fluconazole, acyclovir; consider quinolone at nadir if CD4 <100 DLBCL R-CHOP or DA-EPOCH-R ×6 (with ART, outcomes approach HIV-negative). AMC-034: concurrent R-EPOCH CR 73% vs sequential 55%. Rituximab caveat: CD4 <50 — AMC-010 infectious deaths 14% vs 2% (60% of them at CD4 <50) Plasmablastic CD20− , CD138+, MUM1+, EBV+ in most, MYC often rearranged; oral cavity. Rituximab useless — DA-EPOCH (± bortezomib, small series); poor outcomes PEL HHV8+ (most EBV+), effusions without a mass , CD20−, CD30+, CD138+. Modified EPOCH (NCI: median OS 22 mo); IL-6 high = worse. Exclude KSHV-MCD/KS CNS prophylaxis IT MTX for marrow, paranasal sinus, testicular or epidural involvement (handbook): 12 mg d1+5 of cycles 3–5, or weekly ×4 in cycle 1 Relapsed / refractory DLBCL — agents, evidence, status (Sept 2026) Setting · agent Evidence Status / caveat 2L, early relapse axi-cel ZUMA-7 vs salvage + ASCT: EFS 8.3 vs 2.0 mo (HR 0.40); 4-yr OS 54.6% vs 46.0%, HR 0.73 — the only 2L CAR-T OS win Regular approval (Apr 2022). Gr ≥3 CRS 6%, neuro 21% liso-cel TRANSFORM : EFS NR vs 2.4 mo, CR 74% vs 43%; OS HR 0.72, NS (crossover-adjusted HR 0.42) Approved 2L (Jun 2022), incl. transplant-ineligible (PILOT ORR 80%, median age 74). Gr 3 CRS 1% tisa-cel BELINDA negative : EFS 3.0 vs 3.0 mo, HR 1.07 3L+ only . Lowest CR of the three (JULIET CR 40%) 2L, late relapse salvage + ASCT PARMA (pre-R): ASCT 5-yr EFS 46% vs 12%. CORAL : R-ICE = R-DHAP (ORR ~63%); 3-yr EFS 20% if relapse <12 mo vs 45% if later Standard for chemosensitive late relapse; 2–3 cycles then BEAM-ASCT Transplant-ineligible glofit-GemOx STARGLO : OS 25.5 vs 12.9 mo (HR 0.62) vs R-GemOx; enrollment largely ex-US FDA CRL Jul 2025 — not approved in US (US applicability); still a handbook/NCCN option epco-GemOx EPCORE NHL-2 (single-arm): ORR 85%, CR 61%, median OS 21.6 mo Not FDA-approved. EPCORE DLBCL-4 (epco + len vs R-GemOx) PFS positive, topline Jun 2026 pola-BR GO29365: CR 40% vs 18%; OS 12.4 vs 4.7 mo — only 40 per arm Approved 2019. Bendamustine impairs later T-cell collection — avoid before CAR-T apheresis tafa-len L-MIND single-arm: ORR 57.5%, CR 41%, mPFS 11.6 mo (5-yr) — best after 1 prior line Still accelerated ; CD19 — not before CD19 CAR-T is a real concern BV + R² ECHELON-3 vs placebo + R²: OS 13.8 vs 8.5 mo, HR 0.63 — benefit regardless of CD30 Approved Feb 2025, 3L+, CAR-T and ASCT-ineligible 3L+ CAR-T ZUMA-1 (axi-cel) ORR 82%, CR 54% · TRANSCEND (liso-cel) ORR 73%, CR 53% · JULIET (tisa-cel) ORR 52%, CR 40% All approved 3L+; high-risk, chemo-refractory populations glofitamab NP30179: CR 39% (35% post-CAR-T), fixed 12 cycles ; median CR duration ~30 mo Accelerated , ≥2 lines. Obinutuzumab pretreatment epcoritamab EPCORE NHL-1: ORR 63%, CR 39%, SC, until progression. EPCORE DLBCL-1 vs R-GemOx/BR: PFS HR 0.74 (3.5 vs 3.0 mo) but OS HR 0.96 — US primary endpoint missed Accelerated , ≥2 lines; confirmatory trial missed OS (EHA Jun 2026) loncastuximab CD19-PBD ADC. LOTIS-2: ORR 48%, CR 24%. LOTIS-5 (lonca-R vs R-GemOx): PFS 6.1 vs 4.7 mo, HR 0.73; OS HR 0.96 Accelerated; confirmatory positive on PFS (Jun 2026). Edema/effusions, photosensitivity, GGT selinexor SADAL: ORR 28%, single-arm DLBCL indication withdrawn Apr 30, 2026 (myeloma unaffected) Sequencing: CAR-T first when feasible — bispecifics work after CAR-T (glofit CR 35%), but CAR-T after CD19-directed therapy (tafasitamab, lonca) is less certain; confirm CD19 by IHC. Avoid bendamustine before apheresis. Choosing therapy at first relapse Biopsy the relapse — confirm LBCL, check CD19 (before CD19-directed agents) and CD20 (lost in some after anti-CD20 therapy) Timing is the strongest predictor. In CORAL, relapse <12 months after rituximab-containing therapy gave 3-yr EFS of only 20% with salvage + ASCT — this is why CAR-T replaced ASCT for early relapse CAR-T eligibility is about organ function and performance status more than age — PILOT treated a median age of 74. Refer at relapse, not after failed salvage Bridging: steroids, RT to bulky sites, pola-R ± bendamustine-free chemo; avoid bendamustine before apheresis After CAR-T failure: bispecific (glofitamab fixed-duration, epcoritamab continuous), BV-R², loncastuximab, allo-HCT in fit chemosensitive patients, trial Transformed indolent lymphoma Biopsy the fastest-growing / highest-SUV site (SUV discordance, rising LDH, B symptoms) Anthracycline-naive → treat as de novo DLBCL (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP). Anthracycline-exposed → manage as R/R DLBCL CAR-T and bispecific labels include DLBCL arising from follicular/indolent lymphoma . Richter (from CLL) is different — see the CLL card Frontline dosing Regimen Dosing (mg/m² unless stated) R-CHOP q21d ×6 Rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 750 · doxorubicin 50 · vincristine 1.4 (cap 2 mg) — all d1; prednisone 100 mg d1–5 (handbook: 40 mg/m²). G-CSF if age ≥60 Pola-R-CHP q21d ×6 (+2 R) Polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg replaces vincristine; R 375 · C 750 · H 50 d1; prednisone 100 mg d1–5. G-CSF required DA-EPOCH-R q21d ×6 R 375 d1; etoposide 50 + doxorubicin 10 + vincristine 0.4 /day CIV d1–4 (96 h); cyclophosphamide 750 d5; prednisone 60 BID d1–5 (NCI protocol; handbook lists 60/day); G-CSF from d6. CBC twice weekly: ANC nadir ≥500 → +20% (E, H, C); <500 on 3 checks or plt <25k → −20% R-mini-CHOP q21d ×6 R 375 · C 400 · H 25 · V 1 mg flat d1; prednisone 40 d1–5 R-GCVP q21d R 375 d1; gemcitabine 1000 d1+8; C 750 + V 1–1.4 d1; prednisolone 100 mg d1–5 — anthracycline-free HD-MTX (if used) 3–3.5 g/m² ×2–4 after R-CHOP; alkalinize urine pH >7, leucovorin rescue, levels to <0.1 µM; no third-spacing, no PPI/NSAID/TMP-SMX Deauville 5-point score 1 · 2 No uptake · uptake ≤ mediastinum 3 Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response 4 · 5 Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure Response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited. (The handbook itself specifies only PET/CT at completion, plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis.) CRS and ICANS (ASTCT 2019) Grade CRS (fever ≥38 + …) ICANS (ICE score) 1 Fever alone ICE 7–9, awakens spontaneously 2 Hypotension without pressors and/or O₂ <6 L NC ICE 3–6, wakes to voice 3 One pressor and/or high-flow / face-mask O₂ ICE 0–2, wakes to touch; focal edema, seizure resolving 4 Multiple pressors and/or positive pressure Unarousable, status, diffuse edema CRS: tocilizumab 8 mg/kg (max 800 mg) from grade 2 (earlier for CAR-T), add dexamethasone 10 mg q6h if refractory or grade 3+. ICANS: dexamethasone 10 mg q6h from grade 2; tocilizumab does not treat isolated ICANS (may worsen it); levetiracetam, neuro checks. Bispecific CRS clusters in cycle 1 after step-up doses. Salvage and R/R dosing Regimen Dosing R-ICE q14–21d R 375 d1; ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV 24 h d2 ; carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2; etoposide 100 d1–3 R-DHAP q21d R 375 d1; cisplatin 100 CIV d1; cytarabine 2000 q12h ×2 d2 (1000 if >60; steroid eye drops); dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4. (R-DHAX: oxaliplatin 100) R-GDP q21d R 375 d1; gemcitabine 1000 d1+8; dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4; cisplatin 75 d1 — outpatient, non-inferior to R-DHAP (LY.12) Pola-BR q21d ×6 Polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg + R 375 d1; bendamustine 90 d1+2 Tafa-len q28d Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg C1 d1, 4, 8, 15, 22 → C2–3 weekly → C4+ d1+15; lenalidomide 25 mg d1–21 ×12 cycles, then tafasitamab alone Loncastuximab q21d 0.15 mg/kg ×2 cycles, then 0.075 mg/kg ; dexamethasone 4 mg BID d−1 to d1 BV-R² q21d BV 1.2 mg/kg (max 120 mg) + rituximab q3wk + lenalidomide 20 mg daily Glofitamab IV q21d ×12 Obinutuzumab 1000 mg C1D1 → 2.5 mg C1D8 (inpatient 24 h) → 10 mg C1D15 → 30 mg C2–12. Dexamethasone 20 mg IV before C1–3 doses Epcoritamab SC q28d 0.16 mg C1D1 → 0.8 mg C1D8 → 48 mg C1D15, D22 ; weekly C2–3, q2wk C4–9, q4wk C10+. Dexamethasone 15 mg (or prednisolone 100) on dosing day + 3 days after in C1. C1D15: outpatient monitoring allowed since Apr 2026 CAR-T (single infusion) Axi-cel 2×10⁶/kg (max 2×10⁸) after flu 30 + cy 500 ×3 d · Liso-cel 90–110×10⁶ (2L) after flu 30 + cy 300 ×3 d · Tisa-cel 0.6–6×10⁸ after flu 25 + cy 250 ×3 d Toxicity and monitoring Hepatitis B with every anti-CD20 (and bispecifics): HBsAg+ → entecavir/tenofovir; HBsAg− anti-HBc+ → prophylaxis (or monthly DNA); continue ≥12 months after the last dose Cardiac: baseline echo; R-CHOP ×6 = doxorubicin 300 mg/m². Risk rises steeply past 400–450 mg/m² — dexrazoxane or anthracycline-free regimen when EF borderline Tumor flare with bispecifics (and lenalidomide): painful node swelling, can compress airway/organs — steroids, antihistamine, hold Infection: acyclovir + PJP prophylaxis with bispecifics, CAR-T, pola-BR, EPOCH; IVIG if IgG <400 with infections; CMV monitoring on bispecifics CAR-T: REMS removed Jun 2025 — stay near center 2 weeks , no driving 2 weeks. Prolonged cytopenias; secondary T-cell malignancy boxed warning Neuropathy from vincristine (cap 2 mg) and polatuzumab; TLS prophylaxis for bulky disease or high LDH Key trials GELA LNH-98.5 R-CHOP vs CHOP, age 60–80 — 10-yr OS 43.5% vs 27.6% POLARIX Pola-R-CHP: PFS HR 0.73 → 0.77 at 5 yr; OS HR 0.85, NS frontMIND Tafa-len-R-CHOP: PFS HR 0.75; more fatal AEs; OS immature FLYER / S1001 Limited stage: 4 cycles enough; PET-adapted, RT for iPET+ only ZUMA-7 Axi-cel 2L: EFS HR 0.40, OS HR 0.73 TRANSFORM / BELINDA Liso-cel 2L EFS HR 0.35 (OS NS) / tisa-cel 2L negative STARGLO Glofit-GemOx OS HR 0.62 — US CRL (applicability) EPCORE DLBCL-1 Epcoritamab vs chemo: PFS HR 0.74, OS HR 0.96 (NS) ECHELON-3 BV + R²: OS 13.8 vs 8.5 mo IELSG37 PMBL in CMR: RT omission non-inferior Wilson 2026 HD-MTX: no CNS-relapse reduction in 1,923 ultra-high-risk SWOG 8736 CHOP ×3 + RT vs CHOP ×8 — early edge lost with time R-mini-CHOP Age >80, single-arm: 2-yr OS 59% NCI DA-EPOCH-R PMBL EFS 93% without RT · MYC-rearranged 4-yr EFS 71% PARMA / CORAL ASCT beats salvage alone / R-ICE = R-DHAP; early relapse fares poorly ZUMA-1 / JULIET / TRANSCEND 3L+ CAR-T: CR 54% / 40% / 53% PILOT Liso-cel 2L, transplant-ineligible: ORR 80% NP30179 / EPCORE NHL-1 Glofitamab CR 39% (fixed) / epcoritamab CR 39% (continuous) GO29365 / L-MIND Pola-BR OS 12.4 vs 4.7 mo / tafa-len ORR 58%, CR 41% LOTIS-2 / LOTIS-5 Lonca ORR 48% / lonca-R vs R-GemOx PFS HR 0.73 KEYNOTE-170 / CM436 R/R PMBL: pembro ORR 45% / nivo-BV ORR 73% AMC-010 / AMC-034 HIV: rituximab deaths at CD4 <50 / concurrent R-EPOCH CR 73%

docs.text: Follicular lymphoma The prototype indolent lymphoma — incurable when advanced, but usually a disease measured in many years . Treat symptoms and burden (GELF), not the scan; POD24 and transformation are the events that change prognosis. Old grade 3B is now follicular large B-cell lymphoma — treat as DLBCL Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — follicular lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. Biology and classification t(14;18) IGH::BCL2 ~85% of classic FL BCL2 juxtaposed to the IGH enhancer → BCL2 overexpression blocks apoptosis . Germinal-center phenotype: CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2+; CD5−, CD23− (usually). CREBBP / KMT2D / EZH2 mutations are common secondary hits Classic FL (cFL) WHO-HAEM5 Old grades 1, 2 and 3A. Grading is now optional — poorly reproducible and of little value for individual treatment. Grade 3A is managed as FL Follicular large B-cell lymphoma WHO-HAEM5 name for old grade 3B (sheets of centroblasts, no centrocytes; often CD10− and t(14;18)−). Treat as DLBCL with R-CHOP. ICC 2022 keeps the name “FL grade 3B” Variants that should not be over-treated Pediatric-type FL (young, localized, BCL2−, excellent outcome) · duodenal-type FL (low dissemination risk) · in situ follicular B-cell neoplasm (incidental) Workup Excisional or generous core biopsy — architecture and centroblast content cannot be judged on FNA PET/CT for staging; Lugano / Ann Arbor. Marrow biopsy when it would change management (e.g. apparent limited stage before RT) CBC, CMP, LDH, β2-microglobulin , HBsAg + anti-HBc (reactivation with anti-CD20), HCV, HIV Biopsy the PET-hottest lesion if SUV is discordant or one node grows out of step — it is the site most likely to have transformed FLIPI — “NoLASH”, 1 point each Risk % 5-yr OS 10-yr OS Low (0–1) 36 91% 71% Intermediate (2) 37 78% 51% High (3–5) 27 53% 36% No dal areas >4 · L DH >ULN · A ge ≥60 · S tage III–IV · H gb <12 (Solal-Céligny, Blood 2004; pre-rituximab era). FLIPI-2 : age >60, β2M >ULN, marrow involved, Hgb <12, largest node >6 cm — 5-yr PFS 80% / 51% / 19% . Neither index tells you when to treat — GELF does. Treatment pathway Limited stage (I–contiguous II) ISRT 24 Gy / 12 fractions potentially curative ; 24 Gy = 40–45 Gy (Lowry) 4 Gy ×2 is inferior for durable control (FoRT) adding R-CVP to RT improved PFS, not OS (TROG 99.03) Advanced stage GELF-negative, asymptomatic observe · or rituximab 375 weekly ×4 GELF-positive (high burden) BR (StiL) · R-CHOP · R-CVP or obinutuzumab with chemo (GALLIUM) or R² — chemo-free, equivalent (RELEVANCE) older/unfit: rituximab alone ± chlorambucil Maintenance (optional) rituximab q8wk ×2 yr (PRIMA) or obinutuzumab PFS gain, no OS gain — weigh infections Relapse Rebiopsy first exclude transformation — mandatory after POD24 2L+ (any time after 1 prior line) epcoritamab + R² (EPCORE FL-1) · tafasitamab + R² R² (AUGMENT) · alternative chemoimmunotherapy chemosensitive POD24: consider auto-HCT 3L+ CAR-T : axi-cel, liso-cel, tisa-cel bispecifics : mosunetuzumab, epcoritamab zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab (ROSEWOOD) allo-HCT: young, fit, multiply relapsed GELF — any one = high burden, treat • ≥3 nodal sites, each ≥3 cm • Any nodal or extranodal mass ≥7 cm • B symptoms or other disease-related symptoms • Splenomegaly · effusion or ascites · organ compression • Cytopenias (ANC <1,000 or platelets <100,000) · leukemic phase >5,000/µL Brice, JCO 1997. Meeting none = observe. Watch-and-wait has never lost survival against early treatment; rituximab ×4 delays the need for next therapy (3-yr no new treatment 88% vs 46% , HR 0.21; Ardeshna, Lancet Oncol 2014) but has not improved OS. First-line evidence Question Answer BR vs R-CHOP StiL NHL1 BR: median PFS 69.5 vs 31.2 mo , HR 0.58, far less toxicity (no alopecia, less neuropathy). No OS difference Obinutuzumab vs rituximab GALLIUM 7-yr PFS 63.4% vs 55.7% ; OS identical (88.5% vs 87.2%) . More serious AEs (48.9% vs 43.4%) and infusion reactions. With bendamustine: more grade 3–5 infections, second cancers and fatal events — prolonged T-cell depletion R² vs R-chemo RELEVANCE Negative superiority trial — 6-yr PFS 60% vs 59%, OS 89% both. An equivalent chemo-free option: less neutropenia, more rash Maintenance PRIMA Median PFS 10.5 vs 4.1 yr at 9 yr follow-up; no OS benefit ; grade 2–4 infections 39% vs 24% Low burden: retreat or maintain? RESORT Rituximab retreatment at progression = maintenance for time to treatment failure (3.9 vs 4.3 yr), using 4 vs 18 doses POD24 is the prognostic event that matters. ~20% progress within 2 years of first-line chemoimmunotherapy; their 5-yr OS is ~50% vs ~90% (FLIPI-adjusted HR 6.4; Casulo, JCO 2015). Implications: rebiopsy (a large share are transformed), avoid simply repeating the same chemo, and move early to R²-based triplets, CAR-T or bispecifics ; consolidate chemosensitive relapse with auto-HCT in selected patients. Pearls FLIPI prognosticates; GELF decides. A high FLIPI with no GELF criterion is still a reason to observe No first-line upgrade has improved survival — not obinutuzumab, not maintenance, not R². Choose on toxicity and patient priorities Old grade 3B (FLBL) gets R-CHOP , not BR; grade 3A is treated as FL Rebiopsy every progression that looks different — POD24, a discordant node, a hot PET lesion, a rising LDH Think ahead to CAR-T before giving bendamustine to a high-risk patient Relapsed / refractory — the agents Agent · US status Evidence R² (lenalidomide + rituximab) Regular approval (FL, MZL; 2019) AUGMENT (phase 3, FL + MZL, not rituximab-refractory): PFS 39.4 vs 14.1 mo , HR 0.46; 5-yr update OS HR 0.59 . Benefit carried by FL — the MZL subgroup was not significant Epcoritamab + R² Approved 2L+, Nov 2025 EPCORE FL-1 (phase 3, ≥1 prior line): ORR 95% vs 79% , PFS HR 0.21 , 16-mo PFS 85.5% vs 40.2%. Grade ≥3 AEs 90% vs 68%; CRS low grade (gr 2 in 5%). OS immature Tafasitamab + R² Approved 2L+, Jun 2025 inMIND (phase 3, double-blind): median PFS 22.4 vs 13.9 mo , HR 0.43. No CRS — a fit for patients unsuited to T-cell engagers Mosunetuzumab (CD20×CD3, IV) Accelerated, 3L+ Single-arm phase 2, 3L+: CR 60% ; fixed duration — 8 cycles if CR, up to 17 . CRS 44%, mostly grade 1–2. CELESTIMO (+ lenalidomide vs R², 2L+) met PFS — topline only, Sept 2026 Epcoritamab (CD20×CD3, SC) Regular approval, 3L+ (Nov 2025) EPCORE NHL-1 FL cohort, 3L+: ORR 82% , CR 62.5% ; continuous until progression. 3-step-up dosing cut CRS to 49% (none ≥grade 3) Axi-cel Accelerated, 3L+ ZUMA-5 (single arm, 3L+): ORR 94% FL; median PFS 62.2 mo (all iNHL) at 5-yr follow-up; few relapses after 30 mo. Grade ≥3 neurotoxicity 19% Liso-cel Accelerated, 3L+ (May 2024) TRANSCEND FL : 3L+ ORR 97% , CR 94%; 2L high-risk (POD24) ORR 96%. CRS 58% (grade ≥3 1%) Tisa-cel Accelerated, 3L+ ELARA : CR 69%, ORR 86%; no grade ≥3 CRS Zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab Accelerated, 3L+ (Mar 2024) ROSEWOOD (randomized phase 2 vs obinutuzumab): ORR 69% vs 46% , median PFS 28.0 vs 10.4 mo. Confirmatory MAHOGANY (vs R²) ongoing No head-to-head data between CAR-T and bispecifics. CAR-T gives the most durable single-shot responses; bispecifics are off-the-shelf and outpatient. Recent bendamustine blunts CAR-T expansion and outcome (ZUMA-5) — plan the sequence. Withdrawn — do not reach for these Agent What happened Tazemetostat (EZH2) Accelerated approval 2020 (3L+ EZH2-mutant, or no alternative). Withdrawn from the US market 2026 : in SYMPHONY-1 (+ R²), hematologic second cancers (MDS/AML, B-ALL) in 5.7% vs 0% , 3 deaths PI3K inhibitors Idelalisib, duvelisib FL indications withdrawn 2021–22; umbralisib withdrawn 2022 (excess deaths); copanlisib withdrawn Nov 2023 (CHRONOS-4 negative). Class problem: infections, colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, and an OS signal Ibrutinib Never approved for FL; confirmatory SELENE (FL/MZL) missed PFS Transformation 10-yr cumulative risk ~5–8% in the rituximab era (5.2% with rituximab vs 8.7% without; Aristotle, Lancet Haematol 2018) Suspect it with discordant nodal growth, new B symptoms, rising LDH, hypercalcemia, new extranodal disease, or a PET lesion much hotter than the rest Biopsy the PET-hottest site — a random node can miss it. Check MYC : with the existing BCL2 rearrangement a MYC break makes it HGBL with MYC + BCL2 Treat as DLBCL: anthracycline-naïve → R-CHOP; already had R-CHOP → salvage + auto-HCT or CAR-T (axi-cel, liso-cel and tisa-cel labels include DLBCL arising from FL) How to choose at relapse Late relapse, low burden: rituximab again, or R². Symptomatic, first relapse: epcoritamab + R² is now the strongest randomized 2L data; tafasitamab + R² if a T-cell engager is not suitable POD24 or double-refractory (anti-CD20 + alkylator): favor CAR-T (liso-cel has 2L POD24 data) or a bispecific; auto-HCT for chemosensitive early relapse Frail: rituximab alone, R², or zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab. Palliation of a symptomatic node: 2 × 2 Gy Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing Rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×4 ; maintenance 375 q8 wk ×2 yr (PRIMA). SC rituximab 1400 mg after a first full IV dose BR Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1+2 + rituximab 375 d1, q28d ×6 R-CHOP / R-CVP Rituximab 375, cyclophosphamide 750, vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d1, prednisone 40 mg/m² d1–5, ± doxorubicin 50 — q21d ×6 (CHOP) or ×8 (CVP) Obinutuzumab 1000 mg flat, C1 d1, 8, 15 , then d1 of each cycle (C2–6 with benda, C2–8 with CHOP/CVP); maintenance 1000 mg q2 mo ×2 yr R² Lenalidomide 20 mg PO d1–21 q28d ×12 (10 mg if CrCl 30–59); rituximab 375 weekly C1 then d1 C2–5 Epcoritamab + R² Epcoritamab 48 mg SC after step-up, weekly C1–3, then q4wk C4–12 (fixed duration) + R² as above Epcoritamab mono SC 0.16 → 0.8 → 3 → 48 mg (C1 d1, 8, 15, 22), 48 mg weekly C2–3, q2wk C4–9, then q4wk until progression Mosunetuzumab IV 1 → 2 → 60 mg (C1 d1, 8, 15), 60 mg C2 d1, then 30 mg q21d; stop after 8 cycles if CR , else up to 17 Tafasitamab + R² Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg d1, 8, 15, 22 C1–3, then d1+15 C4–12 (q28d) + R² Zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab Zanubrutinib 160 mg BID continuous + obinutuzumab 1000 mg (C1 d1, 8, 15; C2–6 d1; then q8wk) ISRT 24 Gy / 12 fx curative intent · 2 × 2 Gy palliative mg/m² unless stated. Premedicate every anti-CD20 infusion (acetaminophen, antihistamine, steroid for the first). Toxicity and monitoring HBV: screen HBsAg + anti-HBc before any anti-CD20; entecavir prophylaxis if either positive, continued for ≥12 months after the last dose Bendamustine → profound, prolonged CD4 lymphopenia (months to years). Give PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir/valacyclovir) ; watch for CMV. Worse when followed by maintenance anti-CD20 — think twice about stacking them. Also hampers later CAR-T manufacturing Obinutuzumab: infusion reactions ~60% (mostly C1 d1) — premedicate, slow first infusion, hold antihypertensives. More neutropenia and infection than rituximab Bispecifics: CRS clusters around the first full dose of step-up. Corticosteroid premedication, hydration, close monitoring after the first full dose; tocilizumab for grade ≥2. ICANS uncommon. Continuous B-cell depletion → hypogammaglobulinemia and serious infections : IVIG if recurrent, PJP + antiviral prophylaxis, vaccinate beforehand R²: VTE — aspirin 81 mg if no other risk, LMWH/DOAC if high risk; rash (often grade 1–2; antihistamine, hold/reduce), neutropenia (50% grade 3–4 in AUGMENT), tumor flare, diarrhea. Dose by renal function CAR-T: CRS and ICANS (REMS removed June 2025: stay near the center and no driving for 2 weeks ), prolonged cytopenias, hypogammaglobulinemia; T-cell malignancy boxed warning Zanubrutinib: bleeding (hold 3–7 days peri-procedure), AF, hypertension, neutropenia Key trials StiL NHL1 BR > R-CHOP for PFS; no OS difference GALLIUM Obinutuzumab: PFS gain, no OS gain RELEVANCE R² = R-chemo (negative superiority) PRIMA Maintenance: PFS doubled, no OS FoRT 24 Gy beats 4 Gy for local control AUGMENT R² vs R at relapse: PFS HR 0.46 EPCORE FL-1 Epcoritamab + R²: PFS HR 0.21 inMIND Tafasitamab + R²: PFS HR 0.43

docs.title: Hodgkin lymphoma
docs.subtitle: Classic HL vs NLPHL · highly curable, and managed by interim PET — give enough therapy to cure while withdrawing bleomycin and radiation from those who don't need them · N-AVD (US) and BrECADD (Europe) are the advanced-stage standards
headings: Classic HL vs NLPHL — two different diseases
Treatment pathway — interim PET drives it
docs.text: Hodgkin lymphoma Classic HL vs NLPHL · highly curable, and managed by interim PET — give enough therapy to cure while withdrawing bleomycin and radiation from those who don't need them · N-AVD (US) and BrECADD (Europe) are the advanced-stage standards Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Hodgkin (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. Classic HL vs NLPHL — two different diseases Classic HL NLPHL Tumor cell Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg (HRS) — binucleate, owl-eye nucleoli; a tiny minority of cells in an inflammatory background LP (“popcorn”) cells in nodules of follicular dendritic cells, ringed by PD-1+ T-cell rosettes Phenotype CD30+ CD15+, CD45−, PAX5 dim , MUM1+. CD20 negative or weak/patchy; OCT2/BOB1 lost. EBV (LMP1) + in a subset CD20+ CD45+ , PAX5+, BCL6+, OCT2/BOB1 +. CD30− CD15− Biology 9p24.1 gain → PD-L1/PD-L2 + JAK-STAT, NF-κB — the reason PD-1 blockade works Intact germinal-center B-cell program — really a B-cell lymphoma Subtypes Nodular sclerosis (young, mediastinal) · mixed cellularity (older, EBV+, HIV) · lymphocyte-rich · lymphocyte-depleted ICC 2022: nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma ; WHO-HAEM5 keeps NLPHL. Variant patterns C–F (THRLBCL-like) do worse Targets Brentuximab (CD30), anti-PD-1 Rituximab (CD20) — no CD30 target Lymphocyte-rich cHL mimics NLPHL on morphology — the immunophenotype separates them. Gray-zone lymphoma sits between cHL and PMBL. Workup History: B symptoms, pruritus, alcohol-induced nodal pain ; exam of nodal regions, liver, spleen; performance status Excisional biopsy preferred , core acceptable, never FNA (HRS cells are sparse and architecture matters) IHC — the critical panel: CD30, CD15, PAX5, CD20, CD3 Labs: CBC/diff, CMP ( albumin ), ESR , LDH, HIV , HBV and HCV, pregnancy test PET-CT stages; no routine marrow biopsy — only for focal bone lesions or unexplained cytopenias Echo/MUGA before anthracycline · PFTs with DLCO before bleomycin · before PD-1: TSH, ACTH/cortisol, troponin Fertility: low risk with A(B)VD or N-AVD, so preservation is not mandated; bank before eBEACOPP/BrECADD or salvage Deauville 5-point score 1 · 2 No uptake · uptake ≤ mediastinum 3 Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response 4 · 5 Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure Response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited. (The handbook itself specifies only PET/CT at completion, plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis.) Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor I One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring) II ≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II III Regions on both sides of the diaphragm IV Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site A / B B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats S · X · E S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm , or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum. Early-stage (CS I–II) unfavorable factors Factor EORTC GHSG NCCN Mediastinal mass >0.35 MTR >⅓ CXR >⅓ or >10 cm Age ≥50 yes — — ESR ≥50 (≥30 if B) ≥50 (≥30 if B) ≥50 or any B Extranodal disease — yes — Nodal areas ≥4 (EORTC areas) ≥3 (GHSG areas) >3 Favorable = none present. GHSG areas lump infraclavicular with ipsilateral cervical and both hila with the mediastinum. Stage IIB with bulk or extranodal disease is treated as advanced by GHSG (eligible for HD21). The handbook table lists ≥3 / ≥2 areas — the trial definitions are ≥4 (EORTC) and ≥3 (GHSG). IPS — advanced stage (freedom from progression) Factors Hasenclever 1998 Moccia 2012 0 · 1 84% · 77% 88% · 84% 2 · 3 67% · 60% 80% · 74% 4 · ≥5 51% · 42% 67% · 62% One point each: albumin <4 · Hgb <10.5 · male · stage IV · age ≥45 · WBC ≥15,000 · lymphocytes <600 or <8% . Moccia is the ABVD-era revision. Modern regimens flatten the curve — N-AVD 3-yr PFS was 87% even at IPS 4–7. Treatment pathway — interim PET drives it Early favorable (CS I–II, no risk factors) ABVD ×2 → interim PET (PET2) DS 1–2: + 20 Gy ISRT (HD16, GHSG-favorable) or ABVD ×1 + 30 Gy (H10F, RAPID) no RT: ABVD ×2 more (H10F, CALGB 50604) DS 3: ABVD ×2 + RT, or AVD ×4 (RATHL) DS 4–5: escalate — eBEACOPP ×2 + ISRT (H10) Early unfavorable ABVD ×2 → PET2 DS 1–2: ABVD ×2 more + 30 Gy ISRT (H10U) no RT: ABVD ×2 → AVD ×4 if DS 1–3 (RATHL) DS 4–5: eBEACOPP ×2 + 30 Gy alt: nivo-AVD ×4 (NIVAHL) or BV-AVD (BREACH) + RT GHSG 2+2: omit RT if PET4-negative (HD17) Advanced (III–IV, GHSG IIB-high-risk) Pick one backbone N-AVD ×6 (S1826) — US standard, age ≥12 BrECADD ×4–6 (HD21) — age ≤60; 4 if PET2 neg BV-AVD ×6 (ECHELON-1) — OS win vs ABVD ABVD ×2 → PET2 → AVD ×4 (RATHL) >60 & fit: N-AVD; unfit: BV-DTIC, BV-nivo EOT PET: RT only to avid residual (0.7% in S1826) Relapsed / refractory Salvage → PET-CR → HDT/ASCT PD-1 combo first if checkpoint-naive: pembro-GVD · pembro-ICE · nivo-ICE · BV-nivo high risk → BV ×16 consolidation (AETHERA) Relapse after ASCT / ineligible pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-204) > BV; nivolumab allo-HCT for chemosensitive, fit patients Early stage — the radiation-omission trials Trial Design Result HD16 GHSG fav ABVD ×2; PET2-neg randomized ± 20 Gy IFRT 5-yr PFS 93.4 vs 86.1% without RT — non-inferiority failed ; OS 98% both H10 EORTC I–II PET2-neg: ABVD alone vs ABVD + INRT. PET2-pos: eBEACOPP ×2 + INRT vs ABVD + INRT Fav PET-neg 5-yr PFS 99.0 vs 87.1% — NI failed in both strata. PET-pos escalation 90.6 vs 77.4% (HR 0.42) — no longer significant at 10 yr RAPID IA–IIA non-bulky ABVD ×3; PET-neg (DS 1–2): IFRT vs nothing 3-yr PFS 94.6 vs 90.8% — NI failed; no HL deaths without RT CALGB 50604 non-bulky I–II ABVD ×2 → PET2-neg: ABVD ×2 more, no RT ; PET2-pos: eBEACOPP ×2 + IFRT 3-yr PFS 91% PET-neg vs 66% PET-pos (HR 3.84). Single-arm — the US chemo-only benchmark HD17 GHSG unfav eBEACOPP ×2 + ABVD ×2; PET4-neg: 30 Gy vs none 5-yr PFS 97.3 vs 95.1% , difference 2.2% — NI MET (8% margin). The one success — after intensive 2+2 BREACH unfav, ph 2 BV-AVD vs ABVD ×4, then 30 Gy PET2-neg 82.3 vs 75.4% (primary met); 2-yr PFS 97.3 vs 92.6% NIVAHL unfav, ph 2 Nivo-AVD ×4 (concomitant or sequential) + 30 Gy PFS 100% vs 98% at median 41 mo (n=109) The trade: dropping RT after a negative PET costs ~4–7 points of PFS with no OS difference in any trial . Lean to omission in young women with breast in the field, or when heart/coronaries are in the field; lean to RT for bulk, DS 3, or slow response. Bleomycin — when to drop it Pulmonary toxicity in 18% , fatal in a quarter of those; 5-yr OS 63 vs 90% with vs without it (Mayo, n=141). Risk: age ≥40, ABVD, G-CSF — omitting bleomycin did not reduce CR, PFS or OS RATHL: PET2-neg → AVD ×4 is non-inferior (3-yr PFS 84.4 vs 85.7%; confirmed at 7.3 yr) with less lung toxicity. PET2-pos → escalation, 3-yr PFS only 67.5% Never with brentuximab (contraindicated — pulmonary toxicity), and don't start it at all over 60 — ECHELON-1 ≥60: ABVD lung toxicity 13%, 3 deaths Stop permanently for cough/dyspnea + falling DLCO; avoid G-CSF with ABVD Advanced stage — choosing the backbone Regimen Evidence Choose it / cost N-AVD ×6 S1826 vs BV-AVD (n=994, age ≥12): 3-yr PFS 91 vs 82% , HR 0.48. 3-yr OS 98 vs 97%, not significantly different — no OS benefit yet . FDA approved 20 Mar 2026 US default , incl. adolescents and >60. Neuropathy 28 vs 54%; PROs favor it; G-CSF optional; RT in 0.7%. Benefit held in EBV+ (HR 0.30) and non-NS histology. Comparator was BV-AVD, not ABVD BrECADD ×4–6 HD21 vs eBEACOPP (n=1500, ≤60): treatment-related morbidity 42 vs 59%; 4-yr PFS 94.3 vs 90.9% (HR 0.66); OS 98.6 vs 98.2% European standard (EC-approved 2025; not FDA-labeled). Only 4 cycles if PET2-neg. Still intensive: G-CSF, PJP, febrile neutropenia. Gonadal recovery at 4 yr (men) 86 vs 40% vs eBEACOPP BV-AVD ×6 ECHELON-1 vs ABVD (n=1334): 5-yr PFS 82.2 vs 75.3% (HR 0.68); 6-yr OS 93.9 vs 89.4%, HR 0.59 — the only OS win over ABVD Now beaten by N-AVD head-to-head. Mandatory G-CSF, neuropathy. No PFS benefit at ≥60 (5-yr 67 vs 62%) with grade 3–4 neuropathy 18%, FN 37% eBEACOPP Highest PFS of the chemo-only era (HD9/HD15/HD18) Legacy — infertility (men 40% gonadal recovery at 4 yr), t-MDS/AML 1.7% after ≥4 cycles. Replaced by BrECADD ABVD → AVD RATHL PET-adapted (above); 5-yr ABVD ceiling ~75% PFS in ECHELON-1 Where novel agents are unavailable; PET2-pos patients do poorly No head-to-head N-AVD vs BrECADD. Cross-trial comparison misleads: S1826 enrolled adolescents and >60 with investigator-read response; HD21 was ≤60 and included GHSG stage IIB with risk factors. Older adults (>60) N-AVD if anthracycline-fit: S1826 ≥60 (n=99) 2-yr PFS 89 vs 64% , OS 96 vs 85% (subgroup); non-relapse mortality 6 vs 16% ; 6 cycles without dose reduction in 69 vs 26% Avoid bleomycin and be wary of BV-AVD (neuropathy, FN, no PFS gain at ≥60) Sequential BV ×2 → AVD ×6 → BV ×4 (phase 2, n=48): 2-yr PFS 84%, but 45% if CIRS-G ≥10 and 25% with IADL loss — do a geriatric assessment BrECADD at 61–75 (HD21 cohort, n=83): 2-yr PFS 91.5% but FN 55% — only for the very fit Anthracycline-unfit: BV + dacarbazine (CR 62%, mPFS 17.9 mo) · BV + nivolumab (CMR 48%, missed its target ) · BV + bendamustine stopped for toxicity Relapsed / refractory Rebiopsy suspected relapse. Transplant-eligible: salvage → HDT/ASCT , which cures roughly half; PET-negative going into ASCT is the key predictor PD-1 combinations first if checkpoint-naive (all single-arm phase 2): pembro-GVD CR 95% (n=39) · pembro-ICE CMR 86.5%, 2-yr PFS 87% · nivo → nivo-ICE 2-yr PFS 94% if bridged to ASCT · BV-nivo CR 67%, 3-yr PFS 91% with ASCT BV consolidation ×16 after ASCT for high risk (primary refractory, relapse <12 mo, extranodal at relapse): AETHERA 5-yr PFS 59 vs 41% (HR 0.52), no OS benefit ; less clear after BV- or PD-1-based salvage After ASCT or ineligible: pembrolizumab beat BV (KEYNOTE-204 mPFS 13.2 vs 8.3 mo , HR 0.65; OS not reported). Single agents respond often but rarely completely: nivolumab ORR 69% (CheckMate 205), pembrolizumab ORR 69%, CR 22% (KEYNOTE-087); BV ORR 75%, CR 34%. Nivolumab R/R cHL converted to regular approval Mar 2026 Allo-HCT for fit patients with chemosensitive relapse after ASCT. Prior PD-1 raises early severe GVHD and non-infectious febrile syndromes — plan with the transplant team NLPHL (NLPBL) Indolent with late relapses ; transformation 14% at median 8.1 yr (7% at 10 yr, 30% at 20 yr; splenic involvement predicts) — biopsy any progression IA–IIA contiguous, non-bulky: ISRT 30–36 Gy , or observe after complete excision I–IIA non-contiguous (GHSG-favorable): R-ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy · I–IIB or bulky: R-ABVD or R-CHOP ×4 + 30 Gy III–IV: R-CHOP ×6 ± ISRT; rituximab alone or observation if asymptomatic, low burden, no variant pattern. Transformed/THRLBCL-like → treat as DLBCL Survivorship and late effects No routine surveillance PET after CR — history, exam, CBC/CMP/ESR at visits Breast cancer after chest RT: cumulative incidence 35% by age 50 in childhood-HL survivors, mantle SIR 24. Screen annually from 8–10 yr after RT or age 40, whichever first; add breast MRI if irradiated at age 10–30 (NCCN) Second cancers: SIR 4.6, 40-yr cumulative incidence 48.5% (Dutch cohort treated 1965–2000); axilla-sparing fields cut breast risk (HR 0.37). Lung (smokers), thyroid, GI, sarcoma in field t-MDS/AML: 0.9% overall, 1.7% after ≥4 eBEACOPP (GHSG, n=11,952); median OS 7.2 mo Cardiac: anthracycline + mediastinal RT → CAD, valve disease, cardiomyopathy, pericardial disease — aggressive risk-factor control; consider stress test/echo at ~10-yr intervals; carotid US after neck RT Thyroid: annual TSH after neck/mediastinal RT (or PD-1). Fertility: low risk with A(B)VD/N-AVD, high with eBEACOPP Frontline dosing Regimen Dosing (mg/m² unless stated) Cycle ABVD Doxorubicin 25 · bleomycin 10 units/m² · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15. No G-CSF ; don't delay for afebrile neutropenia q28d AVD As ABVD without bleomycin (RATHL cycles 3–6) q28d N-AVD Nivolumab 240 mg (3 mg/kg, max 240, if <18) + AVD — all d1 + d15 ×6. G-CSF optional q28d BV-AVD Brentuximab 1.2 mg/kg (max 120 mg) + AVD — d1 + d15 ×6. Primary G-CSF mandatory (filgrastim d5–8 + d19–22) q28d BrECADD Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180 mg) d0 · etoposide 150 d1–3 · cyclophosphamide 1250 d1 · doxorubicin 40 d1 · dacarbazine 250 d2–3 · dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4. No vincristine, no bleomycin . G-CSF, PJP + antiviral prophylaxis; start dose level 4, de-escalate for toxicity q21d ×4–6 eBEACOPP Etoposide 200 d1–3 · doxorubicin 35 d1 · cyclophosphamide 1250 d1 · bleomycin 10 d8 · vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d8 · procarbazine 100 d1–7 · prednisone 40 d1–14. G-CSF + PJP q21d Cumulative doxorubicin: ABVD/N-AVD/BV-AVD ×6 = 300 mg/m²; BrECADD ×6 = 240; eBEACOPP ×6 = 210. The handbook's BrECADD table lists vincristine and BV in mg/m² — both are errors (verified against Eichenauer, Lancet Oncol 2017). Toxicity and monitoring BV neuropathy (sensory, cumulative; AETHERA 56 vs 16%). Monotherapy: grade 2–3 → hold to ≤1, resume 1.2 mg/kg; grade 4 stop. With AVD: grade 2 → 0.9 mg/kg; grade 3 hold to ≤2 then 0.9. Boxed PML; pancreatitis Bleomycin: baseline PFTs/DLCO, repeat for symptoms; no G-CSF; warn anesthesia about high FiO₂ PJP (TMP-SMX) + acyclovir with BrECADD, eBEACOPP and every BV-containing regimen Checkpoint irAEs: TSH at baseline and every cycle — thyroid dysfunction 7% (adolescent N-AVD), hypothyroidism 15% (NIVAHL); pneumonitis more with pembrolizumab than BV (KEYNOTE-204); adrenal, hepatitis, colitis → prednisone 1–2 mg/kg Anthracycline: echo at baseline; dacarbazine highly emetogenic; vinblastine vesicant — constipation, neuropathy Salvage and post-ASCT dosing Regimen Dosing Cycle Pembro-GVD Pembrolizumab 200 mg d1; gemcitabine 1000 (800 post-HSCT) + vinorelbine 15 + liposomal doxorubicin 10 — d1 + d8 q21d ×2–4 ICE ± PD-1 Ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV d2 · carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2 · etoposide 100 d1–3. + pembrolizumab 200 mg d1, or nivolumab 240 mg d1 (after nivo alone q2w up to 6 doses) q21d ×2 → collect BV + nivolumab Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180) d1; nivolumab 240 mg C1D8, then d1 of C2–4. PJP + antiviral q21d ×4 BV ± bendamustine Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg d1 ± bendamustine 90 d1–2 (salvage only — toxic in older frontline) q21d ×6 BV consolidation 1.8 mg/kg (max 180), start 30–45 days post-ASCT q21d ×16 PD-1 alone Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w or 400 mg q6w · nivolumab 240 mg q2w or 480 mg q4w until PD ICE: filgrastim from d8 or pegfilgrastim; hydration with bicarbonate. GVD d8: cut gemcitabine/vinorelbine 25% for ANC 500–1199 or plt 75–99K. Special populations and emerging tools Adolescents 12–17 (24% of S1826): N-AVD 3-yr PFS 93 vs 82% (HR 0.37), residual-site RT in 3 patients — one harmonized pediatric/adult protocol HIV-associated cHL: full-dose curative therapy on ART. S1826 enrolled CD4 ≥200 with undetectable viral load (n=16): 2-yr PFS 77.9% N-AVD vs 75.0% BV-AVD — too few to compare EBV+ and non-nodular-sclerosis histology historically do worse; N-AVD largely erased the gap (3-yr PFS EBV+ 91 vs 70% , HR 0.30; non-NS 86 vs 63%) ctDNA MRD after 2 cycles (HD21 case-cohort): MRD-positive 4-yr PFS 36.7 vs 82.2% (HR 5.3); adds to PET2 but is still investigational PET pitfalls: thymic rebound, brown fat, G-CSF marrow uptake, and sarcoid-like reactions on PD-1 — biopsy a DS 4–5 residual before calling refractory disease Key trials Trial Setting / design Result HD16 2019 GHSG early fav; ABVD ×2, PET2-neg ± 20 Gy 5-yr PFS 93.4 vs 86.1% — NI failed ; OS equal H10 2017 EORTC I–II; PET2-adapted RT omission / escalation NI failed; PET-pos escalation HR 0.42, lost at 10 yr RAPID 2015 IA–IIA; ABVD ×3, PET-neg ± IFRT 3-yr PFS 94.6 vs 90.8% — NI failed HD17 2021 GHSG unfav; 2+2, PET4-neg ± 30 Gy 5-yr PFS 97.3 vs 95.1% — NI met CALGB 50604 2018 Non-bulky I–II; ABVD ×4 no RT if PET2-neg 3-yr PFS 91% (single-arm) RATHL 2016 Advanced; PET2-neg ABVD vs AVD 3-yr PFS 85.7 vs 84.4% — NI (confirmed 7.3 yr) ECHELON-1 2018 III–IV; BV-AVD vs ABVD (n=1334) mPFS HR 0.77; 6-yr OS 93.9 vs 89.4% , HR 0.59 SWOG S1826 2024 III–IV, age ≥12; N-AVD vs BV-AVD (n=994) 3-yr PFS 91 vs 82% , HR 0.48; OS p=0.09 GHSG HD21 2024 Advanced, ≤60; BrECADD vs eBEACOPP (n=1500) Morbidity 42 vs 59%; 4-yr PFS 94.3 vs 90.9% AETHERA 2015 High-risk post-ASCT; BV ×16 vs placebo mPFS 42.9 vs 24.1 mo; 5-yr 59 vs 41%; no OS gain KEYNOTE-204 2021 R/R post-/non-ASCT; pembrolizumab vs BV mPFS 13.2 vs 8.3 mo , HR 0.65 KEYNOTE-087 · CheckMate 205 Single-arm PD-1 after ASCT and/or BV ORR 69% both; CR 22% (KN-087) BREACH · NIVAHL 2023 Early unfav, randomized phase 2 BV-AVD PET2-neg 82 vs 75%; nivo-AVD PFS ~100% Pembro-GVD · BV-nivo Single-arm first salvage CR 95% / 67%; high post-ASCT PFS Evens BV→AVD→BV 2018 Age ≥60, phase 2 (n=48) 2-yr PFS 84%; poor if CIRS-G ≥10

docs.title: Mantle cell lymphoma
docs.subtitle: CD5+, cyclin D1+ B-cell lymphoma driven by t(11;14) · a spectrum from observable leukemic non-nodal disease to blastoid disease · TP53 status, Ki-67 and fitness — not stage — choose the therapy; BTK inhibitors have displaced routine ASCT
docs.text: Mantle cell lymphoma CD5+, cyclin D1+ B-cell lymphoma driven by t(11;14) · a spectrum from observable leukemic non-nodal disease to blastoid disease · TP53 status, Ki-67 and fitness — not stage — choose the therapy ; BTK inhibitors have displaced routine ASCT Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — mantle cell (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J, Gupta NK) · NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas v4.2026 · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. Diagnosis Hallmark: t(11;14)(q13;q32), IGH::CCND1 → cyclin D1 overexpression — show it by cyclin D1 IHC or FISH Phenotype: CD5+, CD20 bright, CD23−, CD10−, cyclin D1+, SOX11+. CD23 negativity and cyclin D1 separate it from CLL, which is CD5+ CD23+ Cyclin D1-negative MCL is real: SOX11+, with a CCND2 rearrangement in ~55% . Diagnose it on SOX11 + morphology; treat as MCL Salaverria, Blood 2013 SOX11 does double duty — rescues the cyclin D1-negative diagnosis, and its absence flags the indolent leukemic non-nodal form The spectrum — WHO-HAEM5 / ICC 2022 Form Features → behavior Classic (nodal) SOX11+, IGHV mostly unmutated; nodes + marrow, spleen, GI tract (lymphomatous polyposis). Chronic relapsing course Leukemic non-nodal SOX11−, IGHV-mutated , blood + marrow ± spleen, no significant adenopathy. Indolent : 5-yr OS 78% vs 36% for SOX11+ Fernàndez 2010 — observe unless it acquires TP53 or goes nodal Blastoid / pleomorphic High Ki-67, TP53 enriched, CNS-prone. Treat as high risk ; blastoid adds nothing to prognosis once Ki-67 is known In situ mantle cell neoplasia Cyclin D1+ cells confined to mantle zones of a reactive node — usually incidental; stage and observe Workup PET/CT , marrow biopsy with flow and t(11;14) FISH, CBC with smear (leukemic phase), LDH, β2-microglobulin, HBV serology before anti-CD20 TP53 by NGS (+ del(17p) FISH) and Ki-67 at diagnosis in every patient — they pick the regimen, not the stage EGD + colonoscopy for apparent stage I–II (to confirm limited disease) and when GI symptoms LP / brain MRI if blastoid or neurologic symptoms. Echo before anthracycline Pearls CD5+ CD23− small B cells = send cyclin D1. If cyclin D1− but SOX11+, it is still MCL Send TP53 before choosing. A TP53-mutant patient gets little from cytarabine + ASCT Rituximab maintenance is standard in MCL after both intensive and BR induction — unlike follicular, its OS benefit (LyMa) was real at 4 yr, though attenuated at 7 No BTKi-added frontline trial in older patients has shown OS gain (SHINE, ECHO) — PFS gain costs toxicity Brexu-cel is the most active post-BTKi therapy but the most neurotoxic; liso-cel trades a little efficacy for much less CRS/ICANS MIPI — add the points Pts Age ECOG LDH / ULN WBC ×10 9 /L 0 <50 0–1 <0.67 <6.7 1 50–59 — 0.67–0.99 6.7–9.99 2 60–69 2–4 1.00–1.49 10–14.99 3 ≥70 — ≥1.50 ≥15 Low 0–3 (44%; median OS not reached) · intermediate 4–5 (35%; 51 mo) · high 6–11 (21%; 29 mo). Hoster, Blood 2008 — pre-BTKi survival; use it to stratify, not to counsel. Biology that overrides the score TP53 mutation is the dominant adverse factor. 11% in Nordic MCL2/3 Median OS 1.8 vs 12.7 yr , OS HR 6.2; half relapsed within a year of cytarabine induction + ASCT Eskelund, Blood 2017 Ki-67 ≥30% is the validated cutoff. MIPI-c = MIPI group + Ki-67 → 4 groups, 5-yr OS 85% / 72% / 43% / 17% Hoster, JCO 2016 Blastoid/pleomorphic cytology, complex karyotype, del(17p) travel with TP53 and high Ki-67 Watch and wait is legitimate for selected patients — leukemic non-nodal SOX11− disease, or asymptomatic classic MCL with low burden, low Ki-67 and wild-type TP53. In a Weill Cornell series 32% were observed ; median time to treatment 12 mo (range 4–128) , with no survival penalty (a selected cohort) Martin, JCO 2009 . ASCT in first remission is no longer default. Its PFS benefit predates BTKi and maintenance. TRIANGLE : adding ASCT to ibrutinib gave no FFS gain and more toxicity. EA4151 : in MRD-negative CR, ASCT + rituximab = rituximab alone (abstract only). Chemo-immunotherapy — infection and supportive care Bendamustine is deeply immunosuppressive — prolonged CD4 lymphopenia: PJP (TMP-SMX) + VZV (acyclovir) prophylaxis ; ECHO grade 5 COVID-19 9.4% vs 6.7% . Rash with allopurinol Rituximab maintenance → hypogammaglobulinemia and infection; check IgG, replace if recurrent infections. HBV prophylaxis if core Ab+ Lenalidomide: aspirin or anticoagulant VTE prophylaxis, renal dose adjustment Treatment pathway Frontline — by biology, then fitness Indolent / low burden, TP53 wild-type leukemic non-nodal, or low Ki-67 asymptomatic observe — treat for symptoms or progression Fit, ≤65–70, TP53 wild-type TRIANGLE : R-CHOP + ibrutinib alternating with R-DHAP (or R-DHAOx) ×6 → ibrutinib ×2 yr ± rituximab q8wk — ASCT can be omitted older standard: Nordic or R-DHAP → ASCT → R q2mo ×3 yr Older or unfit, TP53 wild-type acalabrutinib + BR (ECHO) → R maintenance BR → R maintenance · VR-CAP · RBAC500 (fit) chemo-free: BTKi + rituximab (ENRICH) TP53-mutated avoid chemo-heavy regimens and ASCT clinical trial , or BTKi-based: BOVen (zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab + venetoclax) Relapsed / refractory BTKi-naive covalent BTKi : acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib or ibrutinib + venetoclax (SYMPATICO, off-label) After a covalent BTKi CAR-T : brexu-cel or liso-cel (fit) pirtobrutinib — bridge, or if CAR-T not possible sonrotoclax · R² · glofitamab on trial After CAR-T allo-HCT if fit · trials (bispecifics, BTK degraders) Frontline evidence Trial Result How to read it TRIANGLE ≤65, n=870 Ibrutinib + ASCT (A+I) beat ASCT alone (A): 3-yr FFS 88% vs 72% , HR 0.52. At 4.5 yr A+I not better than ibrutinib without ASCT (I) : 4-yr FFS 82% vs 81%. 4-yr OS 88–90% vs 81% for either ibrutinib arm vs A (HR 0.57–0.59) Primary endpoint is FFS . Maintenance grade 3–5 heme toxicity 54% A+I vs 28% I . Uses ibrutinib, which has no US MCL label ; applying it to acalabrutinib/zanubrutinib is extrapolation TRIANGLE R-maint secondary Rituximab maintenance on top of ibrutinib: 4-yr PFS 85% vs 73% (arm I) Non-randomized; grade 3–5 infections 34% vs 11% LyMa <66, n=240 rand. R-DHAP → ASCT → rituximab q2mo ×3 yr vs observation: 4-yr EFS 79% vs 61% , OS 89% vs 80% (HR 0.50) The OS benefit is the one usually quoted — at 7 yr it is no longer significant (83% vs 72%, HR 0.63, p=0.088); PFS gain holds (HR 0.36) EA4151 MRD− CR1, n=516 rand. ASCT + R maintenance vs R maintenance alone : 3-yr OS 82.1% vs 82.7% (HR 1.11); PFS 76.6% vs 77.4%. Crossed futility ASH 2024 abstract, not peer-reviewed. Only 7% had BTKi induction; 25% assigned to ASCT declined it Nordic MCL2 single-arm Maxi-R-CHOP / R-high-dose cytarabine → ASCT: median PFS 8.5 yr , OS 12.7 yr No plateau — not curative SHINE ≥65, n=523 Ibrutinib + BR → R maintenance: median PFS 80.6 vs 52.9 mo (HR 0.75) No OS benefit — excess adverse-event deaths; AF 13.9% vs 6.5% ECHO ≥65, n=598 Acalabrutinib + BR: median PFS 66.4 vs 49.6 mo (HR 0.73). Regular FDA approval, Jan 2025 No OS difference (HR 0.86). AF 6.7% vs 4.4%; grade 5 COVID-19 9.4% vs 6.7% ENRICH ≥60, n=397 Ibrutinib + rituximab vs R-chemo: PFS HR 0.69 . vs R-CHOP HR 0.37; vs BR HR 0.91 (NS) Chemo-free BTKi-R matches BR and beats R-CHOP VR-CAP n=487 Bortezomib for vincristine in R-CHOP: PFS 24.7 vs 14.4 mo ; median OS 90.7 vs 55.7 mo (HR 0.66) The one older-patient trial with an OS gain — but vs R-CHOP, a weak comparator RBAC500 single-arm, n=57 R + bendamustine + cytarabine 500: CR 91% , median age 71 Missed its safety boundary: 72% dose-reduced , grade 3–4 cytopenias in ~half of cycles BOVen TP53-mut, n=25 Zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab + venetoclax: ORR 96% , CR 88% , 2-yr PFS 72% Single-arm phase 2 — the best TP53 data, not yet randomized Relapsed / refractory — agents and status (Sept 2026) Agent Data FDA status Acalabrutinib ACE-LY-004 (n=124): ORR 81% , CR 40% Accelerated 2017 → regular Jan 2025 Zanubrutinib BGB-3111-206 (n=86): ORR 84% , CR 69%, median PFS 22.1 mo Accelerated (Nov 2019), still Ibrutinib Pivotal single-arm data; SHINE did not confirm US MCL indication withdrawn (effective Dec 2023) Ibrutinib + venetoclax SYMPATICO (n=267): median PFS 31.9 vs 22.1 mo , HR 0.65 vs ibrutinib Not approved as a combination in MCL Pirtobrutinib non-covalent BRUIN, after covalent BTKi (n=90): ORR 58% , CR 20%, median DOR 21.6 mo; grade ≥3 AF 1.2% Accelerated (Jan 2023; ≥2 lines incl. BTKi). Confirmatory BRUIN MCL-321 not yet reported Brexu-cel CD19 CAR-T ZUMA-2: ORR 93% , CR 67% ; 3-yr median PFS 25.8 mo , OS 46.6 mo. Grade ≥3 CRS 15%, neurologic events 31% Accelerated 2020 → regular Apr 2026 (added BTKi-naive cohort: CR 79%) Liso-cel CD19 CAR-T TRANSCEND MCL (n=83): ORR 83% , CR 72% , median PFS 15.3 mo. Grade 3–4 CRS 1% , neurologic 9% Approved May 2024 (≥2 lines incl. BTKi) Sonrotoclax BCL2 Phase 2 (n=103), post-BTKi: ORR 52% , CR 16%, median PFS 6.5 mo ; TP53-mut ORR 59%; TLS 7% Accelerated, 13 May 2026 (≥2 lines incl. BTKi) Glofitamab CD20×CD3 Phase 1/2 (n=60): ORR 85% , CR 78% (71% after BTKi); CRS 70% Not approved in MCL (US or EU) — phase 3 GLOBRYTE pending Lenalidomide ± R SPRINT: PFS 8.7 vs 5.2 mo vs investigator choice (HR 0.61); EMERGE post-bortezomib ORR 28% Approved 2013 (after bortezomib) Allo-HCT Only curative-intent option after CAR-T failure — Relapse after frontline BTKi (TRIANGLE, ECHO) is now common: those patients are BTKi-exposed at first relapse, so the post-BTKi column is effectively second line. Response to a covalent BTKi at relapse after BTKi-containing induction is not established. Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing TRIANGLE (A+I / I) R-CHOP + ibrutinib : rituximab 375, cyclophosphamide 750, doxorubicin 50, vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d1, prednisone 100 mg d1–5 + ibrutinib 560 mg d1–19 , alternating with R-DHAP (rituximab 375, dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4, cytarabine 2 g/m² q12h ×2 d2 , cisplatin 100 CIV d1) or R-DHAOx (oxaliplatin 130) — q21d ×6. Then ibrutinib 560 mg daily ×2 yr ± rituximab LyMa R-DHAP q21d ×4 → ASCT → rituximab 375 q2 months ×3 yr BR ± BTKi Rituximab 375 d1 + bendamustine 90 d1–2 , q28d ×6 → rituximab 375 q8wk ×2 yr. ECHO adds acalabrutinib 100 mg BID until progression VR-CAP Rituximab 375, cyclophosphamide 750, doxorubicin 50 d1; bortezomib 1.3 d1, 4, 8, 11 ; prednisone 100 d1–5 — q21d ×6 RBAC500 Rituximab 375 d1, bendamustine 70 d2–3 , cytarabine 500 d2–4 — q28d, up to 6 R² Lenalidomide 20 mg d1–21 q28d + rituximab 375 weekly ×4 (cycle 1), then per protocol. VTE prophylaxis BTK inhibitors Ibrutinib 560 mg daily · acalabrutinib 100 mg BID · zanubrutinib 160 mg BID or 320 mg daily · pirtobrutinib 200 mg daily — continuous CAR-T Brexu-cel : flu 30 + cy 500 mg/m² d−5 to −3, then 2×10 6 CAR-T cells/kg (max 2×10 8 ). Liso-cel : flu 30 + cy 300 mg/m² ×3 d, then 90–110×10 6 CAR+ T cells. Avoid bendamustine shortly before apheresis mg/m² unless stated. Cytarabine: prednisolone 1% eye drops from 12 h before to 48 h after; reduce to 1 g/m² if age >60 ; hold for rising creatinine (cerebellar toxicity). Targeted and cellular therapy — toxicity BTKi class: atrial fibrillation, bleeding, hypertension, infection , plus arthralgia, diarrhea, rash. Hold 3–7 days around procedures ; avoid warfarin; watch CYP3A interactions Second-generation agents cut AF by about half: ELEVATE-RR (CLL) 9.4% acalabrutinib vs 16.0% ibrutinib ; ALPINE fewer cardiac events with zanubrutinib; in MCL, ECHO 6.7% vs SHINE 13.9% (cross-trial). Acalabrutinib: early headache. Zanubrutinib: neutropenia. Pirtobrutinib: grade ≥3 AF ~1% CAR-T: CRS → tocilizumab ± dexamethasone; ICANS → dexamethasone (tocilizumab only if CRS coexists), levetiracetam. Brexu-cel is the more neurotoxic (grade ≥3 neuro 31% vs 9% liso-cel). Late: cytopenias, hypogammaglobulinemia, boxed warning for T-cell malignancy Venetoclax / sonrotoclax: TLS — MCL can be bulky and leukemic; ramp-up, hydration, allopurinol, lab checks at each step

docs.title: Marginal zone lymphoma
docs.subtitle: The antigen-driven lymphoma — extranodal (MALT), splenic and nodal MZL share a CD5−/CD10− phenotype but not a treatment. Find and treat the driver first (H. pylori, HCV, C. psittaci), irradiate localized disease with curative intent, and reserve systemic therapy for disseminated or symptomatic disease
docs.text: Marginal zone lymphoma The antigen-driven lymphoma — extranodal (MALT), splenic and nodal MZL share a CD5−/CD10− phenotype but not a treatment. Find and treat the driver first (H. pylori, HCV, C. psittaci), irradiate localized disease with curative intent, and reserve systemic therapy for disseminated or symptomatic disease Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (NCCN; WHO-HAEM5; EGILS) verified against PubMed, September 2026. Three (now four) entities — WHO-HAEM5 Extranodal MZL of MALT most common Arises in mucosa made lymphoid by chronic antigen . Stomach most common ; then ocular adnexa, lung, salivary gland, thyroid, skin, breast, dura, small bowel. Lymphoepithelial lesions. Usually localized — often curable locally Splenic MZL Spleen + marrow (intrasinusoidal) ± blood; splenomegaly, cytopenias, villous lymphocytes , small IgM paraprotein, autoimmune cytopenias. Nodes uncommon. HCV -linked subset. del(7q), NOTCH2, KLF2 mutations Nodal MZL Nodes only (no extranodal or splenic primary). Behaves and is treated like FL Primary cutaneous MZL Split off as its own entity in WHO-HAEM5 ; very indolent, skin-directed therapy. Borrelia link in European series All are CD5− CD10− small B cells, but genetics differ by site: t(11;18)(q21;q21) BIRC3::MALT1 in gastric and lung MALT; TNFAIP3 loss in ocular adnexa; GPR34 in salivary gland; FAS in cutaneous MZL; KMT2D, NOTCH2, KLF2 in nodal MZL. Also t(14;18)(q32;q21) IGH::MALT1 , t(1;14) IGH::BCL10, t(3;14) IGH::FOXP1. Workup Every MZL: HCV antibody + RNA, HBsAg + anti-HBc, HIV , SPEP/immunofixation (paraprotein common), LDH, β2M Gastric: EGD with multiple biopsies ( map the stomach ), H. pylori by histology + stool antigen or breath test (serology if on PPI), EUS for depth and perigastric nodes, FISH for t(11;18) Splenic: smear (villous lymphocytes), flow, marrow biopsy, CT; DAT and autoimmune screen PET/CT is less reliable than in FL (MALT and SMZL are variably FDG-avid) — CT is acceptable; a hot focus raises concern for transformation Autoimmune history (Sjögren, Hashimoto) and site-specific exams: ophthalmology, ENT, thyroid ultrasound Antigen driver → antimicrobial first Site Driver Antimicrobial therapy & evidence Stomach H. pylori Eradication is first therapy for localized disease. Remission 77.5% (32 studies, 1,408 pts): stage I 78% vs II1 56%; mucosa/submucosa 82% vs deeper 54%; t(11;18)+ only 22% vs 78% Ocular adnexa Chlamydia psittaci (regional) Doxycycline 3 wk: ORR 65%, 5-yr PFS 55% (phase 2, stage I); better if Cp eradicated (86% vs 47%). Cp DNA in 89% of that Italian cohort — prevalence varies widely by region Skin Borrelia burgdorferi (Europe) Antibiotic trial in Borrelia-positive cases Small bowel (IPSID) Campylobacter jejuni α-heavy-chain disease ; early disease regresses with antibiotics Spleen Hepatitis C Antiviral therapy first if no urgent indication: 7/9 CR after interferon with HCV clearance, none in HCV− (Hermine, NEJM 2002); DAAs — SVR 98%, lymphoma response 73% in MZL (Arcaini, Blood 2016) Parotid · thyroid Sjögren · Hashimoto Autoimmune drive — no antimicrobial; treat by stage Staging gastric MALT — Lugano (GI) system I Confined to the GI tract (single or multiple non-contiguous lesions) II1 / II2 Into the abdomen: local (perigastric) nodes / distant (mesenteric, para-aortic) nodes IIE Penetrates serosa into adjacent organs or tissues IV Disseminated extranodal, or supradiaphragmatic nodes. No stage III Non-gastric and nodal/splenic disease: Ann Arbor/Lugano. Small B-cell differential CD5 CD10 CD23 Clue MZL − − − Diagnosis of exclusion; cyclin D1− , MYD88 usually wild-type CLL/SLL + − + CD200+, dim sIg / CD20; LEF1+ Mantle cell + − − Cyclin D1, SOX11 , t(11;14) Follicular − + −/+ BCL2+ follicles, t(14;18) IGH::BCL2 LPL / Waldenström − − − MYD88 L265P (>90%), IgM, plasmacytic Hairy cell − − − CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, annexin A1; BRAF V600E Splenic MZL vs hairy cell: SMZL villi are short and polar , CD25−/annexin−/BRAF wild-type, and the marrow is intrasinusoidal and nodular; HCL has circumferential projections, a “dry tap”, monocytopenia. Splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli (WHO-HAEM5; absorbs HCL-variant) is CD25−, annexin−, TRAP−, CD123−. Splenic diffuse red pulp lymphoma is the other mimic. MALT-IPI — 1 point each Risk Points 5-yr EFS Low 0 70% Intermediate 1 56% High ≥2 29% Age ≥70 · stage III–IV · LDH >ULN . Derived in IELSG-19 (n=401), validated in 633; prognostic in gastric and non-gastric disease (Thieblemont, Blood 2017). Treatment pathway Gastric MALT, localized H. pylori positive eradicate : bismuth quadruple ×14 days confirm cure (breath/stool) ≥4 wk after, PPI off Re-endoscope at ~3 months, then q3–6 mo regression is slow — allow ≥12 months persistent but stable, HP-negative: keep watching HP still present: second-line eradication HP-neg, t(11;18)+, or failure ISRT 24 Gy to stomach — curative intent rituximab if RT not suitable Non-gastric MALT, localized Antimicrobial where a driver fits doxycycline (ocular), antibiotics (skin, IPSID) Then or instead ISRT 24 Gy — curative intent observation acceptable if asymptomatic Splenic MZL HCV positive DAA therapy first unless urgent Indication to treat symptomatic spleen, cytopenias, AIHA/ITP rituximab 375 weekly ×4 ± maintenance splenectomy if rituximab fails or unsuitable Nodal, disseminated, or relapsed Asymptomatic, low burden observe (FL-like GELF logic) Needs systemic therapy BR or rituximab ± chlorambucil R-CHOP rarely (bulky, or concern for large cells) Relapse zanubrutinib · R² · alternative chemo-immunotherapy 3L+: liso-cel CAR-T Systemic therapy — evidence and status Agent · US status Evidence Rituximab ± chlorambucil IELSG-19 (MALT, n=454): 5-yr EFS 68% R-chlorambucil vs 50% rituximab vs 51% chlorambucil; PFS better; OS ~90% in all arms Bendamustine-rituximab Phase 2 MALT data (Salar, Blood 2017) and StiL NHL1 (which included MZL) support BR as the usual frontline chemo-immunotherapy for advanced disease Obinutuzumab not approved for MZL GALLIUM MZL subgroup (n=195): no PFS benefit (4-yr 72.6% vs 64.1%) and more grade 5 AEs (14.9% vs 9.7%) — use rituximab Zanubrutinib accelerated, 2L+ after anti-CD20 (Sep 2021) MAGNOLIA (single arm, n=68): ORR 68% , CR 26%; 24-mo PFS 71%. AF 3%. Confirmatory MAHOGANY (zanubrutinib + rituximab vs R²) still ongoing; approval remains accelerated Ibrutinib MZL indication withdrawn Dec 2023 PCYC-1121 ORR 48% led to 2017 accelerated approval; SELENE (FL/MZL, + chemo) missed PFS → withdrawn R² regular approval FL + MZL (2019) AUGMENT included 63 MZL; overall PFS HR 0.46 — but the MZL subgroup showed no significant PFS benefit (small, imbalanced). Approved nonetheless Liso-cel approved 3L+ (Dec 2025) — first CAR-T for MZL TRANSCEND FL MZL cohort (single arm; nodal 48%, splenic 27%, MALT 25%): ORR 95% of 66 infused (84% of all leukapheresed, per label), CR 56% ITT; grade 3 CRS / neuro 4% each Axi-cel not approved for MZL ZUMA-5 MZL cohort: ORR 77%, median PFS not reached at 3 yr Umbralisib, other PI3Ki withdrawn Umbralisib MZL/FL approval withdrawn 2022 (excess deaths). No bispecific is approved for MZL Transformation to DLBCL is uncommon but prognostically important: suspect with rising LDH, a rapidly growing or FDG-hot lesion, B symptoms. Biopsy, then treat as DLBCL . Scattered large cells in a MALT lymphoma are not by themselves transformation — sheets are. Key evidence Zullo meta-analysis H. pylori eradication: 77.5% remission; t(11;18)+ 22% Ferreri phase 2 Doxycycline, ocular adnexal MZL: ORR 65% Hermine / Arcaini HCV clearance regresses splenic MZL (IFN; DAAs 73%) IELSG-19 R-chlorambucil > either alone for EFS; OS equal GALLIUM (MZL) Obinutuzumab: no PFS gain, more fatal AEs MAGNOLIA Zanubrutinib R/R: ORR 68%, single arm AUGMENT R²: benefit driven by FL, not MZL TRANSCEND FL (MZL) Liso-cel 3L+: ORR 95% infused, CR ~56% After eradication — restaging endoscopy H. pylori Lymphoma Action Gone Gone Observe : EGD q3–6 mo, then yearly Gone Persists Asymptomatic and stable: keep observing (≥12 mo). Symptomatic or progressing: ISRT Present Gone Second-line eradication Present Persists Second-line eradication; ISRT if progressing or symptomatic Splenic MZL — practical points Many never need treatment — observe asymptomatic, stable disease Rituximab alone has largely replaced splenectomy as first therapy: high response rates, no surgical risk. Splenectomy remains diagnostic and therapeutic when tissue is needed or rituximab fails Before splenectomy: pneumococcal, meningococcal (ACWY + B) and Hib vaccines ≥2 weeks before — and before rituximab , which blunts vaccine response Treat autoimmune cytopenias as part of the disease — they often respond to rituximab Dosing Regimen Dosing H. pylori bismuth quadruple PPI BID + bismuth subsalicylate 524 mg QID + tetracycline 500 mg QID + metronidazole 500 mg TID–QID, 14 days Rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×4 ; maintenance 375 q8wk ×2 yr optional BR Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1+2 + rituximab 375 d1, q28d ×6 R-chlorambucil IELSG-19 Chlorambucil 6 mg/m²/d PO wk 1–6, then 2-wk blocks (wk 9–10, 13–14, 17–18, 21–22) + rituximab 375 wk 1–4, 9, 13, 17, 21 Zanubrutinib 160 mg BID or 320 mg daily, continuous R² Lenalidomide 20 mg d1–21 q28d ×12 + rituximab weekly C1, d1 C2–5 ISRT 24 Gy / 12 fx ; 2 × 2 Gy for palliation Pearls Always test for the driver — H. pylori, HCV — before any cytotoxic therapy t(11;18) predicts H. pylori non-response (and dissemination): go to RT rather than repeated antibiotics Give gastric MALT time : histologic regression after eradication can take a year or more MYD88 L265P favors LPL ; CD5+ or cyclin D1+ is not MZL

docs.title: Primary CNS lymphoma
docs.subtitle: A curable brain tumour if you get a clean diagnosis — no steroids before biopsy, a high-dose methotrexate backbone, and thiotepa-based transplant consolidation for the fit. The recurring trade-off is cure versus neurotoxicity
headings: Consolidation — the transplant vs radiation question
Elderly and unfit — what is known
docs.text: Primary CNS lymphoma A curable brain tumour if you get a clean diagnosis — no steroids before biopsy, a high-dose methotrexate backbone, and thiotepa-based transplant consolidation for the fit. The recurring trade-off is cure versus neurotoxicity Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — primary CNS and HIV-associated lymphoma · NCCN · IPCG · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. What it is DLBCL confined to brain, leptomeninges, spinal cord or eyes , no systemic disease. Almost all are non-GCB / ABC-type , with MYD88 L265P and CD79B mutations — the reason BTK inhibitors and lenalidomide work WHO-HAEM5 groups it as primary large B-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites (with vitreoretinal and testicular); ICC keeps primary DLBCL of the CNS Median age late 60s. Immunodeficiency (HIV, transplant) → EBV-driven disease, often multifocal and ring-enhancing Classic MRI: homogeneously enhancing periventricular / deep lesion , restricted diffusion. Presents with focal deficits, personality change, raised ICP Diagnosis AVOID CORTICOSTEROIDS BEFORE BIOPSY unless herniation is imminent — steroids lyse lymphoma cells and the lesion can vanish (“ghost tumor”), leaving a non-diagnostic biopsy. If already given and biopsy is negative, stop them and re-image Stereotactic needle biopsy is the procedure — resection adds nothing and is not the goal Tissue substitutes if biopsy is unsafe: CSF cytology + flow cytometry (and MYD88 L265P) or vitrectomy for vitreous involvement Staging — IPCG extent-of-disease workup Brain MRI with gadolinium (+ spine MRI if symptoms or CSF+) Eyes Slit-lamp + dilated fundus exam by ophthalmology — vitreoretinal disease changes local therapy and follow-up CSF LP if safe (no mass effect): cytology, flow, protein (protein feeds the IELSG score) Exclude systemic PET/CT (or CT C/A/P) · testicular exam ± ultrasound in men · marrow biopsy selectively Labs HIV , HBV/HCV, LDH, creatinine clearance (MTX eligibility), albumin, and look for effusions/ascites Treatment pathway Fit, transplant-eligible (to ~70) Induction: HD-MTX backbone ≥3 g/m² MATRix ×4 (MTX + cytarabine + thiotepa + R) or R-MPV ×5–7, or MT-R (CALGB 50202) MRI after every 2 cycles Consolidation if CR / PR thiotepa-based HDC-ASCT (IELSG43: PFS + OS) not ASCT-fit: EA / HD-cytarabine, or reduced-dose WBRT 23.4 Gy (after R-MPV CR) Older / unfit for MATRix HD-MTX-based, gentler partners R-MPV, MT-R, R-MP, or HD-MTX + R fit >65 years: ASCT on trial (PRIMA-CNS) Then maintain procarbazine, temozolomide or lenalidomide avoid WBRT — neurotoxicity worst in elderly MTX not possible rituximab + temozolomide · WBRT · BTKi best supportive care with steroids Relapsed / refractory Clinical trial first late relapse (>12 mo): re-challenge HD-MTX ibrutinib or lenalidomide ± R; HD-cytarabine ASCT if chemosensitive and not done · WBRT CAR-T on trial · tirabrutinib (PDUFA Dec 2026) Prognostic scores IELSG Ferreri, JCO 2003 1 point each: age >60 · ECOG >1 · LDH ↑ · CSF protein ↑ · deep brain (periventricular, basal ganglia, brainstem, cerebellum). 2-yr OS 0–1: 80% · 2–3: 48% · 4–5: 15% MSKCC Abrey, JCO 2006 Class 1 age <50 · class 2 ≥50 + KPS ≥70 · class 3 ≥50 + KPS <70 — survival falls stepwise; needs only age and KPS Consolidation — the transplant vs radiation question Trial Result IELSG32 2nd rand. Lancet Haem 2017 WBRT vs thiotepa-ASCT after the induction randomization: 2-yr PFS 80% vs 69%, P=0.17 — equivalent disease control, but cognitive decline after WBRT PRECIS Houillier, JCO 2019 Age ≤60, randomized phase 2: 2-yr PFS 63% WBRT vs 87% ASCT ; cognition impaired after WBRT, preserved after ASCT; toxic deaths 1 vs 5 Alliance 51101 Batchelor, Blood Adv 2024 MT-R-A then thiotepa/BCNU-ASCT vs EA: 2-yr PFS 73% vs 51% (P=0.02), but 28% of the EA arm progressed/died in induction; landmark from consolidation 86% vs 71%, NS IELSG43 Illerhaus, Lancet 2026 Phase 3 , n=229, MATRix ×4 then ASCT vs R-DeVIC: 3-yr PFS 78% vs 51% , HR 0.43; OS HR 0.46 (5-yr 84% vs 63%). Fatal events 5 vs 2 — settles ASCT as the standard for fit patients WBRT remains effective but the late leukoencephalopathy, ataxia and dementia make it the last choice for anyone likely to be cured — if used after CR, reduced-dose 23.4 Gy (R-MPV protocol). Elderly and unfit — what is known ANOCEF-GOELAMS Omuro, Lancet Haem 2015 ≥60 yr, randomized phase 2 (non-comparative): MPV-A vs MTX-temozolomide — 1-yr PFS 36% in both ; median OS 31 vs 14 mo; no late neurotoxicity without WBRT PRIMAIN Fritsch, Leukemia 2017 ≥65 yr, R-MP(L) + procarbazine maintenance : CR 36%, 2-yr PFS 37%, OS 47% US real-world David, AJH 2023 539 patients ≥60: combination HD-MTX beat MTX ± R (3-yr PFS 55% with MT-R vs 30%); maintenance 3-yr PFS 65% vs 45% — retrospective Relapsed / refractory agents Ibrutinib 560 mg iLOC phase 2 (n=52): response 52% ITT (CR 19%) at 2 mo, median PFS 4.8 mo ; reaches CSF. Invasive aspergillosis reported (1 fatal). MSKCC phase 1: 10/13 responded. Off-label in the US Tirabrutinib PROSPECT phase 2 (n=48): ORR 67%, CR 44%, median PFS 6.0 mo (ASCO 2025 abstract). Approved in Japan; US NDA under accelerated review, PDUFA 18 Dec 2026 — would be the first US-approved BTKi for PCNSL Lenalidomide ± R REVRI phase 2 (n=50): ORR 36% at end of induction, median PFS 7.8 mo . Lenalidomide maintenance after salvage prolonged response (UCSF, Blood Adv 2018) Re-challenge HD-MTX Reasonable if the prior response lasted >12 months R/R responses are frequent but short — consolidate a second remission (ASCT if not yet done, or maintenance) wherever possible. Regimen dosing (mg/m² unless stated) Regimen Dosing MATRix IELSG32/43 Rituximab 375 d−5 and d0 · MTX 3500 d1 (over 3–4 h) · cytarabine 2000 q12h ×4 d2–3 · thiotepa 30 d4 — q21d ×4, G-CSF. Age 18–70 R-MPV Shah, JCO 2007 Rituximab 500 d1 · MTX 3500 + vincristine 1.4 (handbook cap 2.8 mg) d2 · procarbazine 100 PO d1–7 odd cycles (low-tyramine diet) — q14d ×5; PR → 7 cycles. CR → WBRT 23.4 Gy, then cytarabine 3000 d1–2 ×2 MT-R CALGB 50202 MTX 8000 over 4 h d1 q14d ×8 · rituximab 375 ×6 doses · temozolomide 150 PO d7–11 every other cycle. Then EA : etoposide 40 mg/kg CIV over 96 h + cytarabine 2000 q12h ×8 d1–4 HD-MTX + R MTX 3500–8000 over 4 h q14d + rituximab 375 — elderly / frail backbone HDC-ASCT Thiotepa-based conditioning: carmustine + thiotepa (IELSG32/43, Alliance 51101) or thiotepa + busulfan + cyclophosphamide (PRECIS, MSKCC) Maintenance Lenalidomide 15 mg daily (handbook) · procarbazine 100 mg/day ×5 d q4wk (PRIMAIN) · temozolomide 150 d1–5 q28d (Reni) MTX-ineligible Rituximab 375 + temozolomide (handbook) · temozolomide alone 150 d1–5 q28d · WBRT MT-R and EA dosing per CALGB 50202 (handbook lists EA etoposide as 10 mg/kg/day CIV d1–4, i.e. the same 40 mg/kg total). Prednisolone 1% eye drops with every HD-cytarabine. Supportive care After the biopsy, dexamethasone freely for edema, then taper; PJP prophylaxis on prolonged steroids (atovaquone around MTX) Antiseizure drugs only if seizures — no prophylaxis; prefer non-enzyme-inducing agents VTE is common in PCNSL; weigh anticoagulation against the post-biopsy bleeding window Neurocognitive baseline and follow-up; MRI q3 mo ×2 yr, then less often (late relapses happen) High-dose methotrexate — administration Eligibility CrCl ≥50 mL/min for full dose (50% if 10–50; omit <10). No third-space fluid — drain or avoid with pleural effusion, ascites, edema (MTX sequesters and leaks back, prolonging exposure) Stop interacting drugs PPIs · TMP-SMX · NSAIDs / salicylates · penicillins · probenecid (and levetiracetam has case reports) — hold PJP TMP-SMX until the level clears Hydrate + ALKALINIZE Half-normal saline + 100 mEq NaHCO₃/L at 500 mL/h ×2 h, then 125 mL/h. Do not start until urine pH ≥7 and UOP >100 mL/h; keep pH ≥7 until level <0.05–0.1 µM (MTX precipitates in acid urine). Rescue: NaHCO₃ bolus or acetazolamide Leucovorin PCNSL protocols start 24 h after MTX start (25 mg IV q6h, or 100 mg/m² after 8 g/m² MT-R) — vs 36 h after the 24-h Burkitt infusion. Continue until MTX <0.05 µM Levels Daily from 24 h, with Cr and UOP. Escalate leucovorin (100 mg/m² q6h) for a Cr rise >50% or levels above the protocol curve — handbook thresholds (24-h infusion): >20 µM at 24 h, >1 at 48 h, >0.1 at 72 h; 4-h PCNSL infusions run on their own nomogram Glucarpidase 50 U/kg IV once for level >1 µM with delayed clearance from renal failure. No leucovorin within 2 h either side; immunoassay unreliable for 48 h (DAMPA cross-reacts) — use chromatographic assay Watch AKI · transaminitis (common, transient) · mucositis · myelosuppression · acute / subacute encephalopathy (stroke-like; consider aminophylline, dextromethorphan) Special situations HIV-associated PCNSL is EBV-driven and arises with advanced immunosuppression. Differential is toxoplasmosis — toxo serology, CSF EBV PCR , and biopsy if lesions fail to shrink on empiric anti-toxoplasma therapy. Treat with ART + HD-MTX-based therapy with curative intent (handbook: continue or start ART during chemotherapy) Vitreoretinal involvement: systemic HD-MTX reaches the eye inconsistently — add intravitreal MTX or rituximab, or ocular RT if it persists (handbook: orbital RT or ophthalmology referral for intra-ocular therapy) Response (IPCG): CR requires no enhancing disease, off steroids ≥2 weeks , a normal eye exam and negative CSF cytology — steroid-driven shrinkage is not a response Key trials IELSG20 Ferreri, Lancet 2009 MTX ± HD-cytarabine: CR 46% vs 18% — established the doublet IELSG32 / MATRix Lancet Haem 2016 + rituximab + thiotepa: CR 49% vs 23% ; 7-yr OS 56% vs 21%; 6% toxic deaths. Randomized phase 2 CALGB 50202 Rubenstein, JCO 2013 MT-R → EA, no WBRT, single arm: CR 66%, 2-yr PFS 57% IELSG43 Illerhaus, Lancet 2026 ASCT vs R-DeVIC after MATRix: 3-yr PFS 78% vs 51% ; OS HR 0.46.
