Phase 3 PRECIS · Alliance 51101 ASCT ≥ WBRT or EA for disease control; WBRT costs cognition HOVON 105 / ALLG Bromberg, Lancet Oncol 2019 MBVP ± rituximab, phase 3: no EFS benefit (HR 1.00) ANOCEF elderly · PRIMAIN Outcomes ≥60–65 remain poor: 1–2 yr PFS ~35% iLOC · REVRI · PROSPECT Ibrutinib, R2 and tirabrutinib in R/R disease Pearls Steroids before biopsy are the #1 avoidable diagnostic failure Urine alkalinization is mandatory for HD-MTX (the opposite of TLS, where it is harmful) Intrathecal chemotherapy is generally omitted when systemic MTX ≥3 g/m² is given — no benefit shown in retrospective series (R-MPV adds Ommaya MTX only for positive CSF) Testicular exam in every man — testicular DLBCL can seed the CNS and changes the diagnosis Rituximab is contested: it raised CR in IELSG32, but HOVON 105/ALLG NHL 24 (phase 3, n=199) found no EFS benefit (1-yr EFS 52% vs 49%, HR 1.00) — it stays in most regimens anyway

docs.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma
docs.subtitle: Nodal PTCL · ALCL · NK/T · ATLL · rare extranodal subtypes — CD30 and ALK status pick the induction; ALK+ ALCL is the only subtype CHOP-like therapy reliably cures
headings: Frontline evidence — what it actually shows
Relapsed / refractory agents — and their US status
docs.text: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma Nodal PTCL · ALCL · NK/T · ATLL · rare extranodal subtypes — CD30 and ALK status pick the induction; ALK+ ALCL is the only subtype CHOP-like therapy reliably cures Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin, T-cell lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. Entities — WHO-HAEM5 / ICC 2022 Entity What defines it PTCL-NOS ~26% Diagnosis of exclusion; CD4 > CD8, loss of CD5/CD7 common. GATA3-high subset does worse than TBX21 Nodal TFH lymphoma, angioimmuno­blastic type ~19% Formerly AITL (ICC: follicular helper T-cell lymphoma). Older adults; rash, effusions, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, Coombs+ hemolysis , EBV+ B-blasts. PD-1, CXCL13, ICOS, BCL6, CD10. TET2, DNMT3A, IDH2 R172, RHOA G17V . Follicular and NOS types share the TFH phenotype ALCL, ALK+ Younger; NPM1::ALK t(2;5); strong uniform CD30. 5-yr OS ~85% — the good one ALCL, ALK− Test FISH: DUSP22-R (~30%) 5-yr OS 90% · TP63-R (~8%) 17% · neither 42% Breast implant-associated ALCL Textured implants ; late seroma or capsular mass, CD30+ ALK−. Tap the seroma → cytology + CD30 Extranodal NK/T-cell ~10% WHO-HAEM5 drops “nasal type.” EBV+ always , CD56+, cCD3ε+, surface CD3−; angiocentric, necrotic mid-face mass; Asia and Latin America ATLL ~10% HTLV-1 ; Japan, Caribbean. CD4+CD25+ “flower cells,” hypercalcemia , lytic lesions, skin EATL · MEITL EATL: celiac (refractory sprue). MEITL (old “type II EATL”): no celiac, CD8+CD56+, SETD2 loss. Perforation risk Hepatosplenic γδ TCR; young men, IBD on anti-TNF + thiopurine ; hepatosplenomegaly, sinusoidal marrow, no nodes. Dismal Frequencies from the International T-cell Project (Vose, JCO 2008, n=1,153) — 10% of referral diagnoses were misclassified , so insist on expert hematopathology review. Treatment pathway Nodal PTCL — frontline Induction by CD30 and subtype CD30 ≥10%, esp. sALCL: BV-CHP ×6 (ECHELON-2) CD30−: CHOP or CHOEP (age ≤60) ×6 EATL: CHOP ×1 → IVE/MTX → auto-HCT Consolidate in CR1? ALK+ ALCL and DUSP22-R: no — observe others, fit, in CR: consider auto-HCT evidence is non-randomized (NLG-T-01, COMPLETE) and conflicting (LYSA registry: no benefit) Limited stage CHOP-based ×3–4 + ISRT, or ×6 ± RT Relapsed / refractory Transplant candidate salvage (ICE, GDP, DHAP) or single agent → allo-HCT (auto if chemosensitive, no prior ASCT) Match the agent to the biology CD30+: BV (sALCL ORR 86%, CR 57%) ALK+: crizotinib or alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib TFH/AITL: duvelisib, HDAC inhibitor, aza any: belinostat, pralatrexate, gemcitabine, benda Extranodal NK/T-cell Localized (IE–IIE) RT ≥50 Gy + asparaginase-based chemo concurrent DeVIC or sequential P-GemOx / DDGP no anthracyclines — P-glycoprotein resists them Advanced or relapsed DDGP or mod-SMILE → allo-HCT if fit R/R after asparaginase: PD-1 blockade follow plasma EBV DNA as the tumor marker ATLL (HTLV-1) By Shimoyama subtype smoldering / favorable chronic: watch or AZT/IFN acute: AZT + IFN-α or chemo, then allo-HCT lymphoma type: chemo (CHOP, mLSG15) → allo mogamulizumab : R/R (Japan) — GVHD risk pre-allo Workup Excisional or core biopsy with T-cell panel, CD30 (% of cells), ALK, TFH markers, EBER; TCR clonality . ALK− ALCL → DUSP22 and TP63 FISH PET/CT , marrow biopsy, LDH, HTLV-1 serology (and calcium) in anyone at risk; plasma EBV DNA in NK/T and AITL HBV/HCV/HIV; echo before anthracycline. Nasal NK/T: MRI of the nasopharynx + ENT exam ATLL: screen for Strongyloides (co-endemic with HTLV-1) before steroids Prognosis — PIT and IPI PIT factors 5-yr OS 10-yr OS 0 62% 55% 1 53% 39% 2 33% 18% 3–4 18% 13% PIT (Gallamini, Blood 2004): age >60, LDH >ULN, ECOG ≥2, marrow involvement . The IPI also stratifies PTCL and is the stratifier in ECHELON-2. NK/T uses PINK (age >60, stage III–IV, distant nodes, non-nasal primary; 3-yr OS 81/62/25% for 0/1/≥2); PINK-E adds detectable EBV DNA. ATLL and rare subtypes ATLL subtypes (Shimoyama): acute, lymphoma, chronic (unfavorable if LDH, BUN or albumin abnormal), smoldering. AZT + IFN-α (meta-analysis, n=254): 5-yr OS 46% with first-line antivirals — benefit in acute, chronic and smoldering , while lymphoma type does better with chemo mLSG15 (VCAP-AMP-VECP) beat biweekly CHOP on CR (40% vs 25%), 3-yr OS 24% vs 13% (NS). Mogamulizumab : R/R ATLL ORR 50% (Japan-approved, not US). Given <50 d before allo-HCT it raises severe GVHD and NRM (1-yr OS 32% vs 49%) BIA-ALCL: disease confined to capsule/seroma → total en bloc capsulectomy + implant removal (both sides) is usually curative; nodal or unresectable → BV-CHP Hepatosplenic: CHOP fails — ICE or IVAC-type induction, then allo-HCT in CR1 EATL/MEITL: nutrition + surgical review for perforation; IVE/MTX (Newcastle) → auto-HCT. AITL: steroids/cyclosporine for immune flares; watch for concurrent EBV+ B-cell lymphoma Frontline evidence — what it actually shows ECHELON-2 (BV-CHP vs CHOP, CD30 ≥10%): PFS HR 0.71, OS HR 0.66 — the only regimen to beat CHOP on survival. 5-yr PFS 51% vs 43% , OS 70% vs 61% But the benefit sits in systemic ALCL (70% of enrollment; 5-yr PFS HR 0.55). PTCL-NOS HR 0.75 (NS); AITL favored CHOP (small n). The label is sALCL or other CD30-expressing PTCL ; outside ALCL it is a reasonable, not proven, choice CD30 threshold was ≥10% by local IHC; retreatment with BV at relapse after BV-CHP still gave ORR 59% CHOEP (DSHNHL pooled analysis): etoposide improved 3-yr EFS 75% vs 51% in age ≤60 with normal LDH; over 60, CHOP-21 stays standard Adding to CHOP has failed: Ro-CHOP (PFS 12.0 vs 10.2 mo, HR 0.81, NS , more toxicity); alemtuzumab-CHOP; lenalidomide-CHOP in AITL Auto-HCT in CR1 — never randomized. NLG-T-01 (CHOEP-14 → ASCT, ALK+ excluded): 5-yr OS 51%, PFS 44%, TRM 4%. COMPLETE cohort: ASCT in CR1 OS HR 0.37, driven by AITL. LYSA propensity-matched registry: no PFS or OS benefit (HR 1.02). Offer it to fit non-ALK+ patients in CR, especially AITL and higher IPI Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma Anthracyclines fail — tumor cells express P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Build regimens on L-asparaginase/pegaspargase , methotrexate, gemcitabine, platinum, etoposide Localized: radiation is the backbone. DeVIC ×3 + concurrent RT 50 Gy (JCOG0211): 2-yr OS 78% vs 45% historical RT alone. Sequential/sandwich P-GemOx or DDGP + RT is the common alternative Advanced: DDGP beat SMILE in a randomized trial (n=87; PFS HR 0.42, OS HR 0.41, 5-yr OS 74% vs 52%, less myelosuppression). SMILE: ORR 79% but grade 4 neutropenia 92% — require ALC ≥500 EBV DNA in plasma: detectable at diagnosis is adverse (PINK-E); persistent after therapy predicts relapse R/R after asparaginase: PD-1 blockade — pembrolizumab responded in 7/7 (Kwong, Blood 2017); off-label in the US. Consolidate responders with allo-HCT Relapsed / refractory agents — and their US status Agent Evidence and status (Sept 2026) Brentuximab vedotin anti-CD30 ADC R/R sALCL ORR 86% , CR 57% (Pro, JCO 2012). Regular approval. Activity in CD30+ non-ALCL is lower and not CD30-level dependent Pralatrexate antifolate PROPEL: ORR 29% , DOR 10.1 mo, PFS 3.5 mo. Accelerated approval 2009 — still unconfirmed ; the confirmatory trial will not read out before ~2030 Belinostat pan-HDAC BELIEF: ORR 26% , CR 11%, DOR 13.6 mo, but PFS 1.6 mo. Accelerated 2014, unconfirmed — ODAC (Nov 2023) criticized both delays. Least myelosuppressive; OK with low platelets Romidepsin HDAC 1/2 ORR 25%, DOR 17 mo. PTCL indication withdrawn 2021 after Ro-CHOP was negative — still NCCN-listed and still FDA-approved for CTCL Duvelisib PI3K-δ/γ PRIMO (JCO 2026, n=123): ORR 48% , CR 33%, but PFS 3.4 mo; AITL ORR 62%, CR 51% , PFS 8.3 mo. Not FDA-approved for PTCL (phase 3 TERZO ongoing) Valemetostat EZH1/2 VALENTINE-PTCL01: ORR 44% (52/119). Approved in Japan (ATLL 2022, PTCL June 2024); not US-approved Golidocitinib JAK1 JACKPOT8 B: ORR 44% , CR 24% (94% Asian). Conditional approval in China (June 2024); US fast-track only ALK inhibitors Crizotinib FDA-approved Jan 2021 for age 1–21 (ORR 88%); adults off-label. Alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib also active Others Gemcitabine, bendamustine (ORR 50%, PFS 3.6 mo), lenalidomide (AITL), azacitidine in TET2-mutant TFH , cyclosporine for AITL immune phenomena Response rates are all single-arm and PFS is short — use these to bridge a responder to allo-HCT , the only strategy with a durable plateau in R/R PTCL. Toxicity and monitoring Brentuximab: peripheral neuropathy — hold for grade 3, dose-reduce for grade 2. PML (boxed warning); pancreatitis. Never with bleomycin (pulmonary toxicity) Pralatrexate: mucositis is dose-limiting and prevented by B12/folate; check CBC weekly; reduce for CrCl <30 HDAC inhibitors: thrombocytopenia, nausea, fatigue, QTc — ECG, keep K and Mg replete. Belinostat: UGT1A1 genotype guides the dose Duvelisib boxed warnings: fatal infections, colitis/diarrhea , severe skin reactions, pneumonitis; transaminitis. Mandatory PJP prophylaxis; CMV monitoring Asparaginase: hypersensitivity, pancreatitis , hepatotoxicity, hypofibrinogenemia and thrombosis , hyperglycemia. Check fibrinogen, lipase, LFTs, glucose each cycle HD-MTX (SMILE): hydration + urine alkalinization (pH ≥7) , MTX levels, leucovorin rescue; glucarpidase if delayed clearance with AKI; stop PPIs, TMP-SMX, NSAIDs around the dose Ifosfamide: mesna; watch for encephalopathy (methylene blue) and Fanconi-type nephrotoxicity ALK inhibitors: crizotinib — visual disturbance, transaminitis, QTc, bradycardia Prophylaxis: acyclovir + TMP-SMX with HDAC, duvelisib, SMILE, alemtuzumab; entecavir if HBcAb+ Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing BV-CHP ECHELON-2 Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180 mg) + cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² + doxorubicin 50 mg/m² d1, prednisone 100 mg d1–5 — q21d ×6–8. No vincristine. Primary G-CSF CHOP / CHOEP CHOP as above + vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (max 2) d1; CHOEP adds etoposide 100 mg/m² d1–3 — q21d ×6 (NLG used CHOEP-14) Brentuximab (R/R) 1.8 mg/kg IV q21d up to 16 cycles; 1.2 mg/kg if Child-Pugh A or neuropathy grade 2 Pralatrexate 30 mg/m² IV push weekly ×6 q7wk. Folic acid 1–1.25 mg daily from 7–10 d before until 30 d after; B12 1 mg IM q8–10 wk . Leucovorin mouthwash for mucositis Belinostat 1,000 mg/m² IV over 30 min d1–5 q21d; 750 mg/m² if UGT1A1*28 homozygous Romidepsin 14 mg/m² IV over 4 h d1, 8, 15 q28d — K ≥4, Mg ≥2 before each dose; QTc Duvelisib off-label 75 mg PO BID ×2 cycles, then 25 mg BID , q28d continuous. PJP + HSV/VZV prophylaxis Gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d ×3–6 DeVIC + RT 2/3 dose Dexamethasone 40 mg d1–3 + ifosfamide 1,000 mg/m² d1–3 (+ mesna) + etoposide 67 mg/m² d1–3 + carboplatin 200 mg/m² d1 — q21d ×3, concurrent RT 50 Gy DDGP Dexamethasone 15 mg/m² d1–5 + cisplatin 20 mg/m² d1–4 + gemcitabine 800 mg/m² d1, 8 + pegaspargase 2,500 IU/m² d1 — q21d ×6 Modified SMILE MTX 2 g/m² d1 (leucovorin from 24 h) · ifosfamide 1.5 g/m² + mesna, dexamethasone 40 mg, etoposide 100 mg/m² d2–4 · pegaspargase 2,000 U/m² d7 once MTX <0.04 µM — q28d ×2–6. Urine alkalinization for HD-MTX AZT + IFN ATLL High-dose oral zidovudine + daily SC interferon-α, continued indefinitely while responding — no randomized dosing standard ; follow the treating center's protocol DDGP doses are from the Chinese trial protocol (Li, Clin Cancer Res 2016). Interferon alfa-2b (Intron A) is off the US market — pegylated IFN is the practical substitute. Key trials Trial Design Result and meaning ECHELON-2 Lancet 2019 Phase 3, double-blind, n=452, CD30 ≥10%, 70% sALCL BV-CHP vs CHOP: mPFS 48.2 vs 20.8 mo , HR 0.71; OS HR 0.66 ; 5-yr OS 70% vs 61%. Benefit concentrated in sALCL Ro-CHOP JCO 2022 Phase 3, n=421, untreated PTCL Romidepsin + CHOP: PFS 12.0 vs 10.2 mo, HR 0.81 — negative ; more grade 3–4 cytopenias. Ended the PTCL indication NLG-T-01 JCO 2012 Single-arm phase 2, n=166, ALK+ excluded CHOEP-14 → ASCT: 72% reached transplant; 5-yr PFS 44% , OS 51%, TRM 4% LYSA registry · COMPLETE Observational, n=269 · n=119 in CR1 ASCT in CR1: propensity-matched no benefit (HR 1.02) vs OS HR 0.37 (driven by AITL). Unresolved PROPEL JCO 2011 Single-arm, n=115 Pralatrexate: ORR 29%, DOR 10.1 mo, PFS 3.5 mo — accelerated approval, unconfirmed BELIEF JCO 2015 Single-arm, n=129 Belinostat: ORR 26%, CR 11%, DOR 13.6 mo, PFS 1.6 mo PRIMO JCO 2026 Single-arm, n=123 Duvelisib: ORR 48%, CR 33%; AITL ORR 62%, CR 51% . Not FDA-approved for PTCL VALENTINE-PTCL01 Single-arm, n=133 Valemetostat: ORR 44%. Approved in Japan only JACKPOT8 B Single-arm, n=104, 94% Asian Golidocitinib: ORR 44%, CR 24%. China only JCOG0211 JCO 2009 Phase 1/2, n=33, stage IE–IIE nasal DeVIC + RT 50 Gy: 2-yr OS 78% vs 45% historical RT alone DDGP vs SMILE JAMA Oncol 2022 Randomized, n=87, stage III–IV NK/T PFS HR 0.42, OS HR 0.41; 5-yr OS 74% vs 52%; less myelosuppression JCOG9801 JCO 2007 Phase 3, n=118, aggressive ATLL mLSG15 vs CHOP-14: CR 40% vs 25%; 3-yr OS 24% vs 13% (NS) AZT/IFN meta-analysis JCO 2010 n=254, retrospective First-line antivirals: 5-yr OS 46%; benefit in leukemic subtypes, not lymphoma type

docs.title: Myelodysplastic syndromes
docs.subtitle: Clonal stem-cell disorders with ineffective hematopoiesis → cytopenias, dysplasia, and variable AML risk · blasts <20% · everything collapses to lower risk (fix the cytopenias) vs higher risk (alter the natural history)
docs.text: Myelodysplastic syndromes Clonal stem-cell disorders with ineffective hematopoiesis → cytopenias, dysplasia, and variable AML risk · blasts <20% · everything collapses to lower risk (fix the cytopenias) vs higher risk (alter the natural history) Compiled from the Encyclopedia MDS review note and Fellowship Anki deck · WHO 2022 / ICC · IPSS-M (Bernard, NEJM Evid 2022) · Bernard/Papaemmanuil molecular taxonomy (Blood 2024) Diagnosis Triad: (1) cytopenia + (2) morphologic dysplasia in >10% of a lineage + (3) clonality (cytogenetic or molecular). >90% show clonality on karyotype/NGS Normal marrow cellularity ≈ 100 − age . Most MDS is hypercellular with ineffective hematopoiesis; a hypoplastic variant overlaps aplastic anemia Dysplasia is not MDS without clonality. Exclude mimics first: B12, folate, copper deficiency, HIV, alcohol, medications, post-chemotherapy marrow recovery † Hypoplastic MDS overlaps aplastic anemia and PNH — send flow for a PNH clone † Consider VEXAS (somatic UBA1 ) in older men with inflammatory features, macrocytic anemia and vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors Classification (WHO 2022 / ICC) Genetically defined SF3B1 (favorable, ring sideroblasts) · isolated del(5q) (lenalidomide-responsive) · biallelic TP53 (poor) Blast categories MDS-IB1 = 5–9% blasts · MDS-IB2 = 10–19% The AML border At 10–19% blasts with a defining lesion , ICC calls it MDS/AML (managed as AML) while WHO calls it MDS-IB2 † del(5q) phenotype Macrocytic anemia, normal or high platelets , hypolobated megakaryocytes, female predominance Risk stratification IPSS-R (2012) Cytogenetic risk, marrow blast %, hemoglobin, platelets, ANC → 5 groups IPSS-M (2022) Keeps blasts, Hgb, platelets, cytogenetics · drops ANC · adds 31 gene mutations → 6 groups Mutation weights TP53-multihit highest risk · SF3B1 favorable · adverse: ASXL1, RUNX1, SRSF2, U2AF1, EZH2, FLT3, KMT2A-PTD Calculator at mds-risk-model.com. IPSS-M still outperforms a purely molecular-subgroup model, so use it for risk scoring. Molecular taxonomy (Bernard/Papaemmanuil, Blood 2024). 3,233 patients, 152-gene panel → 16 molecular groups covering 86%, median OS ranging 0.9–8.2 years . Favorable: SF3B1 (14%, most common, OS ~6 yr) · del(5q) · CCUS-like · ZRSR2 · driver-negative. Monocytic: bi-TET2 (13%, CMML overlap). Aggressive: AML-like (OS ~0.9 yr, 40% 2-yr AML transformation) · TP53-complex · IDH-STAG2 · −7/SETBP1 · EZH2-ASXL1 · BCOR. DDX41: high blasts and high transformation but no excess mortality . Take-home: the prognostic weight of blast % depends on genetic subtype — but IPSS-M still outperforms a groups-only model, so the taxonomy informs biology rather than replacing risk scoring. Treatment pathway Lower risk — goal is fixing cytopenias Symptomatic anemia serum EPO <500 + low transfusion burden → erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (epoetin or darbepoetin) By biomarker isolated del(5q) → lenalidomide ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 → luspatercept ESA-refractory non-del(5q) → imetelstat Hypoplastic or younger immunosuppression: ATG ± cyclosporine Throughout transfusions; iron chelation if chronically transfused; infection prophylaxis Higher risk — goal is altering natural history Hypomethylating agent azacitidine (or decitabine) † give ≥4–6 cycles before judging response AZA-001: OS 24.5 vs 15 months Transplant-eligible allogeneic HSCT is the only cure † timing driven by IPSS-M — do not wait for AML transformation in higher-risk disease TP53-multihit poor with all standard therapy → prioritize clinical trial or transplant † After HMA failure dismal — clinical trial or transplant; no established standard salvage Biomarker / setting → therapy Setting Therapy Key trial Lower risk, EPO <500, low transfusion burden Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent — Lower risk, isolated del(5q) Lenalidomide MDS-003 / MDS-004 Lower risk, transfusion-dependent, ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 Luspatercept — activin receptor II ligand trap, improves late-stage erythropoiesis MEDALIST; COMMANDS (beat epoetin alfa first-line) Lower risk, ESA-refractory, non-del(5q) Imetelstat — telomerase inhibitor IMerge (FDA-approved 2024) Hypoplastic / younger lower risk Immunosuppression (ATG ± cyclosporine) — Higher risk Azacitidine or decitabine AZA-001 — OS benefit Higher risk, transplant-eligible Allogeneic HSCT — the only curative option — TP53-multihit Poor with everything → trial or transplant — Trials CALGB 9221 (2002) The first RCT of azacitidine vs supportive care — higher response and delayed transformation to AML or death . The disease-modifying signal (Silverman, JCO) AZA-001 (2009) Practice-defining — overall survival benefit in higher-risk MDS, median OS 24.5 vs 15 months (Fenaux, Lancet Oncol) † Decitabine (D-0007, EORTC 06011) Improved response and delayed AML progression but no OS benefit . Caveat: decitabine was capped at 6 cycles (median 4) while azacitidine continued to progression (median 9). Practically, azacitidine is the HMA with an OS benefit MDS-003 / MDS-004 Lenalidomide in transfusion-dependent lower-risk del(5q) — ~67% transfusion independence (List, NEJM 2006) MEDALIST (2020) Luspatercept after ESA failure, ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 — transfusion independence 38% vs 13% COMMANDS (2023) Luspatercept beat epoetin alfa first-line — ~59% vs ~31% IMerge (2024) Imetelstat in ESA-refractory non-del(5q) — 8-week transfusion independence 40% vs 15% † BMT CTN 1102 Donor vs no-donor in higher-risk MDS age 50–75 — 3-yr OS 47.9% vs 26.6% . The evidence for transplanting older patients (Nakamura, JCO 2021) † VERONA (2025) Venetoclax + azacitidine in higher-risk MDS missed its OS endpoint (22.2 vs 21.7 mo, HR 0.91) despite higher response rates — ven/aza is standard in AML but not MDS

docs.title: Melanoma
docs.subtitle: Staged by Breslow thickness + ulceration; LDH is a staging modifier in M1 disease · ~50% of cutaneous melanomas carry BRAF V600 · the central modern question is immunotherapy sequencing, not whether to give it
docs.text: Melanoma Staged by Breslow thickness + ulceration ; LDH is a staging modifier in M1 disease · ~50% of cutaneous melanomas carry BRAF V600 · the central modern question is immunotherapy sequencing , not whether to give it Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Melanoma — an advanced-disease chapter. Biopsy technique, excision margins, SLNB indications, dosing, surveillance and the variant/toxicity material are not in it ; those are marked † and drawn from NCCN and product labeling. Workup † Excisional biopsy with 1–3 mm margins, full thickness, oriented along lymphatic drainage — avoid a superficial shave , which compromises Breslow depth Pathologic confirmation; report Breslow thickness and ulceration († mitotic rate is still reported though no longer a staging criterion) Imaging: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (add neck if head-and-neck primary), or PET/CT MRI brain for stage III–IV Labs: CBC, CMP, serum LDH BRAF V600 testing in all advanced cutaneous melanoma If BRAF wild-type → NGS ; in acral/mucosal look specifically for KIT mutations or TRK fusions Staging — AJCC 8th T by thickness T1 ≤1 mm · T2 >1–2 · T3 >2–4 · T4 >4 mm; suffix a = no ulceration, b = ulcerated T1a vs T1b T1a = <0.8 mm without ulceration ; T1b = <0.8 mm ulcerated, or 0.8–1.0 mm either way N N1 = 1 node or in-transit/satellite alone · N2 = 2–3 · N3 = ≥4, or matted M M1a skin/soft tissue/non-regional node · M1b lung · M1c other visceral · M1d = CNS LDH Explicit M-category modifier: (0) = normal, (1) = elevated † Localized management (NCCN) Breslow depth Excision margin In situ 0.5–1.0 cm ≤1.0 mm 1 cm >1.0–2.0 mm 1–2 cm >2.0 mm 2 cm † Sentinel lymph node biopsy: not recommended for T1a (risk <5%) · discuss for T1b · recommended for T2 and above . Completion lymph node dissection is no longer routine after a positive sentinel node (MSLT-II, DeCOG-SLT) — nodal ultrasound surveillance instead. Treatment pathway Localized and resectable Surgery is potentially curative wide local excision by Breslow depth † SLNB for T1b and above Adjuvant anti-PD-1 nivolumab or pembrolizumab × 1 year for resected stage IIB and higher † BRAF V600: dabrafenib + trametinib an option Resectable stage III — neoadjuvant preferred Give immunotherapy before surgery NADINA : ipilimumab 1 + nivolumab 3 mg/kg (“flipped dose”) ×2 pre-op, then adjuvant nivo S1801 : pembrolizumab 200 mg ×3 pre-op improves EFS vs adjuvant therapy alone Unresectable stage III or IV First line — immunotherapy nivolumab + ipilimumab (CheckMate-067) nivolumab + relatlimab (RELATIVITY-047) anti-PD-1 alone if not fit for a combination BRAF V600-mutant sequencing immunotherapy FIRST, then BRAF/MEK DREAMseq 2-yr OS 72% vs 52% exception: visceral crisis, or steroid-dependent brain mets → brief BRAF/MEK then switch (sandwich) Later lines TIL therapy after ICI (RR ~30%) T-VEC for cutaneous/subcutaneous/nodal disease chemotherapy last resort — RR <20% Oligometastatic metastasectomy not preferred alone if fit for systemic therapy — give adjuvant therapy after complete resection Brain metastases Steroid requirement is the discriminator asymptomatic, no steroids: ipi/nivo intracranial ORR 53–57% (CheckMate-204) symptomatic or on steroids: RR only ~17% → add surgery + targeted therapy; SRS, not WBRT Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Setting Pembrolizumab † 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk adjuvant ×1 yr; metastatic Nivolumab † 240 mg q2wk or 480 mg q4wk adjuvant ×1 yr; metastatic Ipilimumab + nivolumab † ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg q3wk ×4, then nivolumab maintenance 1L metastatic (CheckMate-067) — neoadjuvant “flipped” ipilimumab 1 mg/kg + nivolumab 3 mg/kg × 2 cycles pre-op resectable stage III (NADINA) Nivolumab + relatlimab † 480 mg + 160 mg q4wk (Opdualag) 1L metastatic Dabrafenib + trametinib † 150 mg BID + 2 mg daily BRAF V600; also adjuvant Encorafenib + binimetinib † 450 mg daily + 45 mg BID BRAF V600 Vemurafenib + cobimetinib † 960 mg BID + 60 mg daily (21/7) BRAF V600 Imatinib † for activating KIT mutations acral / mucosal TIL therapy (lifileucel) resect → expand ex vivo with IL-2 → lymphodepleting chemo → single infusion → high-dose IL-2 PD-1-refractory T-VEC intralesional oncolytic HSV expressing GM-CSF cutaneous, subcutaneous, nodal High-dose IL-2 largely replaced by checkpoint and targeted therapy historical Chemotherapy dacarbazine · temozolomide · carboplatin + paclitaxel salvage; RR <20%, 4–6 months † Doses are from product labeling — the handbook chapter states dosing only for the two neoadjuvant regimens. Cytotoxic chemotherapy “no longer plays a well-defined role” in metastatic melanoma. Biomarker → therapy Alteration Therapy BRAF V600 (~50%) BRAF + MEK doublet — always dual, never single-agent BRAF (resistance, and BRAFi skin toxicity). Immunotherapy still works and generally comes first KIT (~15% of acral/mucosal) Imatinib — responses with activating mutations (~1/3 respond); KIT amplification alone typically does not respond TRK fusion Found on NGS in BRAF wild-type acral/mucosal disease † HLA-A*02:01 Tebentafusp in metastatic uveal melanoma; also eligibility for brenetafusp trials in cutaneous disease BRAF wild-type Send NGS for other actionable drivers Trial evidence CheckMate-067 (10-yr) ipi/nivo vs nivo vs ipi — median OS 72 / 37 / 20 months ; 10-yr OS 43% / 37% / 19% . If progression-free at 3 years, 10-yr melanoma-specific survival >96% (Wolchok, NEJM 2024) CheckMate-204 brain metastases on ipi/nivo — asymptomatic: intracranial ORR 53–57%, 36-mo iPFS ~54%, OS ~72%. Symptomatic or on steroids: RR ~17%, iPFS ~19%, OS ~37% (Long, JCO 2023) RELATIVITY-047 relatlimab + nivolumab vs nivolumab — median PFS 10.1 vs 4.6 months (Tawbi, NEJM 2022) NADINA neoadjuvant ipi/nivo → adjuvant nivolumab — EFS and distant-metastasis-free survival benefit; major pathologic response 58% ; grade 3+ AEs ~30% (Rozeman, Nat Med 2024) SWOG S1801 neoadjuvant → adjuvant pembrolizumab — 2-yr EFS 72% vs 48% with adjuvant alone; no added surgical complications (Patel, NEJM 2023) DREAMseq BRAF V600: IO first then targeted vs the reverse — 2-yr OS 72% vs 52% (Atkins, JCO 2023) SECOMBIT at 4 years, IO-first or sandwich beats targeted-first for PFS and OS (Ascierto, JCO 2023) Dabrafenib + trametinib pooled phase III: 34% alive at 5 years , ~20% progression-free; better with normal LDH, good performance status, <3 metastatic sites TIL therapy RR ~30% with durable remissions; superior to ipilimumab in PD-1-refractory disease (Warner, Clin Cancer Res 2022) † Adjuvant trials KEYNOTE-716 pembrolizumab, resected stage IIB/IIC — 3-yr RFS 76.2% vs 63.4% (HR 0.65) CheckMate 76K nivolumab 480 mg q4wk × 12 months, resected stage IIB/IIC — RFS HR 0.42 , DMFS HR 0.47 KEYNOTE-054 pembrolizumab, resected stage III CheckMate 238 nivolumab vs ipilimumab, resected stage IIIB/C–IV COMBI-AD dabrafenib + trametinib × 12 months, resected stage III BRAF V600 All are 1-year regimens. The stage IIB/IIC trials have shown RFS and DMFS benefit but no definitive OS benefit yet — worth saying out loud when consenting a patient with resected node-negative disease. Stage groupings Clinical 0 Tis · IA T1a · IB T1b or T2a · IIA T2b/T3a · IIB T3b/T4a · IIC T4b · III = any N ≥N1, M0 · IV = M1 Pathologic IIIA T1a–T2a with N1a or N2a Pathologic IIIB T0 with N1b/c · T1a–T2a with N1b/c or N2b · T2b/T3a with N1a–c or N2a/b Pathologic IIIC T0 with N2b/c or N3b/c · T1a–T3a with N2c or N3a–c · T3b/T4a with any N ≥N1 · T4b with N1a–N2c Pathologic IIID T4b with N3a/b/c N suffixes a = clinically occult (found on SLNB) · b = clinically detected · c = in-transit, satellite or microsatellite disease present † Immune-related adverse events Grade 1: usually continue with close monitoring. Grade 2: hold the checkpoint inhibitor; prednisone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day if persistent Grade 3–4: hold or permanently discontinue; prednisone or methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day , tapered over at least 4–6 weeks Steroid-refractory colitis → infliximab or vedolizumab. Hepatitis → mycophenolate, not infliximab (hepatotoxicity) Myocarditis → urgent high-dose steroids and permanent discontinuation — rare but highly lethal Endocrine events are the exception: hypophysitis, thyroiditis, adrenal insufficiency and type 1 diabetes are usually irreversible , but you replace the hormone and generally continue the checkpoint inhibitor Monitor TSH and free T4 at baseline and every 4–6 weeks; check HBsAg and HBcAb before starting Onset is typically weeks to months — but can occur after discontinuation . Ipilimumab-containing regimens carry the highest risk Variants & special situations Acral (~2–3%) More common in darker skin. Lower TMB, lower BRAF rate, lower immunotherapy response , more aggressive — check KIT Mucosal (~1–2%) Distinct genetics, low BRAF, poor immunotherapy response, presents late because the site is hidden; KIT actionable Uveal Biologically distinct; metastasizes to liver first . Localized: plaque radiation or enucleation. Metastatic: liver-directed therapy (HAI, TACE, radioembolization, ablation); † tebentafusp if HLA-A*02:01 † Desmoplastic Usually BRAF wild-type with very high TMB — unusually responsive to anti-PD-1. SLNB value is debated in pure desmoplastic disease † Lentigo maligna Margin assessment is difficult (subclinical extension); imiquimod or radiation if not a surgical candidate † In-transit disease Isolated limb infusion or perfusion, T-VEC, intralesional therapy, or systemic therapy † Unknown primary Treat by stage as though cutaneous — outcomes are similar or better † Surveillance (NCCN) Stage IA–IIA: H&P q6–12 months × 5 years, then annually; no routine imaging Stage IIB–IV: H&P q3–6 months × 2 years, then q3–12 months × 3 years; imaging q3–12 months for 2–3 years Annual skin examination for life , plus education on skin self-examination and sun protection Pseudoprogression: immunotherapy responses can be slow with transient worsening before shrinkage — especially with ipilimumab-containing regimens. † iRECIST requires confirmatory imaging before calling progression † Hereditary predisposition CDKN2A / p16 Familial melanoma — also confers pancreatic cancer risk BAP1 Uveal melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cell carcinoma, cutaneous melanocytic tumors MC1R variants Red hair and fair skin phenotype; modest risk modifier

docs.title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (PV / ET / PMF)
docs.subtitle: Philadelphia-negative MPNs driven by constitutive JAK-STAT activation (JAK2 V617F, CALR, MPL) · shared risks are thrombosis, progression to myelofibrosis, and blast-phase transformation
docs.text: Myeloproliferative neoplasms — PV, ET, PMF Philadelphia-negative MPNs driven by constitutive JAK-STAT activation ( JAK2 V617F, CALR, MPL ) · shared risks are thrombosis , progression to myelofibrosis , and blast-phase transformation No Stanford handbook chapter — compiled from WHO 2022 / ICC criteria, NCCN MPN guidelines, and landmark trials. Verify against primary sources before acting. Driver mutations Driver PV ET PMF JAK2 V617F ~95% 50–60% ~60% JAK2 exon 12 ~3% — — CALR — 20–25% 25–30% MPL — 3–5% 5–8% Triple-negative — 10–15% ~10% PV is essentially always JAK2-mutated — a JAK2-negative erythrocytosis should send you back to the differential, not to a PV diagnosis. In ET, CALR predicts higher platelets but lower thrombosis risk than JAK2. Mutation biology All three drivers converge on JAK-STAT — JAK inhibitors work irrespective of which one is present JAK2 V617F — exon 14 pseudokinase (JH2) domain ; relieves autoinhibition → ligand-independent signaling. Homozygosity via 9p uniparental disomy is common in PV/PMF, rare in ET; higher allele burden tracks with PV phenotype, pruritus and fibrotic progression JAK2 exon 12 — ~3% of PV: isolated erythrocytosis , younger, very low EPO; outcomes similar to V617F CALR — exon 9 frameshift; the mutant C-terminus loses the KDEL ER-retention motif and instead activates MPL — which is exactly why CALR occurs in ET and PMF but never in PV . Type 1 (del52) predominates in PMF and is favorable; type 2 (ins5) in ET MPL W515L/K — exon 10 TPO receptor; ET and PMF only. Triple-negative — worst prognosis in PMF Diagnostic anchors (WHO 2022) PV: Hb >16.5 (M) / >16.0 (F) or Hct >49% (M) / >48% (F) + trilineage hypercellularity with pleomorphic megakaryocytes + JAK2 mutation; subnormal EPO is a minor criterion ET: platelets ≥450 ×10 9 /L + large hyperlobulated (“staghorn”) megakaryocytes + reticulin ≤ grade 1 + a clonal marker, having excluded other MPNs PMF: megakaryocyte atypia with dense clustering + fibrosis grade (prefibrotic vs overt) + leukoerythroblastosis, anemia, splenomegaly, ↑LDH The hardest and highest-stakes distinction is prefibrotic PMF vs ET. They look alike on counts, but prefibrotic PMF has materially worse survival and higher transformation risk. It turns on marrow morphology — megakaryocyte clustering and atypia — not on the CBC. Masked PV: concurrent iron deficiency can normalize the hematocrit. If JAK2 is mutated with a “normal” Hct, think PV. Splanchnic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari, portal vein) — test JAK2 in everyone, even with normal counts; MPN is a leading occult cause. Treatment pathway Polycythemia vera All patients phlebotomy to Hct <45% (CYTO-PV) aspirin 81 mg + cardiovascular risk control do not replace iron — it defeats the target High risk — age ≥60 or prior thrombosis cytoreduce: ropeginterferon (NCCN-preferred) or hydroxyurea; peg-IFN alfa-2a alternative HU-resistant/intolerant: ruxolitinib (RESPONSE) phlebotomy-dependent: rusfertide (VERIFY) Essential thrombocythemia Low / very low risk aspirin 81 mg — consider BID if JAK2+ or CV RFs observation reasonable if very low risk check vWF activity if platelets >1000 High risk — prior thrombosis, or >60 + JAK2+ cytoreduce: hydroxyurea first line anagrelide second line (PT-1) interferon preferred in pregnancy / young Primary myelofibrosis Risk-stratify first DIPSS / DIPSS-plus, MIPSS70+ v2, GIPSS allogeneic transplant is the only cure refer intermediate-2 / high risk if eligible Spleen and symptom directed ruxolitinib first line — most survival data platelets <50: pacritinib anemia / transfusion-dependent: momelotinib after ruxolitinib: fedratinib Risk stratification Disease Scheme PV High risk = age ≥60 OR prior thrombosis ; low risk = neither. High risk (or symptomatic/progressive) triggers cytoreduction ET IPSET-thrombosis (revised): very low = ≤60, no thrombosis, JAK2 WT · low = ≤60, no thrombosis, JAK2-mutant · intermediate = >60, no thrombosis, JAK2 WT · high = prior thrombosis, or >60 AND JAK2-mutant PMF IPSS (at diagnosis) · DIPSS / DIPSS-plus (any time) · MIPSS70 / MIPSS70+ v2 (molecular; transplant candidates) · GIPSS (genetic only) Non-driver mutations set prognosis, not diagnosis. High-molecular-risk in PMF: ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2, U2AF1 Q157 — these drive the MIPSS scores and push toward transplant. TP53 drives blast-phase transformation. Agents & dosing Agent Dose Setting Aspirin 81 mg daily; BID if JAK2+ or high-risk ET all PV, most ET Hydroxyurea 500–1000 mg daily, titrated to counts 1st-line cytoreduction Ropeginterferon alfa-2b 100 µg SQ q2wk (50 if switching from HU); titrate by 50 to max 500 NCCN-preferred 1st-line PV Peginterferon alfa-2a 45–180 µg SQ weekly alternative; pregnancy Rusfertide (Mimrylo) weekly SQ, dose-titrated PV erythrocytosis, phlebotomy-dependent Anagrelide 0.5 mg BID, titrate 2nd-line ET Ruxolitinib PV 10 mg BID · MF 5–20 mg BID by platelet count HU-resistant PV; 1st-line MF Fedratinib 400 mg daily MF after ruxolitinib Pacritinib 200 mg BID MF, platelets <50 Momelotinib 200 mg daily MF with anemia (also anti-ACVR1) Fedratinib requires thiamine — check and replete before and during treatment (Wernicke encephalopathy). Never stop ruxolitinib abruptly — cytokine rebound/withdrawal syndrome; taper. Complications & pearls Acquired von Willebrand syndrome with extreme thrombocytosis (>1000–1500) — paradoxical bleeding . Check ristocetin cofactor before starting aspirin; hold aspirin if severely reduced CYTO-PV: Hct target <45% gave ~4× fewer cardiovascular deaths and major thromboses than a 45–50% target — the number to defend Post-PV / post-ET myelofibrosis (IWG-MRT criteria) — suspect with rising LDH, falling counts, enlarging spleen, new constitutional symptoms Blast phase (≥20% blasts) is dismal and chemo-refractory — allogeneic transplant is the only meaningful option Aquagenic pruritus in PV — antihistamines, SSRIs, interferon, or ruxolitinib (a genuine quality-of-life issue, not a nuisance) Anemia in MF: ESAs if EPO <500, danazol, luspatercept, or switch to momelotinib

docs.title: Neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NET)
docs.subtitle: Managed on two axes: differentiation (well-differentiated NET vs poorly differentiated NEC) and grade (Ki-67 / mitotic count) · then modified by primary site and whether the tumor is functional
docs.text: Neuroendocrine tumors — gastroenteropancreatic Managed on two axes: differentiation (well-differentiated NET vs poorly differentiated NEC) and grade (Ki-67 / mitotic count) · then modified by primary site and whether the tumor is functional Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Neuroendocrine Tumors (GI section) · AJCC 8th · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter WHO classification Grade Differentiation Ki-67 Mitoses /10 HPF 1 — low Well-differentiated 0–<3% <2 2 — intermediate Well-differentiated 3–20% 2–20 3 — high Well-differentiated >20% >20 3 — high Poorly differentiated >20% >20 Grade is the higher of Ki-67 or mitotic count. Poorly differentiated = neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) ; well differentiated = NET . Well-differentiated G3 is a distinct sub-group — well-differentiated histology with Ki-67 >20%, and its behavior varies widely. It is not the same as NEC. Mixed neuroendocrine + adenocarcinoma = MANEC . “Carcinoid” is the older term for NET. Gastric NET types Type Gastrin % Setting 1 ↑ 70–80% Autoimmune atrophic gastritis ; elderly, female, pernicious anemia 2 ↑ 5–8% Gastrin-secreting tumor — MEN1, Zollinger-Ellison 3 normal 20% Solitary nodule >1.5 cm, healthy gastric mucosa ; usually symptomatic Type applies to gastric NETs only . Check gastrin at baseline and on follow-up for gastric primaries. Site-specific points Frequency: GI tract > lung > other . Most are sporadic; a minority arise in MEN1/MEN2 Small bowel: the classic carcinoid-syndrome primary (with lung); consider resecting the mesenteric mass prophylactically to avoid future complications Pancreatic: broadest baseline hormone panel; sunitinib is approved here only ; CAPTEM and temozolomide data are in pancreatic G1–G2 Carcinoid syndrome: small bowel and lung primaries with elevated serotonin — flushing is the archetypal functional symptom. If the tumor is functional, somatostatin analogue therapy is indefinite † Telotristat and carcinoid crisis are not addressed in this chapter Staging follows AJCC 8th by primary site (stomach, small bowel/ampulla, pancreas, colon/rectum) Treatment pathway Localized / resectable Resect the primary if possible there is no role for adjuvant therapy in NETs small bowel: also resect the mesenteric mass Low-burden, unresectable, non-functional watch and wait is acceptable Advanced well-differentiated NET (G1–G2) Start with a somatostatin analogue octreotide LAR 30 mg IM or lanreotide 120 mg SQ every 4 weeks — PROMID, CLARINET antitumor and hormonal control Then by site and burden PRRT Lu-177 dotatate (NETTER-1) everolimus any site · sunitinib pancreatic only cabozantinib pancreatic and extrapancreatic Pancreatic G1–G2 CAPTEM (PFS 23.2 mo) or temozolomide (15.1 mo) cap at ~12 months Liver-dominant disease chemoembolization · radioembolization bland embolization · microwave ablation Ki-67 >20% — well-diff G3 or NEC Treat as an aggressive tumor FOLFOX or CAPOX cisplatin/etoposide or carboplatin/etoposide ipilimumab + nivolumab is an option But G3 NET is not NEC well-differentiated G3 behaves variably NETTER-2 enrolled high-risk G2–G3 GEP-NETs Regimens & dosing Agent / regimen Dosing Schedule Octreotide LAR 30 mg IM q4 weeks Lanreotide 120 mg deep subcutaneous q4 weeks Lu-177 dotatate (Lutathera) 7.4 GBq (200 mCi) IV q8 weeks × 4 doses Everolimus 10 mg PO daily continuous Sunitinib 37.5 mg PO daily — pancreatic NET only continuous Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily continuous CAPTEM capecitabine 750 mg/m² PO BID d1–14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² PO d10–14 q28d, ≤12 months Temozolomide alone 200 mg/m² PO d1–5 q28d, ≤12 months FOLFOX 5-FU 1200 mg/m²/day CIV 48 h + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² d1 q14d CAPOX capecitabine 850 mg/m² PO BID d1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² d1 q21d Cisplatin / etoposide cisplatin 60 mg/m² d1 + etoposide 100 mg/m² d1–3 q21d Carboplatin / etoposide carboplatin AUC 5 d1 + etoposide 100 mg/m² d1–3 q21d Ipilimumab + nivolumab ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6wk + nivolumab 240 mg q2wk as above Pre-medicate temozolomide with ondansetron 8 mg PO 30 minutes prior . Temozolomide-containing regimens are typically capped at ~12 months. Workup — imaging & genetics Multiphasic CT or MRI; for liver metastases, MRI with Eovist may help Ga-68 DOTATATE PET at baseline, then every 2 years , or for a specific clinical question — not a routine restaging scan Endoscopy as indicated Brain MRI only for poorly differentiated disease with symptoms or raised suspicion MR spine for symptoms, or considered annually for axial bone metastases Genetics referral if diagnosed <50 years , family history suggesting MEN1/MEN2 , or a somatic NGS finding with germline implications (BRCA1/2, MEN1, Lynch genes) Biochemical workup by site Primary Baseline / pre-op Follow-up Pancreatic Chromogranin A · gastrin · glucagon · insulin/proinsulin · NSE · pancreatic polypeptide · VIP · 24-h urine 5-HIAA . As indicated: PTHrP, ACTH, GHRH Chromogranin A, NSE, and only those elevated at baseline Small bowel / other Chromogranin A · NSE · 24-h urine 5-HIAA · gastrin if gastric primary Same panel All serum labs preferably fasting ; metastatic follow-up interval is usually q1–3 months as clinically indicated. Follow only the markers that were elevated at baseline. 24-hour urine 5-HIAA requires a 3-day serotonin-restricted diet , before and during collection. Avoid: bananas, plums, pineapple, kiwi, avocado, eggplant, tomato products, nuts (especially walnuts), coffee, tea and chocolate . Medications to avoid where feasible: cough and antihistamine preparations, antihypertensives, fluorouracil, MAO inhibitors, acetaminophen, aspirin, melphalan — weigh risks and benefits before stopping anything essential . Monitoring on therapy On somatostatin analogues: check vitamin B12, vitamin D and TSH at least annually SSA adverse effects: injection-site pain, abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, gallstones , hyper- or hypoglycemia, pancreatic exocrine insufficiency Everolimus: stomatitis, rash, fatigue, diarrhea, infection, elevated lipids, pneumonitis Sunitinib: diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, stomatitis, rash Cabozantinib: hypertension, fatigue, diarrhea, hand-foot syndrome, thromboembolic events Trial evidence PROMID octreotide — TTP 14.3 vs 6 mo vs placebo (Rinke, JCO 2009) CLARINET lanreotide — PFS 38.5 mo (Caplin, NEJM 2014) NETTER-1 Lu-177 dotatate, 2nd line+, G1/G2 — PFS not reached vs 8.5 mo; 2018 update median OS NR vs 27.4 mo (Strosberg, NEJM 2017) NETTER-2 Lu-177 dotatate first line , high-risk SSTR-positive G2–G3 GEP-NET — PFS 22.8 vs 8.5 mo vs high-dose octreotide. Not yet FDA approved (Singh, Lancet 2024) COMPETE Lu-177 edotreotide vs everolimus, G1/2 GEP-NET — PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 mo ; OS trending favorable, not yet significant CABINET cabozantinib — extrapancreatic PFS 8.4 vs 3.9 mo ; pancreatic 13.8 vs 4.4 mo (Chan, NEJM 2024) RADIANT-3 everolimus, pancreatic — PFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo (Yao, NEJM 2011) RADIANT-4 everolimus, non-functional GI/lung — PFS 11.0 vs 3.9 mo (Yao, Lancet 2015) Sunitinib pancreatic NET only — PFS 11.4 vs 5.5 mo (Raymond, NEJM 2011) CAPTEM (E2211) pancreatic G1/G2 — PFS 23.2 mo vs temozolomide alone 15.1 mo (Kunz, JCO 2022) Pearls & caveats Grade is the higher of Ki-67 or mitotic count — not an average, and not Ki-67 alone Well-differentiated G3 is not NEC. Same Ki-67 threshold, different disease, and behavior varies widely There is no role for adjuvant therapy in NETs — resect and observe Sunitinib is pancreatic-only. CAPTEM and temozolomide data are also pancreatic G1–G2. Cabozantinib is the one with both pancreatic and extrapancreatic data Ga-68 DOTATATE PET is not a routine restaging scan — baseline, q2 years, or a specific question Follow only the tumor markers that were elevated at baseline NETTER-2 (first-line PRRT in G2–G3) is not FDA approved yet ; COMPETE's OS is not yet significant † The chapter is GEP-NET focused — lung/bronchial carcinoid, thymic NET and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma are separate entities not covered here

docs.title: Non-small cell lung cancer
docs.subtitle: Adenocarcinoma · squamous · large cell · TNM 9th edition (Jan 2025) · the driver landscape moves faster than any printed card — re-check NCCN at every new diagnosis
docs.text: Non-small cell lung cancer Adenocarcinoma · squamous · large cell · TNM 9th edition (Jan 2025) · the driver landscape moves faster than any printed card — re-check NCCN at every new diagnosis Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, NSCLC (Salter A, Roy M) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. Workup Chest CT with contrast (nodes are far easier to call with contrast) Brain MRI with contrast for every stage except IA — PET never substitutes for it PET/CT for distant disease (or CT C/A/P + bone scan if unavailable) Biopsy: EBUS, CT-guided transthoracic, metastatic site, or pleural cytology. Non-decalcified cores preferred for molecular Pathologic mediastinal nodal evaluation for non-metastatic disease, especially stage II–III. EBUS reaches 2R/2L, 4R/4L, 7, 10, 11; mediastinoscopy cannot reach stations 5–6 (needs a Chamberlain procedure) PD-L1 in every case. Molecular sequencing in all adenocarcinoma; add for squamous if never/light smoker, small biopsy, or adenosquamous Stage IIIB or IV: concurrent tissue + liquid molecular testing (ctDNA ~7-day turnaround). A negative liquid biopsy does not rule out a driver — confirm on tissue Staging — TNM 9th (Jan 2025) Definition T1 / T2 ≤3 cm / >3–5 cm, or visceral pleura, adjacent lobe, or main bronchus T3 / T4 >5–7 cm or chest wall, phrenic nerve, same-lobe nodule / >7 cm or mediastinum, great vessels, carina, esophagus, spine, different ipsilateral lobe N1 / N2 / N3 Ipsilateral hilar (stations 10–14) / ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal — N2a single station, N2b multiple / contralateral or any supraclavicular M1a / M1b Pleural-pericardial effusion or nodules, or contralateral lung nodule / single extrathoracic met M1c1 / M1c2 Multiple mets, single organ system / multiple organ systems What changed from the 8th edition: N2 split into N2a/N2b and M1c split into M1c1/M1c2. T descriptors are unchanged. Treatment pathway Resectable — stage I to III Decide resectability FIRST before any neoadjuvant therapy, at tumor board systemic therapy if stage I >4 cm, stage II, stage III Perioperative immunotherapy CheckMate 816 (neoadjuvant only) · KEYNOTE-671 AEGEAN · CheckMate 77T (perioperative) omit IO if EGFR / ALK / RET / ROS1 altered Adjuvant (no neoadjuvant given) retest the specimen: EGFR, ALK, PD-L1 platinum doublet ×4, then IO if PD-L1 ≥1% EGFR → osimertinib ×36 mo (ADAURA) ALK → alectinib ×24 mo (ALINA) Unresectable stage III Concurrent chemoradiation non-squamous: carboplatin AUC 5 + pemetrexed squamous: cisplatin/etoposide or weekly carbo/paclitaxel Consolidation durvalumab within 6 weeks, ×12 months (PACIFIC) EGFR-mutant: osimertinib instead (LAURA) — PFS 39.1 vs 5.6 months , HR 0.16 Metastatic Wait for molecular results do not start systemic therapy until they return IO before excluding a driver worsens outcomes if severely symptomatic: 1–2 cycles platinum, then tailor Then treat by result driver positive → targeted therapy , whatever the PD-L1 PD-L1 ≥50%, no driver → single-agent IO any PD-L1 → platinum doublet + pembrolizumab Oligometastatic (≤3–5 sites) local consolidative therapy (SBRT or surgery) to all sites, plus systemic therapy — improves PFS and OS Screening USPSTF 2021 (Grade B): annual low-dose CT , age 50–80 , ≥20 pack-years , currently smoking or quit within 15 years Stop at 15 years since cessation , or when comorbidity would preclude curative surgery NLST: 20% reduction in lung-cancer mortality vs chest radiography · NELSON: 24% in men (the women's subgroup did not reach significance) Smoking cessation remains the highest-yield intervention — duration of smoking matters more than pack count Histology Type Features Adenocarcinoma ~50%; peripheral, non/light smokers. TTF-1, napsin A, CK7 positive. Highest yield for actionable drivers. Mucinous (TTF-1−) is KRAS-enriched and EGFR-poor Squamous ~25%; central, cavitating, heavy smokers. CK5/6, p40 / p63 ; keratin pearls and intercellular bridges. Pemetrexed and bevacizumab are both contraindicated Large cell Diagnosis of exclusion — treat as non-squamous Adenosquamous Both components, each ≥10% of the tumor Early stage — surgery and radiation Lobectomy + mediastinal nodal sampling or dissection is the standard; VATS preferred over thoracotomy Sublobar resection is acceptable for peripheral cT1aN0 ≤2 cm , after intraoperative nodal confirmation. CALGB 140503: non-inferior DFS (HR 1.01). JCOG0802: segmentectomy gave superior 5-yr OS (94.3% vs 91.1%) but doubled local relapse (10.5% vs 5.4%), and the survival gain came from non-lung-cancer deaths — read it as tolerability, not better cancer control SBRT for medically inoperable stage I. Avoid central SBRT within 2 cm of the proximal bronchial tree Preoperative assessment: predicted postoperative FEV1 and DLCO ; <30% predicted flags high surgical risk Driver → therapy Alteration First line and beyond EGFR ex19del / L858R ~15% US adeno Osimertinib 80 mg daily (FLAURA). Add carbo/pemetrexed ×4 for higher-risk disease — CNS involvement, L858R, TP53 co-mutation (FLAURA2: mPFS 25.5 vs 16.7 mo ; OS 47.5 vs 37.6). Or amivantamab + lazertinib (MARIPOSA: mPFS 23.7 vs 16.6 mo , HR 0.70; OS HR 0.75 ) — but grade ≥3 AEs 80% vs 52% , and it needs VTE prophylaxis for 4 months EGFR exon 20 ins ~10% of EGFR Resistant to osimertinib and the classic TKIs. 1L amivantamab + carboplatin/pemetrexed (PAPILLON: mPFS 11.4 vs 6.7 mo , HR 0.40). Post-platinum: sunvozertinib (accelerated, 2L+ only ). Mobocertinib was withdrawn in 2023 ALK ~3–7% Lorlatinib 100 mg daily (CROWN: 5-yr PFS 60% vs 8% vs crizotinib, median not reached — the longest single-agent PFS reported in any solid tumor). Watch CNS effects (mood, cognition, seizures) and hyperlipidemia . Alternatives: alectinib, brigatinib, ensartinib ROS1 ~1–2% Four co-preferred 1L agents: crizotinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib, taletrectinib. Prefer entrectinib / repotrectinib / taletrectinib if brain metastases — crizotinib has no CNS activity. Repotrectinib TKI-naive ORR 79%, mPFS 35.7 mo. Alectinib has no ROS1 activity despite its ALK potency RET ~1–2% Selpercatinib — the only randomized 1L evidence (LIBRETTO-431: mPFS 24.8 vs 11.2 mo vs chemo ± pembrolizumab, HR 0.47; intracranial ORR 82%). Pralsetinib is an alternative with more pneumonitis. Watch hypertension and transaminitis MET exon 14 ~3–4%, older never-smokers Capmatinib (1L ORR 68%) or tepotinib (1L ORR ~57%) — both single-arm, so those two numbers are not comparable . Tepotinib: watch peripheral edema BRAF V600E ~2%, smokers Encorafenib + binimetinib (PHAROS, treatment-naive ORR 75%) or dabrafenib + trametinib (ORR 64%, mPFS 10.9 mo). Pyrexia is the classic combination toxicity — hold and dose-modify KRAS G12C ~13% of adeno Not a first-line target — 1L is chemo-IO. 2L after platinum + anti-PD-(L)1: adagrasib (KRYSTAL-12: mPFS 5.5 vs 3.8 mo, HR 0.58) or sotorasib (CodeBreaK 200: 5.6 vs 4.5 mo, no OS difference ; still on accelerated approval after a failed confirmatory filing — the weakest evidence base on this page) HER2 (ERBB2) mutant ~2–3%, non-smoker women Mostly exon 20 insertions; high rate of brain metastases at presentation . Zongertinib — oral, and as of Feb 2026 it carries a 1L indication (treatment-naive ORR 76%). T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3wk (DESTINY-Lung02: ORR 49%) — ILD in 13–15%, including fatal cases ; monitor with serial imaging NTRK fusion <1% Larotrectinib, entrectinib or repotrectinib — all tumor-agnostic approvals NRG1 fusion Zenocutuzumab — accelerated approval, after progression on prior systemic therapy , for NSCLC and pancreatic adenocarcinoma only Progression on osimertinib Rebiopsy — resistance is heterogeneous, with no single dominant mechanism On-target: EGFR C797S . Off-target: MET amplification, HER2 amplification, acquired fusions Histologic transformation is the one you cannot afford to miss: SCLC transformation (with RB1 and TP53 loss) or squamous transformation. Treat SCLC transformation as SCLC — platinum/etoposide Standard next step is platinum-doublet chemotherapy Amivantamab + chemotherapy (MARIPOSA-2: mPFS 6.3 vs 4.2 mo, HR 0.48). The approved regimen is amivantamab + chemo only — the lazertinib triplet was not approved, for excess hematologic toxicity Datopotamab deruxtecan — TROP2 ADC on accelerated approval. The label is EGFR-mutant-specific : the all-comers trial met PFS but missed OS Driver-negative metastatic PD-L1 ≥50%: pembrolizumab monotherapy (KEYNOTE-024: OS 30 vs 14 months); atezolizumab or cemiplimab are alternatives. Use chemo-IO instead if the burden is high or the patient is symptomatic PD-L1 1–49% or <1%: chemo-IO doublet. Non-squamous → pembrolizumab + carboplatin + pemetrexed (KEYNOTE-189). Squamous → pembrolizumab + carboplatin + paclitaxel (KEYNOTE-407) Dual IO — ipilimumab/nivolumab (CheckMate 227, 9LA) or durvalumab/tremelimumab (POSEIDON): chemo-sparing but more toxic, most attractive at PD-L1 <1% and in squamous Second line: docetaxel 35 mg/m² days 1+8 — split dosing is better tolerated than 75 q3wk — ± ramucirumab Adjuvant therapy Cisplatin doublet ×4 for stage II–IIIA (LACE: ~5% absolute 5-yr OS gain). Stage IB only if ≥4 cm or high-risk features ; no benefit and possible harm in stage IA EGFR → osimertinib ×36 months (ADAURA: DFS HR 0.17, OS HR 0.49). ALK → alectinib ×24 months (ALINA: DFS HR 0.24). Omit IO in both Atezolizumab (IMpower010) is approved for stage II–IIIA with PD-L1 ≥1% , EGFR/ALK wild-type — but the 2025 update showed no significant OS benefit overall , with the signal concentrated at PD-L1 ≥50% Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-091) after adjuvant chemotherapy, no PD-L1 restriction : DFS HR 0.76 overall — yet the PD-L1 ≥50% subgroup was not significant , the reverse of what you would predict Perioperative and adjuvant dosing Regimen Dosing CheckMate 816 neoadjuvant only Cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² (or gemcitabine 1250 d1+8) + nivolumab 360 mg on day 1 — q21d ×3 , then surgery KEYNOTE-671 perioperative Cisplatin 75 + pemetrexed 500 (or gemcitabine 1000 d1+8) + pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×4 → surgery → within 12 weeks, pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×13 AEGEAN perioperative Cisplatin 75 + pemetrexed 500 (or gemcitabine 1250 d1+8) + durvalumab 1500 mg q21d ×4 → surgery → durvalumab 1500 mg q28d ×12 CheckMate 77T perioperative Cisplatin 75 + pemetrexed 500 (or docetaxel 75) + nivolumab 360 mg q21d ×4 → surgery → within 90 days, nivolumab 360 mg q28d ×1 year Adjuvant chemo Cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 (non-squamous), gemcitabine 1250 d1+8, or docetaxel 75 — q21d ×4 . Growth factor support if using docetaxel Adjuvant IO Atezolizumab 1680 mg q4wk or pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk , after adjuvant chemotherapy Chemoradiation and metastatic dosing Regimen Dosing ChemoRT non-squamous Carboplatin AUC 5 + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² q21d ×4, with daily RT ChemoRT squamous Cisplatin 50 mg/m² days 1, 8, 29, 36 + etoposide 50 mg/m² days 1–5 and 29–33 ; or carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 45 mg/m² weekly — with daily RT Consolidation durvalumab 10 mg/kg q14d ×12 months (or 1500 mg q4wk). Start within 6 weeks of finishing chemoRT Platinum doublet + IO Carboplatin AUC 5–6 + pemetrexed 500 (non-squamous) or paclitaxel 200 (squamous) + pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×4 → pemetrexed + pembrolizumab maintenance Single-agent IO Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk (or 400 q6wk) · atezolizumab 1200 mg q3wk · cemiplimab 350 mg q3wk Osimertinib + chemo FLAURA2 Carboplatin AUC 6 + pemetrexed 500 q21d ×4, with osimertinib 80 mg daily continuously , then pemetrexed maintenance Amivantamab + lazertinib Amivantamab weight-based ( <80 kg 1050 mg , ≥80 kg 1400 mg ) — split over days 1–2 in week 1, weekly through week 5, then q2wk from week 7 ; + lazertinib 240 mg PO daily . VTE prophylaxis ×4 months Docetaxel, 2L 35 mg/m² days 1+8 q21d — preferred over 75 q21d; reduce to 30 or 25 if heavily pretreated. ± ramucirumab 10 mg/kg Pemetrexed maintenance 500 mg/m² q21d — non-squamous only Monitoring and cautions Baseline HBsAg + anti-HBc before any immunosuppressive therapy ; consider quantitative TB testing by risk Pemetrexed: folic acid from ≥1 week before until 3 weeks after · B12 1000 mcg q9wk · dexamethasone 4 mg BID the day before and after, for rash. Never in squamous Bevacizumab: contraindicated in squamous histology, significant hemoptysis, and large cavitary tumors. Urine protein every other cycle; treat hypertension Cisplatin: avoid with hearing loss, CrCl <30, severe neuropathy, or poor performance status. Extensive hydration and aprepitant-containing antiemetics Osimertinib: echo at baseline and q3 months ×6 months; ECG at baseline, 2 weeks, 6 weeks, and with any QT-prolonging drug Alectinib: CK at baseline, 2 weeks, then q3 months · LFTs q2 weeks ×3 months. Lorlatinib: CNS effects and hyperlipidemia — median onset 15 days ; rosuvastatin first-line Immunotherapy: TSH and free T4 at baseline then q4–6 weeks. Prednisone 1–1.5 mg/kg for irAEs with a slow taper Do not start a targeted agent — osimertinib and crizotinib above all — within 3 months of immunotherapy ; the toxicity is additive. IO is also less effective in EGFR/ALK-driven disease Key trials CheckMate 816 Neoadjuvant platinum + nivolumab ×3 — pCR 24% vs 2%, EFS HR 0.63, OS HR 0.62 KEYNOTE-671 Perioperative pembrolizumab — EFS HR 0.58; the first perioperative IO trial with a confirmed OS benefit AEGEAN / 77T Perioperative durvalumab (EFS HR 0.68) / nivolumab (EFS HR 0.58) ADAURA / ALINA Adjuvant osimertinib ×36 mo (DFS HR 0.17, OS HR 0.49) / alectinib ×24 mo (DFS HR 0.24) PACIFIC Consolidation durvalumab after chemoRT — 5-yr OS 43% vs 33% LAURA Consolidation osimertinib, EGFR-mutant stage III — PFS 39.1 vs 5.6 mo , HR 0.16 FLAURA / FLAURA2 Osimertinib 1L; adding chemo gives mPFS 25.5 vs 16.7 mo and OS 47.5 vs 37.6 MARIPOSA Amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib — mPFS 23.7 vs 16.6 mo, OS HR 0.75 , at a real toxicity cost CROWN Lorlatinib 1L in ALK — 5-yr PFS 60% vs 8% PAPILLON Amivantamab + chemo 1L for EGFR exon 20 — mPFS 11.4 vs 6.7 mo LIBRETTO-431 Selpercatinib vs chemo ± pembrolizumab in RET — mPFS 24.8 vs 11.2 mo CALGB 140503 Sublobar resection non-inferior for peripheral cT1aN0 ≤2 cm — DFS HR 1.01

docs.title: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
docs.subtitle: >90% of pancreatic cancers (PNET <5%) · median age 71 · 60–70% arise in the head · 5-yr relative survival — localized 44%, regional 16%, distant 3%; 13% all stages, 8% for adenocarcinoma
docs.text: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma >90% of pancreatic cancers (PNET <5%) · median age 71 · 60–70% arise in the head · 5-yr relative survival — localized 44% , regional 16% , distant 3% ; 13% all stages, 8% for adenocarcinoma Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Pancreatic Cancer (Johnson T, Lee W) · NCCN v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup — all patients Pancreatic-protocol CT chest/abdomen/pelvis — required for staging and resectability EUS with biopsy if clinically indicated MRI for indeterminate liver lesions or local extent Labs: CBC, CMP, baseline CA 19-9 Germline testing in ALL patients regardless of family history — ~10% harbor a mutation Tumor genomic profiling in all metastatic patients Manage at a high-volume center with multidisciplinary input Presentation Early: weight loss, nausea, bloating, abdominal pain “Painless jaundice” is common but by no means universal † New-onset diabetes in an older adult; migratory thrombophlebitis † CA 19-9 pitfalls: falsely elevated by biliary obstruction — recheck after decompression; 5–10% are Lewis-antigen negative and never secrete it Staging — AJCC 8th T1 / T2 / T3 ≤2 cm / >2–4 cm / >4 cm T4 celiac axis, SMA, or common hepatic artery — regardless of size N1 / N2 1–3 nodes / ≥4 nodes Stage III / IV T4 or N2 / M1 In practice resectability — not TNM — drives management: resectable · borderline · unresectable localized · metastatic. The call belongs to a hepatobiliary surgeon experienced with the Whipple. Key trials PRODIGE-24 adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX — OS 54.4 vs 35.0 mo (NEJM 2018) ESPAC-4 adjuvant gem + capecitabine (Lancet 2017) PRODIGE-4 FOLFIRINOX in metastatic disease (NEJM 2011) MPACT gem + nab-paclitaxel (NEJM 2013) POLO olaparib maintenance, germline BRCA (NEJM 2019) KEYNOTE-158 pembrolizumab in MSI-H (JCO 2020) RASolute 302 daraxonrasib, 2L metastatic — median OS 13.2 vs 6.6 mo in RAS G12-mutant (NEJM 2026) Treatment pathway Resectable or borderline Neoadjuvant chemotherapy FOLFIRINOX strongly preferred gem + nab-paclitaxel if PS limits no RCT vs adjuvant — see note below Surgery resection at a high-volume center Adjuvant chemotherapy mFOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE-24) preferred gem + capecitabine if moderate PS start ≤12 wk; 6 months total perioperative Surveillance see surveillance panel at right Unresectable or metastatic First line by performance status robust PS: FOLFIRINOX or NALIRIFOX moderate PS: gem + nab-paclitaxel poor PS: single agent gem, 5-FU, capecitabine Maintenance olaparib if germline BRCA1/2, no progression after 16 wk platinum (POLO) Second line RAS G12-mutant (~90%): daraxonrasib OS 13.2 vs 6.6 mo (RASolute 302) otherwise switch backbone Biomarker-directed therapy see biomarker table at right Neoadjuvant therapy has no RCT support. No prospective trial shows it beats adjuvant therapy; use is extrapolated from PRODIGE-24 and justified because it identifies bad biology before a morbid operation and gives early systemic control. Two comparisons never made head-to-head: adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/capecitabine, and first-line metastatic mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/nab-paclitaxel — choose by performance status . Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Cycle FOLFIRINOX oxaliplatin 85 · irinotecan 150 · 5-FU 1200/day CIV d1–2 q14d NALIRIFOX 5-FU 1200 d1–2 · liposomal irinotecan 50 · oxaliplatin 60 q14d Gem + nab-paclitaxel gemcitabine 1000 + nab-paclitaxel 125, d1, 8, 15 q28d Gem + capecitabine gemcitabine 1000 d1, 8, 15 + capecitabine 850 BID d1–21 q28d Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² PO BID d1–14 q21d 5-FU 1200 mg/m²/day CIV d1–2 q14d All doses mg/m² unless stated. PRODIGE-24 used irinotecan 180 mg/m², reduced to 150 mg/m² — preplanned subgroup analysis showed equal efficacy . Biomarker → therapy Alteration Therapy RAS G12 mutation (~90% of PDAC) Daraxonrasib — oral multi-selective RAS(ON) inhibitor; metastatic disease after ≥1 prior line, or not a candidate for multiagent therapy Germline BRCA1/2 Olaparib 300 mg PO BID — maintenance after ≥16 wk platinum (POLO) MSI-H / dMMR / TMB >10 Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk NRG1 fusion Zenocutuzumab (Bizengri) 750 mg IV q2wk BRAF V600E Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg daily NTRK fusion Entrectinib 600 daily · larotrectinib 100 BID · repotrectinib 160 RET fusion Selpercatinib 120 mg BID (<50 kg) or 160 mg BID (≥50 kg) Actionable alterations were historically rare — daraxonrasib changes that , since ~90% of PDAC is KRAS-mutant. Still profile every metastatic patient for the remainder. Surveillance after resection H&P q3–6 months × 2 years , then q6–12 months CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast q3–6 months × 2 years, then q6–12 months CA 19-9 q3–6 months × 2 years Signatera or equivalent ctDNA q3–6 months if indicated Supportive care Nutrition referral · palliative care for all metastatic patients · hospice as appropriate † Pancreatic enzyme replacement (PERT) — chronically underprescribed; exocrine insufficiency drives weight loss and treatment intolerance † VTE prophylaxis — among the highest-risk malignancies for thrombosis † Biliary stenting for obstruction · celiac plexus neurolysis for refractory pain

docs.title: Prostate cancer
docs.subtitle: Managed on two axes — extent (localized → PSA-only → metastatic) crossed with castration status (sensitive vs resistant, testosterone <50 ng/dL). Test every metastatic patient for germline + somatic HRR — it now changes therapy in mHSPC as well as mCRPC
headings: mCRPC — PARP inhibitors: trial vs FDA label
docs.text: Prostate cancer Managed on two axes — extent (localized → PSA-only → metastatic) crossed with castration status (sensitive vs resistant, testosterone <50 ng/dL). Test every metastatic patient for germline + somatic HRR — it now changes therapy in mHSPC as well as mCRPC Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Prostate Cancer (Chien J, Parikh D, Srinivas S) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026. Screening & diagnosis USPSTF (Grade C): shared decision on PSA at 55–69 ; not recommended ≥70. Consider starting at 40–45 for Black men and BRCA2 carriers Pre-biopsy multiparametric MRI (PI-RADS) → targeted biopsy. PRECISION: clinically significant cancer 38% vs 26% vs standard TRUS biopsy, with fewer insignificant cancers, and 28% of the MRI arm avoided biopsy Risk inputs: cT stage, Grade Group, PSA , % positive cores, PSA density. Tissue genomic classifiers (Decipher, Prolaris) can refine AS vs treatment Staging imaging by risk: none for very low / low / favorable intermediate · soft tissue ± bone for unfavorable intermediate · bone + soft tissue for high / very high PSMA PET (Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat) beats CT + bone scan. proPSMA: accuracy 92% vs 65% , fewer equivocal reads. Preferred for BCR restaging and required before Lu-PSMA Grade group & NCCN risk (localized) Grade Group GG1 ≤3+3 · GG2 3+4 · GG3 4+3 · GG4 = 8 · GG5 = 9–10 Very low All of: T1c, GG1, PSA <10, <3 cores positive (≤50% each), PSA density <0.15 Low cT1–T2a + GG1 + PSA <10, not very low Favorable interm. 1 IRF + GG1–2 + <50% cores positive Unfavorable interm. 2–3 IRFs, or GG3, or ≥50% cores positive High One of: cT3–T4, GG4–5, PSA >20 Very high ≥2 of: cT3–T4, GG4–5, PSA >40 IRF (intermediate risk factor) = cT2b–T2c, GG2–3, or PSA 10–20. Stage IVA = N1 M0; IVB = M1 (M1a non-regional nodes, M1b bone, M1c other ± bone). Localized disease Active surveillance for very low / low and selected favorable intermediate: PSA q6 mo, repeat MRI ± biopsy; treat on upgrading Definitive: radical prostatectomy or EBRT ± brachytherapy boost — similar cancer control, different toxicity (RP: incontinence, ED; RT: bowel/bladder) ADT with RT scales with risk: unfavorable intermediate 4–6 mo ; high / very high 18–36 mo (~12 mo if brachy boost). Very high or N1: add abiraterone ×2 yr (STAMPEDE) 2026 IPD meta-analysis (13 RCTs, n=10,266): benefit plateaus beyond ~9–12 mo while non-cancer death keeps rising — argues for the short end of each range Treatment pathway by disease state Localized (M0, castration-sensitive) Risk-adapted local therapy low: active surveillance interm./high: RP, or EBRT + ADT 4–6 or 18–36 mo very high / N1: EBRT + ADT + abiraterone 2 yr Biochemical recurrence (PSA only) Restage with PSMA PET, then post-RP: salvage RT ± ADT (RTOG 9601, SPPORT) high-risk BCR (PSADT ≤9 mo): enzalutamide + leuprolide (EMBARK — OS benefit, HR 0.60) nmCRPC (castrate T, rising PSA, M0) PSADT ≤10 mo → add an ARPI apalutamide, darolutamide or enzalutamide MFS gain ~2 yr, OS HR 0.69–0.78 (SPARTAN / ARAMIS / PROSPER) mHSPC (metastatic, castration-sensitive) ADT alone is never enough doublet: ADT + ARPI (abi, apa, daro, enza) high volume / de novo: triplet + docetaxel ×6 (PEACE-1, ARASENS); low volume: + RT to primary Biomarker add-ons (2025–26) BRCA2 : niraparib + abiraterone (AMPLITUDE) PTEN-deficient : capivasertib + abi (CAPItello-281) PSMA+ : Lu-PSMA + ARPI (PSMAddition) mCRPC Rotate mechanisms — test HRR first never ARPI → ARPI (CARD: cabazitaxel wins) BRCA/HRR : PARPi (+ ARPI if ARPI-naive) docetaxel → cabazitaxel · PSMA+ : Lu-PSMA bone-only symptomatic: radium-223 · MSI-H: pembro Metastatic risk definitions CHAARTED high volume Visceral mets and/or ≥4 bone lesions with ≥1 beyond the spine/pelvis LATITUDE high risk ≥2 of: Gleason ≥8, ≥3 bone lesions, measurable visceral mets Castration resistance Progression (PSA, radiographic) with testosterone <50 ng/dL — confirm the level before using the label Timing De novo (synchronous) is worse than metachronous; drives the case for triplet Volume is judged on conventional imaging (CT + bone scan) — the trials predate PSMA PET. Applying them to PSMA-only disease is unvalidated. Germline & somatic testing Germline All metastatic or N1 , high/very-high risk, BCR with high risk or family history, Ashkenazi ancestry, family history (breast, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, Lynch); consider if ≤55 or intraductal histology Frequency metastatic Germline DNA-repair mutation in 11.8% — BRCA2 5.3% (most common), CHEK2 1.9%, ATM 1.6%, BRCA1 0.9% (vs 4.6% in localized disease; independent of age / family history) Somatic HRR panel (tissue or ctDNA) in all metastatic. MSI-H/dMMR + TMB in mCRPC. PTEN IHC (companion test, 2026) in mHSPC Why it matters BRCA2 → PARP benefit is largest, and cascade testing of relatives. ATM/CDK12/CHEK2 respond poorly to PARPi mCRPC — sequencing in practice Most patients now reach mCRPC already ARPI-exposed — a second ARPI is the weakest option (CARD) ARPI-exposed: docetaxel ; PARP monotherapy if HRR/BRCA (olaparib, rucaparib); Lu-PSMA if PSMA+ (pre-taxane PSMAfore, post-taxane VISION); then cabazitaxel ARPI-naive: ARPI, adding a PARPi by genotype — BRCA: olaparib or niraparib + abiraterone; HRR: talazoparib + enzalutamide Symptomatic bone-only, no visceral disease: radium-223 · MSI-H/dMMR or TMB ≥10: pembrolizumab · asymptomatic, low burden: sipuleucel-T Pearls ADT continues indefinitely in CRPC — the AR axis is still active LHRH agonist flare: start bicalutamide ~7 days before if there is cord/obstructive risk, or use an antagonist (castrate by day 3–4) Rapid progression with disproportionately low PSA , visceral/lytic mets → suspect neuroendocrine transformation ; biopsy and treat with platinum-etoposide Localized & high-risk M0 — RT + ADT Trial Design → result RTOG 9408 RT ± 4 mo ADT, mostly intermediate risk → 10-yr OS 62% vs 57% ; benefit confined to intermediate risk EORTC 22863 RT ± 3 yr ADT, locally advanced → 10-yr OS 58% vs 40% (HR 0.60) EORTC 22961 6 mo vs 3 yr → 6 mo not non-inferior (5-yr OS 81% vs 85%) RTOG 9202 · DART Short vs long → long course wins mainly in Gleason 8–10 / high risk (9202 GS 8–10 10-yr OS 45% vs 32%) PCS IV 18 vs 36 mo , high risk → 10-yr OS 62% vs 62%; 18 mo sufficient, better QoL Zaorsky 2026 IPD 13 RCTs → optimal ADT: 0 mo for 1 IRF, 6 mo ≥2 IRFs, 12 mo high risk; gains flatten after ~9–12 mo STAMPEDE (abi M0) High-risk N0 or N1: ADT 3 yr ± abiraterone 2 yr → MFS HR 0.53 , 6-yr MFS 82% vs 69%, OS HR 0.60. Adding enzalutamide added nothing PATCH (2026) Transdermal estradiol vs LHRH , locally advanced M0 → non-inferior MFS (HR 0.96); fractures 5% vs 11%, hot flashes far fewer; gynecomastia 85% Biochemical recurrence & nmCRPC Trial Design → result RTOG 9601 Salvage RT ± bicalutamide 150 mg ×24 mo → 12-yr OS 76% vs 71% (HR 0.77); gynecomastia 70% SPPORT Salvage bed RT vs + 4–6 mo ADT vs + ADT + pelvic nodes → 5-yr freedom from progression 71% / 81% / 87% EMBARK High-risk BCR (PSADT ≤9 mo): enza + leuprolide vs leuprolide vs enza mono → 5-yr MFS 87% / 71% / 80% . Final OS (2025): combination HR 0.60 (8-yr 79% vs 70%); enzalutamide monotherapy HR 0.83, NOT significant PRESTO Post-RP BCR, 52 wk ADT ± apalutamide (± abi) → PSA-PFS 24.9 vs 20.3 mo (HR 0.52); no OS data SPARTAN nmCRPC, PSADT ≤10 mo: apalutamide → MFS 40.5 vs 16.2 mo; OS 73.9 vs 59.9 (HR 0.78) PROSPER Enzalutamide → MFS 36.6 vs 14.7 mo; OS 67.0 vs 56.3 (HR 0.73) ARAMIS Darolutamide → MFS 40.4 vs 18.4 mo; OS HR 0.69 (3-yr 83% vs 77%); least CNS toxicity EMBARK is the reason to use the combination , not enzalutamide alone, when survival is the goal; monotherapy is a compromise for a patient avoiding castration. mHSPC — doublet and triplet Trial Design → result CHAARTED ADT ± docetaxel ×6 → OS 57.6 vs 44.0 mo (HR 0.61); benefit concentrated in high volume (49.2 vs 32.2) LATITUDE High-risk de novo: + abiraterone → 3-yr OS 66% vs 49% (HR 0.62) TITAN + apalutamide , any volume → 24-mo OS 82% vs 74% (HR 0.67) ARCHES + enzalutamide → rPFS HR 0.39; OS HR 0.66 ENZAMET + enzalutamide vs + NSAA (docetaxel allowed) → 3-yr OS 80% vs 72% (HR 0.67) ARANOTE + darolutamide (no docetaxel) → rPFS HR 0.54; OS HR 0.81, not significant . FDA June 2025 PEACE-1 De novo: ADT ± docetaxel ± abiraterone ± RT → high volume OS 5.1 vs 3.5 yr with abi on top of docetaxel; RT to primary helps low volume ARASENS ADT + docetaxel ± darolutamide → OS HR 0.68 ; little added toxicity Triplet = high-volume, de novo, fit for docetaxel. No trial randomized triplet vs ARPI doublet — the triplet advantage over an ARPI doublet is inferred, not proven. mHSPC — biomarker-directed (2025–26) Trial Design → result · label AMPLITUDE HRR-altered (56% BRCA): niraparib + AAP vs AAP → rPFS HR 0.52 BRCA , 0.63 ITT; OS immature (HR 0.79). Grade 3–4 AEs 75% vs 59%, anemia 29%. FDA Dec 2025: BRCA2 only CAPItello-281 PTEN-deficient by IHC (~25%): capivasertib + AAP → rPFS 33.2 vs 25.7 mo (HR 0.81 ); OS HR 0.90, NS. Diarrhea 52%, hyperglycemia 38%, rash 35%. FDA June 2026 PSMAddition PSMA PET+: Lu-PSMA ×6 + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI → rPFS HR 0.72 ; OS immature. Dry mouth 46%. FDA July 2026 All three are rPFS wins with immature or non-significant OS and added toxicity — none yet displaces docetaxel triplet for high-volume disease. Choosing mHSPC therapy Low volume or metachronous: ADT + ARPI doublet; add RT to the prostate for low-volume de novo disease High volume, de novo, fit: triplet — docetaxel + darolutamide (ARASENS) or abiraterone (PEACE-1) Pick the ARPI by comorbidity: darolutamide for falls, cognition, seizures, polypharmacy; avoid abiraterone with uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes, liver disease; enzalutamide/apalutamide are strong CYP inducers Then check biomarkers: BRCA2 → niraparib + AAP; PTEN-deficient → capivasertib + AAP; PSMA+ → Lu-PSMA add-on mCRPC — PARP inhibitors: trial vs FDA label Trial Population → result US label PROfound Post-ARPI, HRR-selected: olaparib vs ARPI switch → BRCA/ATM rPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 (HR 0.34); OS 19.1 vs 14.7 HRR-mutated, post-ARPI TRITON2 / 3 Rucaparib : single-arm BRCA ORR 44% → TRITON3 BRCA rPFS 11.2 vs 6.4 (HR 0.50); ATM no benefit (HR 0.95) BRCA, post-ARPI; regular Dec 2025 PROpel 1L, all-comers : olaparib + abiraterone → rPFS HR 0.66 (BRCA 0.23); OS HR 0.81, NS BRCA only MAGNITUDE 1L, HRR-selected: niraparib + AAP → BRCA rPFS 16.6 vs 10.9 (HR 0.53); HRR-negative cohort stopped for futility BRCA only TALAPRO-2 1L, all-comers : talazoparib + enzalutamide → final OS 45.8 vs 37.0 (HR 0.80); HRR-def OS HR 0.62 , BRCA 0.50, non-HRR 0.88 NS HRR-mutated ; all-comers rejected (ODAC 8–0, 2025) Signal tracks BRCA2 > BRCA1 > other HRR ; non-HRR benefit is small or absent. PARP + ARPI combinations are for ARPI-naive mCRPC; after an ARPI, use PARP monotherapy. mCRPC — radioligand, bone, chemo Trial Design → result VISION PSMA+, post-ARPI + taxane: Lu-PSMA-617 → OS 15.3 vs 11.3 mo (HR 0.62) PSMAfore Post-ARPI, taxane-naive : Lu-PSMA vs ARPI switch → rPFS 12.0 vs 5.6 (HR 0.41); no OS gain (84% crossover). FDA Mar 2025 ENZA-p phase 2 Enzalutamide ± Lu-PSMA, 1L mCRPC → OS 34 vs 26 mo (HR 0.55); not approved ALSYMPCA Symptomatic bone-only: radium-223 → OS 14.9 vs 11.3 mo (HR 0.70) ERA 223 Abiraterone + radium → fractures 29% vs 11% , more deaths — unblinded early. Never combine PEACE-3 Enzalutamide + radium , bone agent mandatory → rPFS 19.4 vs 16.4 (HR 0.69); final OS HR 0.76; fractures still 24% vs 13% TAX 327 · TROPIC Docetaxel q3w OS 18.9 vs 16.5 mo (HR 0.76) · post-docetaxel cabazitaxel 15.1 vs 12.7 (HR 0.70) CARD Post-docetaxel + 1 ARPI: cabazitaxel vs 2nd ARPI → rPFS 8.0 vs 3.7, OS 13.6 vs 11.0 (HR 0.64) CONTACT-02 Cabozantinib + atezolizumab vs ARPI switch → PFS HR 0.65 but OS HR 0.89, NS ; not approved Hormonal therapy dosing Agent Dose Notes Leuprolide 7.5 / 22.5 / 30 / 45 mg IM/SQ q4 / 12 / 16 / 24 wk LHRH agonist — flare Goserelin · triptorelin 3.6 mg SQ q4wk or 10.8 q12wk · 3.75 q4wk / 11.25 q12wk Agonists Degarelix 240 mg SQ load → 80 mg SQ q4wk Antagonist, no flare; injection-site reactions Relugolix (HERO) 360 mg PO load → 120 mg PO daily Oral antagonist: sustained castration 97% vs 89%, castrate day 4 56% vs 0%, MACE 2.9% vs 6.2%. Adherence matters — T recovers fast Transdermal estradiol (PATCH) 4 × 100 µg patches twice weekly → 3 once castrate Not licensed for prostate cancer in the US Bicalutamide 50 mg daily (flare cover; with ADT) · 150 mg (RTOG 9601) First-gen antiandrogen Abiraterone 1000 mg fasting + prednisone 5 mg daily (mHSPC) or 5 mg BID (mCRPC) Low-dose option: 250 mg with a low-fat meal — non-inferior PSA decline (phase 2) at a quarter of the dose Enzalutamide 160 mg daily CYP3A4/2C9/2C19 inducer Apalutamide 240 mg daily Rash, hypothyroidism Darolutamide 600 mg BID with food Least CNS penetration Abiraterone + dexamethasone 1000 mg + dexamethasone 0.5 mg daily Steroid switch after abi/pred progression (modest PSA responses) Abiraterone 1000 mg must be taken fasting — food raises exposure several-fold, which is the basis of the low-dose-with-food option. Special situations New metastatic disease with cord compression or impending obstruction: dexamethasone + RT/surgery, and start castration with a GnRH antagonist (degarelix) or orchiectomy — never an agonist alone Neuroendocrine / small-cell transformation: platinum + etoposide, as for SCLC Check testosterone on ADT when PSA rises — not castrate means the ADT is failing, not the cancer Chemo, targeted, radioligand dosing Regimen Dose Docetaxel (mHSPC) 75 mg/m² q3wk ×6, no prednisone required (CHAARTED; PEACE-1/ARASENS triplet) Docetaxel (mCRPC) 75 mg/m² q3wk + prednisone 5 mg BID; 50 mg/m² q2wk if frail Cabazitaxel 20 mg/m² q3wk (PROSELICA non-inferior) or 25 mg/m² + prednisone; G-CSF prophylaxis Olaparib 300 mg BID ± abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisone 5 mg BID Niraparib / abiraterone 200 / 1000 mg fixed-dose tablet daily + prednisone 10 mg (mCRPC) or 5 mg (mCSPC) Talazoparib 0.5 mg daily + enzalutamide 160 mg Rucaparib 600 mg BID Capivasertib 400 mg BID, 4 days on / 3 off + abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisone Lu-177-PSMA-617 7.4 GBq IV q6wk ×up to 6 — requires PSMA PET positivity Radium-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6 (= the trials' 50 kBq/kg, re-standardized) Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk — MSI-H/dMMR or TMB ≥10 (tumor-agnostic) Sipuleucel-T 3 infusions q2wk — asymptomatic / minimally symptomatic mCRPC Bone health & supportive care ADT bone loss: denosumab 60 mg SQ q6 mo or zoledronic acid; calcium + vitamin D CRPC bone metastases: denosumab 120 mg SQ q4wk or zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q3–4 wk (q12wk acceptable) to prevent skeletal events.
