No bone agent is indicated for SRE prevention in mHSPC Before bone agents: dental evaluation (osteonecrosis of the jaw); correct calcium and vitamin D — denosumab causes hypocalcemia; renally dose zoledronic acid Hot flashes: venlafaxine, gabapentin, or medroxyprogesterone. Exercise (resistance + aerobic) counters fatigue and sarcopenia Monitoring & toxicity ADT (all): baseline DEXA , calcium + vitamin D, bone agent if osteoporotic; lipids, A1c, BP (metabolic syndrome, CV risk); hot flashes (venlafaxine, gabapentin); fatigue, sarcopenia → resistance exercise; anemia; cognition ARPIs: falls and fractures ; fatigue; hypertension. Enzalutamide/apalutamide: seizure risk — avoid with seizure history. Apalutamide: rash, TSH. Check drug interactions (enza/apa are strong inducers — DOACs, statins, immunosuppressants) Abiraterone: mineralocorticoid excess — hypokalemia, hypertension, edema ; LFTs q2wk ×3 mo then monthly ; take 1000 mg on an empty stomach PARPi: anemia (talazoparib grade ≥3 43–49%) — CBC monthly, transfuse / dose-reduce; MDS/AML rare; VTE with olaparib + abiraterone (7% vs 2%) Lu-PSMA: xerostomia (~45%), nausea, fatigue, cytopenias (CBC before each dose), renal function Radium-223: ANC ≥1.5, platelets ≥100 before first dose; not with abiraterone ; bone agent if combined with enzalutamide Capivasertib: diarrhea, hyperglycemia (fasting glucose/A1c), rash Taxanes: neutropenia, neuropathy (docetaxel), diarrhea (cabazitaxel) Key trials EMBARK Enza + leuprolide in high-risk BCR — MFS and OS HR 0.60 ; monotherapy no OS gain CHAARTED / LATITUDE Docetaxel (high volume) / abiraterone (high risk) with ADT in mHSPC PEACE-1 / ARASENS Triplet: ADT + docetaxel + abiraterone / darolutamide SPARTAN / PROSPER / ARAMIS ARPI in nmCRPC — MFS ~2 yr longer, OS HR 0.69–0.78 TALAPRO-2 Talazoparib + enza 1L mCRPC — OS HR 0.80; label HRR-only VISION / PSMAfore Lu-PSMA post-taxane (OS HR 0.62) / pre-taxane (rPFS only) CARD Cabazitaxel beats a second ARPI — OS HR 0.64 ERA 223 / PEACE-3 Radium + abiraterone harms; + enzalutamide helps with bone protection HERO Oral relugolix vs leuprolide — better castration, fewer MACE AMPLITUDE / CAPItello-281 / PSMAddition Biomarker-directed mHSPC add-ons, all approved 2025–26

docs.title: Renal cell carcinoma
docs.subtitle: Two forks decide everything — clear cell vs non-clear cell, and IMDC risk. Localized disease is surgical ± adjuvant pembrolizumab; metastatic clear cell gets an IO backbone (IO/TKI or ipi/nivo) with no predictive biomarker; after IO, switch mechanism — never re-add IO
headings: First-line clear cell — all vs sunitinib unless stated
docs.text: Renal cell carcinoma Two forks decide everything — clear cell vs non-clear cell , and IMDC risk . Localized disease is surgical ± adjuvant pembrolizumab; metastatic clear cell gets an IO backbone (IO/TKI or ipi/nivo) with no predictive biomarker; after IO, switch mechanism — never re-add IO Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, GU: Renal Cell Carcinoma (Ruiz SM, Fan AC) · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. Workup Most are found incidentally on imaging; the classic triad (flank pain, hematuria, mass) is seen in only ~10% Paraneoplastic: erythrocytosis (EPO), hypercalcemia (PTHrP), hypertension (renin), Stauffer syndrome (cholestasis without liver mets — resolves after nephrectomy) CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast (MRI if poor renal function, IVC thrombus, or to call fat in an angiomyolipoma) + chest CT . Brain MRI and bone scan when symptomatic or before systemic therapy in high-risk disease Biopsy is not required before nephrectomy for a solid enhancing mass — get it for small masses when it would change AS vs treatment, suspected lymphoma/metastasis/infection, or before systemic therapy without surgery Labs that feed IMDC: CBC with differential, calcium , plus LDH, creatinine, LFTs Genetics referral (NCCN): RCC at age ≤46 , bilateral or multifocal tumors, ≥1 first/second-degree relative with RCC, or a somatic hit with germline implications Staging (AJCC 8th) T1 Confined to kidney, ≤7 cm — T1a ≤4 cm, T1b >4–7 cm T2 Confined to kidney, >7 cm — T2a ≤10 cm, T2b >10 cm T3 Major veins or perinephric fat, not beyond Gerota's — a renal vein / sinus or perirenal fat · b IVC below diaphragm · c IVC above diaphragm or caval wall T4 Beyond Gerota's fascia, incl. contiguous ipsilateral adrenal Stage I T1N0 · II T2N0 · III T1–2N1 or T3 any N · IV T4 or M1 Grade (WHO/ISUP) is nucleolar: G1–G3 by nucleolar prominence at 400×/100×; G4 = marked pleomorphism, giant cells, rhabdoid or sarcomatoid . IMDC risk — the 6 factors KPS <80% Hemoglobin < LLN Diagnosis → systemic tx <1 year Calcium > ULN (corrected) Neutrophils > ULN Platelets > ULN Favorable = 0 · Intermediate = 1–2 · Poor = ≥3. Two clinical + four labs. Prognostic, and it is how the 1L trials were stratified — but it does not predict IO vs TKI benefit except that ipi/nivo underperforms in favorable risk. After nephrectomy Surveillance (NCCN, risk-adapted): history, labs and chest/abdominal imaging every 3–6 months for ~3 years after stage II–III, then annually to year 5 and beyond — RCC recurs late , sometimes a decade or more after surgery Unusual metastatic sites are classic: pancreas, thyroid, adrenal, skin, and hypervascular brain lesions that bleed Treatment pathway Localized — stage I–III Resect (or surveil the small mass) T1a: partial nephrectomy , ablation <3 cm, or AS T1b–T3: partial if feasible, else radical renal vein / IVC thrombus: still resectable Adjuvant — clear cell, increased risk pT2 G4/sarcomatoid, ≥pT3, N+, or M1 NED pembrolizumab ×1 yr (KEYNOTE-564, OS HR 0.62) or pembro + belzutifan (LITESPARK-022, FDA 6/2026) non-clear cell: surveillance — no adjuvant data Metastatic clear cell — first line by IMDC Favorable (0 factors) IO/TKI: pembro + axitinib, nivo + cabozantinib, or lenvatinib + pembro not ipi/nivo (ORR 30% vs 52% for sunitinib) indolent, low-volume: active surveillance Intermediate (1–2) / poor (≥3) ipi/nivo (8-yr OS HR 0.69) or any IO/TKI sarcomatoid: IO combination, not TKI alone IO-ineligible: cabozantinib (CABOSUN) no triplet — COSMIC-313 had no OS gain Cytoreductive nephrectomy selected only — usually deferred after response Later lines & non-clear cell After IO (1L or adjuvant) switch to a VEGF TKI : cabozantinib, axitinib, lenvatinib + everolimus; tivozanib after ≥2 lines belzutifan after IO + VEGF TKI do not add IO back (CONTACT-03, TiNivo-2) belz + lenvatinib: FDA decision due 4 Oct 2026 Non-clear cell — trial preferred papillary: cabozantinib (PAPMET) lenva + pembro or cabo + nivo (single-arm) collecting duct / medullary: gem + platinum HLRCC: erlotinib + bevacizumab Histology Subtype Biology · what it means Clear cell ~75% VHL loss (3p) → HIF-2α accumulation → VEGF . Why VEGF TKIs, IO and belzutifan work; chemo-resistant Papillary ~10–15% MET-driven subset (chr 7 gain, MET alterations). Cabozantinib best randomized data Chromophobe ~5% Usually indolent; IO barely works . BHD (FLCN) association Collecting duct <1% Aggressive, often metastatic at diagnosis — treat like urothelial: gemcitabine + platinum Renal medullary <1% Young patients with sickle cell trait ; SMARCB1 (INI1) loss. Platinum-based chemo; dismal prognosis FH-deficient HLRCC-associated (formerly 'type 2 papillary'); metastasizes when small Translocation TFE3/TFEB (MiT family); children and young adults Sarcomatoid any subtype Not a subtype but dedifferentiation — poor prognosis, yet the best responders to IO Localized disease & surgery Small renal mass (≤4 cm): active surveillance is legitimate , especially in the elderly or comorbid — many are benign or indolent. Serial imaging; intervene for growth (~>5 mm/yr) or size >3–4 cm. Ablation (cryo/RFA) for <3 cm Partial nephrectomy preferred for T1a (and T1b when feasible) to protect renal function. The one RCT, EORTC 30904 , did not show OS non-inferiority (10-yr OS 75.7% vs 81.1%) but was underpowered — nephron-sparing remains standard IVC tumor thrombus is not a contraindication to resection. Lymphadenectomy has no proven OS benefit; no role for adjuvant RT Cytoreductive nephrectomy is no longer routine: CARMENA — sunitinib alone non-inferior (OS 18.4 vs 13.9 mo); SURTIME — deferred CN after 3 cycles of sunitinib gave longer OS (exploratory). Keep it for good PS, low-volume disease, symptomatic primary, or a responder with residual primary Metastasectomy / SBRT for oligometastatic disease, especially with a long disease-free interval Pearls No chemotherapy for clear cell — the only chemo-sensitive RCCs are collecting duct and medullary Renal mass + sickle cell trait in a young Black patient = medullary carcinoma until proven otherwise Belzutifan is the VHL drug (hereditary) and a later-line drug in sporadic ccRCC — same target, HIF-2α Cabozantinib appears at every step: 1L (with nivo or alone), 2L after IO (METEOR, CONTACT-03 control arm), and papillary (PAPMET) Adjuvant — why KEYNOTE-564 stood alone Trial Agent · result KEYNOTE-564 Pembrolizumab ×1 yr vs placebo — DFS HR 0.68; OS HR 0.62 (48-mo OS 91.2% vs 86.0%). The first adjuvant therapy in RCC with an OS benefit LITESPARK-022 Pembro + belzutifan vs pembro — DFS HR 0.72, 24-mo DFS 80.7% vs 73.7%. OS immature (HR 0.78, NS); grade ≥3 AEs 52% vs 30% . FDA approved 12 Jun 2026 RAMPART abstract only Durvalumab + tremelimumab vs monitoring — DFS HR 0.65; durvalumab alone NS (HR 0.74). Not approved CheckMate 914 A Nivo + ipi ×24 wk — DFS HR 0.92, negative ; 32% stopped for toxicity, 4 treatment deaths CheckMate 914 B Nivolumab alone — DFS HR 0.87, negative PROSPER One neoadjuvant nivo dose + 9 adjuvant — RFS HR 0.94, stopped for futility (included non-clear cell) IMmotion010 Atezolizumab ×1 yr — DFS HR 0.93, negative S-TRAC Sunitinib ×1 yr — DFS 6.8 vs 5.6 yr (HR 0.76), no OS benefit (HR 0.92). FDA-approved 2017, rarely used ASSURE · PROTECT · ATLAS Sunitinib or sorafenib (DFS HR 1.02 / 0.97) · pazopanib (HR 0.86) · axitinib (HR 0.87, stopped for futility) — all negative Candidate explanations for the IO split — anti-PD-1 vs anti-PD-L1, inclusion of resected M1 NED patients, adding CTLA-4 toxicity, PROSPER's single neoadjuvant dose — none is proven . Adjuvant therapy is for clear cell only. First-line clear cell — all vs sunitinib unless stated Regimen · trial Long-term result Ipi + nivo CheckMate 214 Int/poor: OS HR 0.69 at 8 yr, CR 11.8% vs 2.6%, median DOR 82.8 mo — the most durable tail. Favorable: OS HR 0.82 (NS), ORR 30% vs 52%. PFS co-primary missed its α Pembro + axitinib KEYNOTE-426 Final (43 mo): OS HR 0.73 , PFS HR 0.68, ORR 60% vs 40%. All risk groups Nivo + cabozantinib CheckMate 9ER Final (5.6 yr): OS 46.5 vs 35.5 mo, HR 0.79 ; PFS 16.4 vs 8.3 mo; ORR 55.7% vs 27.4%, CR 13.9%. Best QoL data Lenvatinib + pembro CLEAR PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.47), ORR 71.3% — highest response rate. Final OS HR 0.79, medians equal (53.7 vs 54.3 mo) Cabo + nivo + ipi COSMIC-313 vs ipi/nivo, int/poor — PFS 16.6 vs 11.2 mo (HR 0.82) but OS HR 1.02 , grade 3–4 AEs 79% vs 56%. Triplet rejected Cabozantinib CABOSUN Int/poor, randomized phase 2 — PFS 8.2 vs 5.6 mo. The IO-ineligible option No head-to-head trial between IO combinations and no predictive biomarker (PD-L1 does not select). Pick by risk group, comorbidity, and whether you want response (IO/TKI) or a durable treatment-free tail (ipi/nivo). Choosing among the first-line regimens Symptomatic, bulky, or need a response now → IO/TKI; lenvatinib + pembro has the highest ORR and longest PFS Int/poor risk, want a chance at a durable treatment-free remission → ipi/nivo ; also avoids chronic TKI toxicity. Expect front-loaded irAEs Favorable risk → IO/TKI (ipi/nivo lost on ORR and PFS); indolent low-volume disease can be watched Autoimmune disease, transplant, or IO-ineligible → cabozantinib (int/poor) or sunitinib/pazopanib Relapse after adjuvant pembrolizumab: no randomized data — most use a VEGF TKI-based regimen, especially if relapse occurs on or soon after IO Second line and beyond Trial Setting · result LITESPARK-011 Belzutifan + lenvatinib vs cabozantinib after anti-PD-(L)1 — PFS 14.8 vs 10.7 mo (HR 0.70), ORR ~53% vs ~40%; interim OS HR 0.85, not significant (final pending). FDA action date 4 Oct 2026 LITESPARK-005 Belzutifan vs everolimus after IO + TKI — ORR 21.9% vs 3.5%, 18-mo PFS 24% vs 8%, but median PFS 5.6 mo in both and OS HR 0.88, NS . FDA 14 Dec 2023 METEOR Cabozantinib vs everolimus after VEGF TKI — OS 21.4 vs 16.5 mo (HR 0.66), PFS HR 0.51 CheckMate 025 Nivolumab vs everolimus after VEGF TKI — OS 25.0 vs 19.6 mo (HR 0.73); the IO-naive 2L option Study 205 Lenvatinib + everolimus vs everolimus, randomized phase 2 — PFS 14.6 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.40) TIVO-3 Tivozanib vs sorafenib after ≥2 lines — PFS 5.6 vs 3.9 mo; no OS benefit CONTACT-03 Atezolizumab + cabo vs cabo after IO — PFS HR 1.03, OS HR 0.94: negative TiNivo-2 Tivozanib + nivolumab vs tivozanib after IO — PFS 5.7 vs 7.4 mo, negative IO rechallenge does not work — two negative phase 3s. After IO, the next drug is a VEGF TKI; belzutifan comes after IO + TKI. Non-clear cell — mostly single-arm data Histology / trial Evidence Papillary SWOG S1500 (PAPMET) Cabozantinib vs sunitinib , randomized phase 2 — PFS 9.0 vs 5.6 mo (HR 0.60), ORR 23% vs 4%; OS NS. Savolitinib and crizotinib arms closed for futility Mixed nccRCC KEYNOTE-B61 Lenvatinib + pembro , single-arm — ORR 49% (51% at 2 yr), sarcomatoid 47% Mixed nccRCC phase 2 Cabo + nivo — ORR 47.5% papillary/unclassified; 0 of 7 chromophobe responded Mixed nccRCC KEYNOTE-427 B Pembrolizumab alone — ORR 26.7%, mPFS 4.2 mo Chromophobe IO largely inactive; VEGF TKI ± mTOR (e.g., lenvatinib + everolimus). Trial preferred Collecting duct · medullary Gemcitabine + cisplatin/carboplatin ; TKIs and IO rarely help. Check sickle status in a young patient with a renal mass Sarcomatoid Use an IO combination whatever the parent histology — the highest CR rates in 1L subgroups Hereditary syndromes (all autosomal dominant) Syndrome / gene Renal tumor · other features · management VHL VHL, 3p Clear cell, multifocal/bilateral ; CNS/retinal hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytoma, pNET, pancreatic cysts. Belzutifan (LITESPARK-004: RCC ORR 49%; FDA Aug 2021) spares repeated surgery; resect when the largest tumor reaches ~3 cm HLRCC FH FH-deficient RCC — solitary, aggressive, metastasizes early: excise promptly, no surveillance . Cutaneous + uterine leiomyomas. Advanced: erlotinib + bevacizumab (ORR 72%, mPFS 21.1 mo) Birt-Hogg-Dubé FLCN Chromophobe / hybrid oncocytic , bilateral; fibrofolliculomas, lung cysts → pneumothorax Tuberous sclerosis TSC1/2 Angiomyolipomas (rarely RCC); everolimus . Angiofibromas, SEGA, LAM BAP1 TPDS BAP1 Aggressive clear cell ; uveal and cutaneous melanoma, mesothelioma HPRC MET Papillary , multifocal and bilateral Hereditary PGL/PCC SDHB/C/D SDH-deficient RCC ; paraganglioma, pheochromocytoma, GIST Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing Adjuvant pembrolizumab KEYNOTE-564 200 mg IV q3wk ×17 or 400 mg q6wk (~1 yr) + Belzutifan LITESPARK-022 Belzutifan 120 mg PO daily ×up to 54 wk with pembrolizumab 200 q3wk / 400 q6wk ×12 mo Pembro + axitinib Axitinib 5 mg PO BID (titrate to 7 then 10 mg BID if BP controlled) + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk / 400 q6wk, IO up to 2 yr Ipi + nivo Nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV q3wk ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg q2wk or 480 mg q4wk Nivo + cabozantinib Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily (not 60) + nivolumab 240 q2wk / 480 q4wk, nivo max 2 yr Lenvatinib + pembro Lenvatinib 20 mg PO daily + pembrolizumab 200 q3wk / 400 q6wk, IO up to 2 yr Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily on an empty stomach; hold ≥3 wk before surgery Belzutifan 120 mg PO daily — after IO + VEGF TKI, and for VHL tumors Belzutifan + lenvatinib 120 mg + 20 mg daily (LITESPARK-011; pending FDA) Tivozanib 1.34 mg PO daily, 21 days on / 7 off — after ≥2 prior systemic lines Lenvatinib + everolimus Lenvatinib 18 mg + everolimus 5 mg PO daily Axitinib alone 5 mg BID → 7 → 10 mg BID if BP ≤150/90 and tolerated Sunitinib 50 mg PO daily, 4 wk on / 2 wk off (or 2 on / 1 off for tolerance) Pazopanib 800 mg PO daily , empty stomach Nivolumab alone 240 mg q2wk or 480 mg q4wk Erlotinib + bevacizumab Erlotinib 150 mg PO daily + bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV q2wk — HLRCC / papillary Pembrolizumab in RCC is 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk — not 300/600. Historical: high-dose IL-2 (ORR ~14%, rare durable CRs), temsirolimus (poor-risk, ARCC). Toxicity & monitoring Hypertension is the signature VEGF-TKI toxicity — control BP before starting, home BP log, add agents early rather than stopping the TKI. Urine protein with lenvatinib and bevacizumab Transaminitis on axitinib + pembrolizumab (or cabo/lenva + IO): hold both drugs . TKI hepatitis resolves within days (short half-lives); if ALT is not falling after ~1 week, or grade ≥3, treat as immune hepatitis with prednisone 1–2 mg/kg. Restart the TKI first at reduced dose; rechallenge IO only if it wasn't the culprit Pazopanib carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity — LFTs before starting and every ~2 weeks through month 4; also QT prolongation Hypothyroidism from both TKIs (sunitinib, axitinib, lenvatinib) and IO — TSH every 4–6 wk on treatment Belzutifan: on-target anemia (HIF-2α drives EPO — decreased Hgb is the most common adverse reaction) and hypoxia : check Hgb and pulse oximetry at baseline and periodically; transfuse, hold or dose-reduce. Boxed warning: embryo-fetal toxicity , and it can make hormonal contraception ineffective Ipi/nivo: front-loaded irAEs — colitis, hepatitis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency. Check cortisol with fatigue or hyponatremia Cabozantinib: diarrhea, hand-foot, stomatitis, wound-healing and bleeding — dose reductions to 40/20 mg are routine Sunitinib: hand-foot, mucositis, cytopenias, cardiomyopathy. mTOR inhibitors: pneumonitis, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia Bone metastases (lytic, ~1/3): zoledronic acid (renally dosed) or denosumab; brain metastases — SRS before or alongside systemic therapy Special situations Brain metastases: treat locally first (SRS or resection); patients with treated, stable brain mets can receive standard systemic therapy Dialysis / poor renal function: IO needs no renal adjustment; dose-adjust zoledronic acid, and denosumab carries a severe-hypocalcemia risk in advanced CKD Pre-existing autoimmune disease or solid-organ transplant: avoid IO; TKI monotherapy Surgery on a TKI: hold cabozantinib ≥3 wk before and resume only after wound healing; bevacizumab ≥28 days Key trials KEYNOTE-564 Adjuvant pembrolizumab — DFS HR 0.68, OS HR 0.62 LITESPARK-022 Adding belzutifan to adjuvant pembro — DFS HR 0.72, OS immature CheckMate 914 · PROSPER · IMmotion010 Adjuvant nivo ± ipi, perioperative nivo, atezolizumab — all negative CheckMate 214 Ipi/nivo, int/poor — 8-yr OS HR 0.69, durable CRs CLEAR Lenva + pembro — PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo, ORR 71% COSMIC-313 Triplet cabo + ipi/nivo — PFS gain, no OS gain CARMENA · SURTIME Immediate cytoreductive nephrectomy not needed; defer and select METEOR Cabozantinib after TKI — OS HR 0.66 LITESPARK-005 / -011 Belzutifan after IO + TKI (ORR 22%); + lenvatinib post-IO, PFS HR 0.70 CONTACT-03 · TiNivo-2 IO rechallenge after IO — no benefit PAPMET Papillary: cabozantinib beats sunitinib on PFS LITESPARK-004 Belzutifan in VHL disease — RCC ORR 49% S-TRAC · ASSURE Adjuvant sunitinib: DFS+ but no OS (S-TRAC); negative (ASSURE) KEYNOTE-426 · 9ER IO/TKI vs sunitinib — final OS HR 0.73 / 0.79 CheckMate 025 Nivolumab after TKI — OS 25.0 vs 19.6 mo NCI bev + erlotinib HLRCC papillary RCC — ORR 72%, mPFS 21.1 mo EORTC 30904 Partial vs radical nephrectomy — the only RCT; underpowered

docs.title: Rectal adenocarcinoma
docs.subtitle: Neoadjuvant chemoradiation is the hallmark deviation from the colon strategy — metastatic regimens are otherwise the same. Staging, prognosis and most systemic therapy defer to the colon page
docs.text: Rectal adenocarcinoma Neoadjuvant chemoradiation is the hallmark deviation from the colon strategy — metastatic regimens are otherwise the same. Staging, prognosis and most systemic therapy defer to the colon page Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Rectal Cancer (Tam AY, Shaheen S) · NCCN · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup Colonoscopy + biopsy with MMR / MSI testing and pathology review MRI pelvis (3T) — the rectal-specific study; rectal ultrasound if MRI contraindicated, inconclusive, or for superficial lesions CT chest/abdomen/pelvis · FDG-PET if potentially curable M1 Labs: CBC, CMP, CEA PIK3CA testing in stage II–III — if mutated, aspirin 100–162 mg daily × 3 years post-op If metastatic: KRAS, BRAF, HER2, POLE/POLD1, RET, NTRK Genetics referral for all rectal cancer <50 y , or a somatic finding with germline implications Risk definitions High-risk rectal cT4a or cT4b · extramural vascular invasion · cN2 · involved mesorectal fascia · enlarged lateral nodes considered metastatic High-risk path after local excision positive margins · lymphovascular invasion · poorly differentiated · submucosal invasion to the lower third T4 (rectal nuance) direct extension through serosa into prostate, seminal vesicles, cervix or vagina TNM is otherwise identical to colon — see the colon one-pager for stage groups and for all metastatic systemic therapy. Key trials PROSPECT RT-sparing: FOLFOX/CAPEOX × 12–16 wk with radiation reserved for inadequate regression RAPIDO short-course RT + chemo TNT: pCR 28% vs 14% ; lower distant relapse but possible higher local recurrence (Dijkstra, Ann Surg 2023) PRODIGE 23 induction mFOLFIRINOX: pCR 27.8% vs 12.1% (Conroy) OPRA watch-and-wait after clinical CR to TNT preserves the organ without compromising survival Cercek (NEJM 2025) dostarlimab in dMMR rectal cancer — basis for immunotherapy over TNT SHORTFOX ongoing — RT omission and course length Watch-and-wait requires a complete clinical response on all three of DRE, rectal MRI, and direct endoscopic evaluation — and only in centers with experienced multidisciplinary teams, after careful discussion with the patient. RAPIDO caveat: short-course RT lowered distant relapse but may raise local recurrence, so high-risk patients get TNT as induction chemo followed by chemoradiation. Short-course candidacy is a multidisciplinary decision weighing downstaging against long-term toxicity. Treatment pathway Early — cT1–2 N0 cT1 N0 endoscopic submucosal dissection, or transanal local excision pT1 without high-risk features → surveillance pT1 high-risk or pT2 transabdominal resection preferred then 6 months adjuvant chemoRT + chemo or TNT, then restage → surgery Locally advanced — pMMR / MSS TNT is the standard FOLFOX or CAPEOX + chemoRT concurrent capecitabine during radiation ~6 months of total neoadjuvant therapy High-risk disease sequencing induction chemo THEN chemoRT driven by the RAPIDO local-recurrence signal induction mFOLFIRINOX an option (PRODIGE 23) RT-sparing (PROSPECT-eligible) non-T4, ≤4 nodes, sphincter-sparing candidate FOLFOX/CAPEOX 12–16 wk → restage add RT only if regression inadequate After neoadjuvant therapy restage → transabdominal resection if clinical CR: watch and wait (see note) dMMR / MSI-H or POLE-POLD1 Immunotherapy, preferred OVER TNT dostarlimab, nivolumab, or pembrolizumab up to 6 months; reassess every 2–3 months (Cercek, NEJM 2025) Then clinical CR → surveillance, no surgery persistent at 6 mo → chemoRT → surgery Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Schedule ChemoRT (infusional 5-FU) 5-FU 225 mg/m² IV over 24 h, 5 days per week with RT × 5 wk ChemoRT (capecitabine) capecitabine 825 mg/m² PO BID on days of radiation concurrent with RT Long-course radiation 5–6 weeks — Short-course radiation 5 days — Dostarlimab 500 mg IV × 4 doses, then 1000 mg IV q3wk → q6wk Nivolumab 240 mg (or 3 mg/kg if <40 kg) · or 480 mg q2wk · q4wk Nivolumab + ipilimumab nivo 3 mg/kg + ipi 1 mg/kg × 4, then nivo maintenance q3wk → q2–4wk Aspirin (PIK3CA-mutant) 100–162 mg PO daily × 3 years post-op stage II–III FOLFOX · CAPEOX · mFOLFIRINOX named only here — dosing on the colon page — Biomarker → therapy Alteration Therapy dMMR / MSI-H or POLE-POLD1 (TMB >50) Neoadjuvant/definitive immunotherapy up to 6 months — preferred over TNT ; dostarlimab, nivolumab or pembrolizumab Same, metastatic ICI preferred if no prior exposure: nivolumab ± ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, dostarlimab, cemiplimab, retifanlimab, toripalimab, tislelizumab pMMR/MSS, TMB ≥10 Pembrolizumab in the refractory setting (KEYNOTE-158) PIK3CA, stage II–III Aspirin 100–162 mg daily × 3 years after surgery ctDNA Prognostic only — not for treatment decisions outside a trial Surveillance Same as colon cancer for stage I–IV, except after transanal local excision Transanal local excision: proctoscopy (with EUS or MRI) q3–6 months × 2 years , then q6 months to 5 years total Colonoscopy at 1 year ; if advanced adenoma repeat in 1 year, otherwise 3 years then every 5 years dMMR on immunotherapy: re-evaluate q2–3 months ; MSS metastatic being converted to resectable: q2 months Pearls FOLFOXIRI is not recommended when resection is contraindicated after neoadjuvant therapy Resection is preferred over ablation or SBRT for oligometastatic liver- or lung-only disease Favorable pT3 N0 (well/moderately differentiated, <2 mm mesorectal invasion, no lymphovascular involvement, upper rectum) may go to surveillance rather than adjuvant therapy pT1–3 N1 can be treated with FOLFOX or CAPEOX alone, without radiation

docs.title: Testicular cancer
docs.subtitle: Most common solid malignancy in males 15–35 · >90% cure, >95% 5-yr survival — chemotherapy is curative even in advanced disease · lung is the commonest met site (62%); liver (16%) and brain (7%) are negative prognostic factors
docs.text: Testicular germ cell tumor Most common solid malignancy in males 15–35 · >90% cure, >95% 5-yr survival — chemotherapy is curative even in advanced disease · lung is the commonest met site (62%); liver (16%) and brain (7%) are negative prognostic factors Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Testicular Cancer (Moore K, Glover M, Shah S) · NCCN v1.2025 · trial data verified against the primary publications Workup Suspicious mass: H&P, AFP, bHCG, LDH, chemistry, testicular ultrasound Repeat all markers after orchiectomy — TNM staging uses post-orchiectomy values Pure seminoma (seminoma histology + normal AFP; bHCG may be elevated): abdominal/pelvic CT + chest X-ray; chest CT only if abdominal CT positive or CXR abnormal Non-seminoma (incl. mixed, and seminoma histology with elevated AFP): chest/abdominal/pelvic CT up front Both: brain MRI if clinically indicated · sperm banking Nodal spread is predictable — right-sided to inter-aortocaval, left-sided to para-aortic Histology → marker pattern Subtype Markers Seminoma AFP always normal ; hCG ↑ in ~15–20% Embryonal carcinoma AFP and/or hCG; commonest mixed component Yolk sac tumor AFP — the classic AFP producer Choriocarcinoma hCG, often >50,000; hemorrhage, brain mets Teratoma neither — marker-negative, chemoresistant Mixed germ cell tumor reflects whichever components are present Seminoma hCG comes from syncytiotrophoblasts and is compatible with pure seminoma — only AFP reclassifies . Very high hCG in choriocarcinoma can cause hyperthyroidism (TSH receptor cross-reactivity) and gynecomastia. LDH is non-specific and tracks tumor bulk. Teratoma is marker-negative and chemoresistant — the reason post-chemotherapy masses must be resected. Serum tumor markers (S) S LDH hCG AFP S1 <1.5× N <5,000 <1,000 S2 1.5–10× N 5,000–50,000 1,000–10,000 S3 >10× N >50,000 >10,000 hCG mIU/mL, AFP ng/mL. pT1a/pT1b (<3 vs ≥3 cm) applies to pure seminoma only. cN1 ≤2 cm · cN2 >2–5 cm · cN3 >5 cm. M1a nodal/pulmonary · M1b non-pulmonary visceral. IGCCCG risk — the asymmetry Non-seminoma Good: testis/retroperitoneal primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP<1,000 + hCG<5,000 + LDH<1.5×. Intermediate: markers in the middle band. Poor: mediastinal primary, non-pulmonary visceral mets, or AFP>10,000 / hCG>50,000 / LDH>10× Seminoma Good: any primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, normal AFP. Intermediate: non-pulmonary visceral mets. There is no poor-risk category — only AFP matters, not hCG or LDH Treatment pathway Stage I Seminoma ~85% cured by orchiectomy alone surveillance strongly preferred alt: carboplatin ×1–2 or RT (risk factor >4 cm) Non-seminoma orchiectomy cures ~70%; relapses highly curable surveillance if no risk factors RFs (LVI, cord/scrotal, embryonal): BEP ×1 Stage IIA–IIB Both histologies BEP ×3 or EP ×4 seminoma: RT or RPLND if IIA / non-bulky IIB non-seminoma: or nerve-sparing RPLND Stage IIC–III By IGCCCG risk good risk: BEP ×3 or EP ×4 intermediate or poor: BEP ×4 or VIP ×4 seminoma IIC treated as BEP ×3 / EP ×4 Residual mass and relapse Rules differ by histology seminoma >3 cm: PET — avid resect, non-avid observe non-seminoma: resect ALL masses >1 cm ~10% viable cancer, 40% teratoma, 50% necrosis relapse: resect, else TIP/VeIP ×4 or HDCT Pearls The AFP rule overrides histology. Pure seminoma requires seminoma histology and a normal AFP; seminoma histology with an elevated AFP is worked up and treated as a non-seminoma. Elevated bHCG is compatible with pure seminoma Dose holds and reductions are discouraged in the curative (1st and 2nd line) setting — delay only for severe active infection or illness. The one stated exception: hold or reduce cisplatin for creatinine >1.5 (EP) Residual mass rules differ by histology — PET works for seminoma but not non-seminoma, because teratoma is not FDG-avid yet is chemoresistant and must be resected Non-pulmonary visceral metastases define intermediate-risk seminoma and poor-risk non-seminoma RT or RPLND remains an option only for stage IIA and non-bulky IIB seminoma (nodes <3 cm) Sperm banking before treatment; restage markers after orchiectomy Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Cycle BEP (Einhorn) cisplatin 20/day d1–5 · etoposide 100/day d1–5 · bleomycin 30 units d1, 8, 15 · filgrastim d6–12 q21d EP etoposide 100/day d1–5 · cisplatin 20/day d1–5 · pegfilgrastim d5→6 q21d VIP etoposide 75 · ifosfamide 1200 · cisplatin 20, all d1–5 · mesna · pegfilgrastim d6 q21d TIP (2L) paclitaxel 250 d1 · ifosfamide 1500 d2–5 · cisplatin 25 d2–5 · mesna q21d VeIP (2L) vinblastine 0.11 mg/kg d1–2 · ifosfamide 1200 d1–5 · cisplatin 20 d1–5 · mesna q21d HDCT carboplatin 700 + etoposide 750 — days −5, −4, −3 before stem-cell infusion, ×2 cycles with PBSC rescue 3L options gemcitabine + paclitaxel ± oxaliplatin · oxaliplatin + irinotecan · oral etoposide 50–100 mg d1–21 Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk (or 400 mg q6wk) — MSI-H, dMMR, or TMB >10 q3wk All doses mg/m² unless stated. Growth factor support is built into every first- and second-line regimen; mesna with every ifosfamide-containing regimen. Landmark trials Trial Result IGCCCG 1997 · upd. 2021 2021 (n=9,728): 5-yr OS good 96% / int 89% / poor 67% (was 91/79/48); adds LDH >2.5× ULN Einhorn 1989 (SECSG) 3 vs 4 BEP , favorable risk — NED 98% vs 97%. n=184 EORTC 30941 / TE20 3 vs 4 BEP and 5- vs 3-day — 2-yr PFS 90.4% vs 89.4%, equivalent Kondagunta 4×EP Single-arm n=289, good risk — CR 98% . Bleomycin-free option MRC TE19 / EORTC 30982 Stage I seminoma: carboplatin AUC7 ×1 non-inferior to RT (5-yr RFS 94.7% vs 96.0%) MRC TE18 / EORTC 30942 Seminoma RT 20 Gy = 30 Gy , less lethargy SWENOTECA CS I non-sem 1×BEP : 5-yr relapse 3.2% LVI+ / 1.6% LVI− vs 41.7% / 13.2% surveillance Kondagunta TIP First salvage n=46 — durable CR 63% TI-CE (Feldman) High-dose + PBSC, n=107 — CR 50%, 5-yr DFS 47% TIGER (A031102) Ongoing phase 3, TIP vs TI-CE at first salvage, primary OS Phase 3 only for the BEP-cycle and seminoma-RT questions. SWENOTECA is population-based; Kondagunta TIP (ph 2), 4×EP and TI-CE (ph 1/2) are single-arm. Biomarkers: testicular cancer is marker-driven, not biomarker-driven — AFP, bHCG and LDH determine stage, risk group and response. The only biomarker-selected therapy in the chapter is pembrolizumab for MSI-H, dMMR, or TMB >10.

docs.subtitle: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with an IgM paraprotein · MYD88 L265P in ~90%+ · treat symptoms and IgM complications, not the IgM number · genotype (MYD88/CXCR4) steers BTKi vs chemoimmunotherapy
headings: Fixed-duration vs continuous — how to choose
docs.text: Waldenström macroglobulinemia Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with an IgM paraprotein · MYD88 L265P in ~90%+ · treat symptoms and IgM complications, not the IgM number · genotype (MYD88/CXCR4) steers BTKi vs chemoimmunotherapy Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (NCCN; IWWM-2, IWWM-11 and IWWM-12 consensus panels) verified against PubMed, September 2026. Definitions and the IgM differential Entity Defining features WM Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL) in the marrow + an IgM monoclonal protein of any size. IWWM-2 and IWWM-11: no IgM or marrow-% cutoff separates WM from IgM MGUS — the diagnosis rests on marrow histology + immunophenotype IgM MGUS IgM M-protein, no LPL on marrow, no symptoms. Progresses to lymphoma/WM at ~1.5%/yr . IWWM-11 splits it: plasma-cell type (MYD88 wild-type — myeloma/AL lineage) vs B-cell type (may be MYD88-mutant) Asymptomatic (smoldering) WM Meets WM criteria, no treatment indication → observe . 72% progress (median follow-up 7.8 yr). Progression risk: IgM ≥4,500 mg/dL, marrow ≥70%, β2M ≥4 mg/L, albumin ≤3.5 ; MYD88 wild-type HR 2.7 IgM myeloma CD138+ plasma cells without a B-cell/LPL component, t(11;14), MYD88 wild-type, lytic lesions. Treat as myeloma — not WM Marginal zone Can make IgM and show plasmacytic differentiation. MYD88 L265P absent or rare — the most useful discriminator IgM-related disorder Symptoms from the IgM itself (neuropathy, cryo, CAD, amyloid) without overt lymphoma — still may need clone-directed therapy Workup SPEP + immunofixation, quantitative IgM (SPEP M-spike and nephelometric IgM are not interchangeable — follow one method), free light chains, β2-microglobulin, albumin, LDH, CBC, CMP Marrow biopsy : intertrabecular LPL infiltrate; surface IgM+, CD19+, CD20+, CD22+, with CD138+ plasma cells; usually CD5− CD10− CD23− (variants do not exclude WM) Molecular on marrow before any therapy (IWWM-11): AS-PCR for MYD88 L265P and CXCR4 S338X on whole marrow ; CXCR4 + TP53 sequencing and 6q/17p FISH on CD19-selected cells CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for nodes/spleen. Serum viscosity + fundoscopy if IgM is high or any HVS symptom Targeted: cryoglobulins (draw and transport at 37°C), DAT + cold agglutinin titer , anti-MAG + EMG if neuropathy, NT-proBNP/troponin, urine protein, fat pad if amyloid suspected, MRI brain/spine + CSF if CNS symptoms Prognosis: IPSSWM — age >65, Hb ≤11.5, plt ≤100, β2M >3 mg/L, M-protein >7 g/dL; 5-yr OS 87% / 68% / 36% (low/int/high). Not a treatment trigger Treatment pathway Diagnosis Asymptomatic → watch and wait IWWM: IgM level alone is NOT an indication clinic + labs q3–6 mo; IgM MGUS yearly SPEP Treat when a criterion is met Hb ≤10 or plt <100 from marrow infiltration B symptoms, bulky/symptomatic nodes or spleen HVS, neuropathy, amyloid, cryo, CAD, renal Emergencies first Symptomatic hyperviscosity plasmapheresis FIRST , then start therapy no RBC transfusion before pheresis High IgM + rituximab planned hold rituximab until IgM falls, or pheresis first — the IgM flare can precipitate HVS First line — genotype + patient Fixed-duration chemoimmunotherapy BR ×6 or DRC ×6 — IWWM default, affordable MYD88-WT , CXCR4-mutant, fit, want time off Bortezomib-based (BDR / B-DRC) rapid IgM control: HVS, cryo, amyloid, renal avoid with pre-existing neuropathy Continuous covalent BTKi zanubrutinib preferred (ASPEN); ibrutinib ± R MYD88-mutant, CXCR4-WT, frail, CNS disease not for AL amyloid (IWWM-11) Relapse Switch class; reuse only after a long remission after chemo → cBTKi; after cBTKi → BR/DRC/BDR pirtobrutinib or venetoclax (off-label) bridge — don't stop a BTKi until next Rx IgM-mediated complications — each managed differently Syndrome Recognize → manage Hyperviscosity large pentameric IgM Blurred vision, headache, epistaxis/oronasal bleeding, dizziness, confusion, heart failure. Fundoscopy: dilated “sausage” veins, hemorrhages, papilledema. Viscosity poorly predicts symptoms per patient. Plasmapheresis first (IgM is ~80% intravascular, so it clears efficiently), then cytoreduce — pheresis alone is a bridge. Avoid RBC transfusion until pheresed Anti-MAG neuropathy Slowly progressive, distal, symmetric sensory-predominant demyelinating neuropathy with ataxia/tremor. EMG + anti-MAG titer; joint heme-neuro care. Rituximab-based therapy ; stabilization is the realistic goal. Avoid bortezomib (and vincristine) Cryoglobulinemia type I or II Raynaud's, acral necrosis, purpura, vasculitic neuropathy, GN. Draw at 37°C or it is missed. Keep warm; plasmapheresis for severe ; rapid cytoreduction (BR, BDR) Cold agglutinin disease Chronic hemolysis with cold acrocyanosis; DAT C3d+, IgMκ titer. Keep warm, warm IV fluids/blood . Rituximab-based (BR most active); sutimlimab blocks C1s for hemolysis AL amyloidosis Lambda light chain, cardiac/renal/nerve. Treat as AL : bortezomib- or bendamustine-based; daratumumab. cBTKi not recommended (IWWM-11) Bing-Neel CNS WM Headache, cognitive change, cranial nerve palsies, gait. MRI brain + spine with gadolinium, CSF cytology/flow + MYD88 PCR. BTKi cross the BBB : ibrutinib (n=28: 85% symptom improvement, 2-yr EFS 80%); IWWM-12 made zanubrutinib a standard . Alternatives: HD-MTX / HD-araC, fludarabine Genotype drives BTKi choice Lesion Why it matters MYD88 L265P ~90%+ Drives NF-κB via IRAK/BTK. Supports the diagnosis (rare in MZL, absent in myeloma). MYD88 wild-type: weaker BTKi response (ibrutinib major response 29%), worse OS — favor chemoimmunotherapy CXCR4 WHIM-like ~30–40% Nonsense/frameshift C-tail mutations; higher IgM + marrow burden, more hyperviscosity. Slower, shallower BTKi responses : TN ibrutinib major response 71% vs 94%, VGPR 7% vs 31%, time to major response 7.3 vs 1.8 mo TP53 , del6q, del17p Adverse; IWWM-11 counts TP53 and 6q/17p among essential pre-treatment tests First-line options — the evidence Regimen Evidence and the catch Bendamustine-rituximab IWWM/NCCN preferred chemoimmunotherapy. Randomized evidence is StiL NHL1 (BR beat R-CHOP in indolent NHL, WM a small subgroup). Rituximab maintenance after BR: no benefit overall (StiL NHL7-MAINTAIN) DRC Phase 2, n=72: ORR 83% (CR 7%), 2-yr PFS 67%; grade 3–4 neutropenia only 9%. Slow: median time to response 4.1 mo . ECWM-1: adding bortezomib (B-DRC) did not improve PFS (24-mo 80.6% vs 72.8%, P=0.32) but responses came faster (3.0 vs 5.5 mo) BDR Weekly-bortezomib EMN regimen: ORR 85% , median PFS 42 mo ; neuropathy 46% (grade ≥3 7%). Bortezomib lead-in blunts rituximab flare. Zoster prophylaxis mandatory Ibrutinib ± rituximab iNNOVATE (phase 3, n=150): IR vs placebo-R — final median PFS NR vs 20.3 mo , HR 0.25; benefit regardless of MYD88/CXCR4 . Adding ibrutinib cut rituximab IgM flare (8% vs 47%). Grade ≥3 AF 12% vs 1% , HTN 13% vs 4% Zanubrutinib ASPEN (phase 3, n=201 MYD88-mutant): primary endpoint VGPR+CR 28% vs 19%, P=0.09 — not met . Final (44 mo): VGPR+CR 36% vs 25%; CXCR4-mutant 21% vs 10%. Less AF (7.9% vs 23.5%), HTN, bleeding, diarrhea ; more neutropenia. FDA-approved Aug 2021 Acalabrutinib Single-arm phase 2, n=106: ORR 93% TN and R/R; grade 3–4 AF 1%. Not FDA-approved for WM Ibrutinib + venetoclax Fixed-duration TN trial: VGPR 42% but ventricular arrhythmia 9% incl. 2 deaths → stopped early . Not a standard Fixed-duration vs continuous — how to choose Chemoimmunotherapy: finite (~6 mo), then time off therapy; myelosuppression, infections; the better fit for MYD88 wild-type and a reasonable one for CXCR4-mutant disease cBTKi: oral, rapid Hb recovery, indefinite — cost, cumulative AF/HTN/bleeding, and IgM rebound if stopped . Best in MYD88-mutant/CXCR4-WT; zanubrutinib over ibrutinib for tolerability IgM lags the marrow: IgM can plateau or rise transiently (rituximab flare; bortezomib/rituximab-era discordance ) — do not call progression on IgM alone; confirm, check marrow/Hb/nodes. BR/DRC responses deepen for months after the last cycle Relapsed / refractory Durable first remission → the same regimen can be reused ; early relapse or refractory → switch class Ibrutinib withdrawal: IgM rebound (≥25%) in 73% of discontinuations, half within 4 weeks, some with HVS; salvage works better if started within 2 weeks. Continue the BTKi until the next therapy starts ; hold only ~3–7 days peri-procedure Pirtobrutinib (non-covalent; binds C481-mutant BTK): BRUIN WM n=80 (79% cBTKi-exposed) — ORR 82.5% (81% post-cBTKi), major response ~72%. Not FDA-approved for WM (MCL/CLL only) — single-arm, off-label Venetoclax 200→800 mg daily ×2 yr: ORR 84%, major 81%, median PFS 30 mo ; slower after BTKi (4.5 vs 1.4 mo); CXCR4 did not matter . Neutropenia 45%. Off-label Also: bortezomib/carfilzomib-based, BR after BTKi, clinical trials (BTK degraders, CXCR4 antagonists, bispecifics). Autologous SCT for select chemosensitive young patients. Transformation to DLBCL → treat as DLBCL Response (IWWM-6 / simplified IWWM-11) CR Normal IgM, negative immunofixation , no marrow disease, resolved nodes/spleen VGPR ≥90% IgM reduction PR 50–89% IgM reduction · major response = PR or better MR 25–49% IgM reduction (counts in “overall” response) PD ≥25% IgM rise from nadir (confirmed) or new disease/complication IWWM-11 lets PR/VGPR be called on serum IgM alone, with guidance for flare/rebound. ORR in WM trials includes minor responses — compare major response rates across studies. Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing BR Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1–2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² d1, q28d ×6 DRC Dexamethasone 20 mg IV + rituximab 375 mg/m² d1 + cyclophosphamide 100 mg/m² PO BID d1–5 , q21d ×6 BDR EMN Cycle 1 bortezomib alone 1.3 mg/m² d1,4,8,11; then 1.6 mg/m² weekly d1,8,15,22 q35d ×4 ; dex 40 mg + rituximab 375 in cycles 2 and 5. SC bortezomib in practice Zanubrutinib 160 mg BID or 320 mg daily , continuous Ibrutinib ± R 420 mg daily , continuous; iNNOVATE rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly, weeks 1–4 and 17–20 Acalabrutinib 100 mg BID, continuous Pirtobrutinib 200 mg daily, continuous Venetoclax Ramp 200 → 800 mg daily , up to 2 yr; TLS precautions Monitoring and prophylaxis HBsAg + anti-HBc before any anti-CD20 — entecavir if core-Ab positive. Acyclovir/valacyclovir with bortezomib (zoster in 4 of the first 7 BDR patients) and commonly with BR and BTKi BTKi: baseline ECG and BP; ask about palpitations; treat HTN . AF → rate control, weigh anticoagulation with bleeding; switch ibrutinib → zanubrutinib. No warfarin; avoid fish oil/vit E ; hold ~3–7 days around surgery. Strong CYP3A inhibitors → dose-adjust Bortezomib: neuropathy check every cycle; weekly + SC dosing lowers it; dose-reduce at grade 2 with pain Rituximab: IgM before each dose; hold or pre-pherese if IgM is high (commonly ≥4,000 mg/dL); a rising IgM in the first months is often flare, not progression IgM + CBC q1–3 mo on therapy; SPEP/IgM q3–6 mo in remission. Same lab, same method Key trials iNNOVATE Ibrutinib-R vs placebo-R — median PFS NR vs 20.3 mo, HR 0.25, genotype-independent ASPEN Zanubrutinib vs ibrutinib — VGPR+CR primary not met (28 vs 19%); far less AF ECWM-1 B-DRC vs DRC — no PFS gain; faster response DRC (Dimopoulos) Phase 2 — ORR 83%, 2-yr PFS 67% BDR (EMN) Phase 2 — ORR 85%, median PFS 42 mo, weekly bortezomib Ibrutinib TN / R/R Phase 2 — CXCR4 and MYD88 genotype set depth and speed BRUIN WM Pirtobrutinib R/R — ORR 82.5%, active post-cBTKi Venetoclax (Castillo) R/R — major response 81%, median PFS 30 mo
